The proposed development consists of a high density residential apartment scheme that is considered excessive in terms of bulk, height and scale at a visually sensitive location fronting onto the River Barrow and the Barrow Track in Carlow Town. Accordingly, the proposed development would contravene materially Heritage Objective - 5 and Heritage Policy - 2 of the Carlow County Development Plan 2015-2021 and would therefore be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The application site is located within an identified flood risk area in the OPW CFRAM study for Carlow Town, with the proposed development introducing new residential development into an area that is not included in the defended area of the completed works forming part of the Carlow Flood Relief Scheme. The proposal therefore seeks to introduce a “highly vulnerable' land use into an identified flood risk area, contrary to the requirement for Opportunity Site 17 as contained in the Strategic Flood Risk Assessment of the Joint Spatial Plan for the Greater Carlow Graiguecullen Urban Area 2012-2018 (as extended), with a lack of a sequential test to consider alternatives sites for residential development that are not at risk of flooding. The Planning Authority is also not fully satisfied that the proposed extension of the existing flood defence walls bounding the site and the provision of compensatory storage onsite will suitably mitigate against adverse flood risk impacts. Accordingly, it is considered that the proposed development would be contrary to Ministerial Guidance on flood risk management, would likely exacerbate the risk of flooding within the site and/or increase the risk and consequences for flooding elsewhere, would be prejudicial to public health and be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. No. 18/50559 - Chief Executive’s Order No. 2018PH0990 SCHEDULE The subject site is located on lands zoned as ‘Strategic Residential Reserve’ in the Letterkenny and Environs Development Plan 2009-2015 (as varied). It is a policy of the said Plan that the release of lands zoned strategic residential reserve will only be carried out in the context of a variation to or review of the development plan – Policy H4 of the said Plan refers. It is also a policy of the said Plan: “to consider proposals that seek to resolve existing unfinished residential development, including through the appropriate reconfiguration of developments” – Policy CS4 of the said Plan refers. It is considered that the proposed development which provides for the construction of the entire previously permitted residential development and not the resolution of an unfinished estate through the reconfiguration of the area where development has commenced to date, if permitted, would materially contravene the above-mentioned policy context within the said strategic residential reserve lands, which by itself and by precedent for further similar developments on strategic residential reserve lands would be prejudicial to the orderly and sustainable development of Letterkenny. Accordingly to permit the proposed development would be contrary to the provisions of the said Policy H4 and Policy CS4 of the Letterkenny and Environs Development Plan 2009-2015 (as varied) and would thereby be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area.

The development, comprising the demolition of an existing structure and construction of two new standalone apartment blocks containing 24 residential units, does not constitute minor development. The proposal therefore materially contravenes the Established Development 2 zoning objective and is contrary to Policy GEN -F-P-1, which restricts development in such areas to minor works that do not introduce significant additional population into areas of flood risk. Accordingly, the proposal is contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The proposed development is located wholly within Flood Zone B and partially within Flood Zone A under the High- End Future Scenario. The Planning Authority is not satisfied that the development would not be subject to, or exacerbate, flood risk. The proposal is therefore contrary to the Flood Risk Management Guidelines and the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. Accordingly, to permit the proposed development would thus be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The proposal is contrary to the County Donegal Development Plan 2024-2030 Policy UB- P-7 and Policy UB-P-9 in that the development, if permitted, would result in unacceptable damage to the local character and create an undesirable living environment for prospective residents due to unsatisfactory form, design, scale, layout, and inadequate provision of amenity space. Policy 16.10.17 of the Dublin City Council Development Plan 2016-2022 provides that 'the planning authority will actively seek the retention and re-use of buildings/structures of historic, architectural, cultural, artistic and/or local interest or buildings which make a positive contribution to the character and identity of streetscapes and the sustainable development of the city'. Buildings numbers 73 and 74 Francis Street which are proposed to be demolished have been identified by the National Inventory of Architectural Heritage (NIAH) as being of Architectural interest and have been afforded a 'regional rating'. The proposed development fails to integrate with the existing built environment. Having regard to the scale, height, massing, and bulk of the overall development and considering the proximity to two-storey dwellings it is considered that the proposed development would be overbearing, visually obtrusive and would unduly detract from the visual amenities and character of the area. It is considered that the proposed development constitutes over-development of the site and would fail to be absorbed into its physical context. The proposed development by reason of the heights proposed would detract from the landmark status of the existing church on Bird Avenue. The proposed development is therefore contrary to Policy REG1 of the County Development Plan 2004 which states "in evaluating the scale and height of proposed developments, it is Council policy to balance the strategic planning need to make the most efficient use of each site with the visual impact of the proposal and its effect on existing amenities, particularly residential amenities". The proposed development would seriously injure the amenities, or depreciate the value, of property in the vicinity and would therefore be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. 2. Having regard to the substandard provision of public and private open space in terms of quantity and quality, the inadequate rear gardens serving the proposed dwelling houses, the limited separation distances and the lack of play facilities it is considered that the proposed development would fail to create a quality living environment for future residents. It is considered that the proposed public open space provision for a development of this quantum and scale would be seriously substandard. The proposed development is contrary to Section 5.5.7 of the County Development Plan. The proposed development would therefore be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. 3. It is considered that the proposed access route between the site and Churchfields Estate would adversely impact on the public open space serving the Churchfileds estate. The proposed development would contravene an existing permission Register References 92A / 1629 and 93A / 1389, would seriously injure the amenities and would therefore be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. 4. Having regard to the significant volume of traffic that would be generated by the proposed development it is considered that by reason of the absence of a right turning lane at the junction between Chuchfields estate and the Dundrum Road the existing junction would be inadequate to cater for the additional traffic. The proposed development would endanger public safety by reason of traffic hazard or obstruction of road users or otherwise. 5. There are a number of deficiencies in relation to the proposed development including the absence of an adequate traffic impact assessment, insufficient details on proposed traffic calming measures or public lighting, inadequate bicycle parking facilities and the absence of turning points, footpaths or rubbing strip on the access road proposed from Bird Avenue. The applicant has also failed to provide adequate car parking in accordance with requirements of the County Development Plan 2004. The basement car parking arrangement is unsatisfactory in terms of the width of the ramps and turning radius and the excessive number of cul de sacs. The proposed development is therefore contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. 6. Having regard to the details submitted as part of the planning application it is considered that the applicant has not demonstrated sufficient legal estate or interest in the land on which it is proposed to construct the vehicular access between the site and Churchfields estate or the consent of the person who has sufficient legal estate or interest. 7. Having regard to the foul drainage proposal the outfall sewers from the terraced houses would pass through or be very close to the basement car park. This is not acceptable. It has not been demonstrated that the full requirements of the Greater Dublin Strategic Drainage Study (GDSDS) policies in relation to Sustainable Drainage Systems (SUDS) have been considered. In particular it has not been demonstrated that the four criteria set out in the GDSDS document "Regional Drainage Policies, Technical Document, Volume Two, New Development" i.e. river water quality protection, river regime protection, level of service (flooding) for site and river flood protection have been considered. The applicant has not indicated the extent to which the Site Evaluation Tool contained within the website www.irishsuds.com has been applied or demonstrated how the guidance provided in this facility has been applied to the drainage of the subject site. The proposed development may be prejudicial to public health and is therefore contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. 8. The applicant has failed to fully demonstrate compliance with Part V of the Planning and Development Act 2000 (as amended). The location of the units 27 no. units which are to be transferred under Part V have not been identified on the plans submitted. The units identified for traveller accommodation are considered to be substandard in terms of the number of bedrooms proposed. The proposed development is therefore contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area.

Dun Laoghaire Rathdown County Council - Standards for Cycle Parking and associated Cycling Facilities for New Developments (January 2018) Site Description: The subject site is located on the east side of Castlepark Road immediately to the south of a landscaped area / green at the entrance to a residential development known as St. Margaret's Close. The site has an irregular but loosely L-shaped configuration with a stated area of 0.464 hectares. The site comprises a 1930s detached two storey house known as 'Richmond' which is set back from the road with a garden and drive to the front and a large and irregularly shaped garden to the rear. The rear garden of the house, which backs onto the playing fields at Hyde Park and the rear gardens of adjoining residential properties, contains a substantial amount of mature and semi-mature trees. The rear garden also contains a granite wall with entrance piers and stone out-buildings which may pre-date the existing dwelling. There is a pair of semi-detached two storey dwellings to the south of the site - Nos. 41 and 43 Castlepark Road. There is a residential cul-de-sac development comprising 11 no. houses - St. Margaret's Close - to the north of the site. Due to the irregular shape of the application site, the approximately eastern half of the site bounds a range of other residential properties to the north and south. There is a landscaped area / green and two bungalows within the St. Margaret's Close development immediately to the north of the site and a terrace of 6 no. two storey town houses, also located within the St. Margaret's Close development, to the north west of the site. The site abuts the rear gardens of Nos. 23-26 Hyde Park to the north and Nos. 4 and 5 Gosworth Park to the south. The front boundary of the site is defined by a high masonry wall containing an electronic vehicular entrance. decision: REFUSE EXT. OF DURATION OF PERMISSION
reasons_joined: Having regard to the Fingal Development Plan 2011-2017, incorporating a Core Strategy as required by S10(1A) of the Planning and Development (Amendment) Act 2010, which is considered to be a significant change in the development objectives of the Planning Authority, the proposed development, by reason of its overconcentration of housing units on the subject site, would not be consistent with the Core Strategy and would contravene materially a development objective of the County Development Plan. Accordingly, the proposed extension of duration of permission granted under Reg. Ref F08A/1011 would no longer be consistent with, and therefore would be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The development of the kind proposed would be contrary to the objectives of the Rowlestown Local Area Plan which has identified the subject site as being suitable for no more than 8 housing units. Accordingly, the proposed extension of duration of permission granted under Reg. Ref F08A/1011 would no longer be consistent with, and therefore would be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The Fingal East Meath Flood Risk Assessment and Management Study (FEM FRAMS) provides river flood and tidal flood mapping for the study area. The Fingal East Meath Flood Risk and Management Study (FEM FRAMS) shows tidal flooding covering a significant portion of the subject site for the 1% (or 1 in 100) Fluvial and 0.1% (or 1 in 1000) Tidal Annual Exceedance Probability Flood. Allowing this development to proceed without the completion of a justification test and site specific flood risk assessment would be contrary to Objectives SW02 and SW06 of the Fingal Development Plan 2011 – 2017. Furthermore, the development would be inconsistent with proper planning and sustainable development of the area having regard to the requirements of the Planning System and Flood Risk Management - Guidelines for Planning Authorities.

The site of the proposed development is located in an area zoned with the objective ‘GB’ – ‘to protect and provide for a Green Belt’ in the Fingal Development Plan 2011 – 2017. The proposed development would thus contravene materially the zoning objective for this area and be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The applicant has submitted insufficient information on the foul and surface water drainage and water supply arrangements. The proposal would thus be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area.

The site is zoned objective ‘RA’ – 'Provide for new residential communities in accordance with approved local area plans and subject to the provision of the necessary social and physical infrastructure' in the Fingal Development Plan 2011-2017. Fingal County Council is currently preparing a local area plan. In the absence of an adopted local area plan development of the kind proposed would be premature pending adoption of a local area plan in accordance with the development plan. || Having regard to the location of the proposed development relation to neighbouring lands, road and rail infrastructure, social infrastructure including schools and open space, notwithstanding existing permissions the proposed development if permitted would represent ad hoc and piecemeal development. Good links to neighbouring lands, transport nodes and social infrastructure are essential components to providing for sustainable communities. There is currently no guarantee that these essential social and physical requirements will be completed and provided for in an acceptable and timely manner and as such to permit 400 dwellings in this isolated location would represent ad hoc and piecemeal development in an uncoordinated manner. The proposed development would, therefore, be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The proposed development in terms of layout, design and heights of buildings, particularly along the northern edge of the lands fail to fully integrate with adjoining permitted developments. The 8 storey land mark building in particular is excessive in height .The development would by reason of its height, bulk, mass and scale be incongruous, visually dominant and imposing in this designated Sensitive Landscape and would thus detract from the character of previously granted developments in the area. || Having regard to the overall proposed layout of the development, particularly the heights of buildings, orientation and juxtaposition between buildings would lead to poor serious overshadowing of courtyard areas where in particular those within Sectors 42, 43, 54 & 55 and in addition a number of the units with in the development fail to meet minimum standards set out in relation to daylight and sunlight as per ‘Site Layout Planning for Daylight and Sunlight: A Guide to Good Practice’ (B.R.E. 1991) and B.S. 8206 ‘Lighting for Buildings, Part 2 1992: Code of Practice for Daylighting’. This overshadowing is compounded by the location of private amenity space associated and associated fencing with units, particularly in Sectors As such the proposed development would afford future occupants poor levels of residential amenity and would be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || Given the poor overall proposed layout of dwellings, particularly in relation to the courtyards of Sectors 42 and 43 and with particular regard to the proposed arrangement of private and semi-private areas it is In addition inadequate provision of play areas as been indicated in accordance with Objective OS26 and OS27 of the Fingal Development Plan 20011-2017. Within the scheme there are deficiencies with the private open space allocated to individual houses and apartments contrary to the provisions of objectives OS38 and OS40 of the Development Plan. Furthermore there are also serious concerns regarding separation distances between building and living units, leading to a serious reduction in residential amenity by reducing privacy and levels of residential amenity afforded to future occupants of these units. The proposed development would therefore be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area and would be seriously injurious to the amenities of future residents. || Having regard to the road and footpath connections to the wider road network, for example the through route between Grange Road and the Coast Road, and connections to public transport nodes including the Clongriffin Railway Station the applicant has failed to demonstrate that the necessary connections can be secured and made fully operational to afford safe passage prior to the first occupation of the proposed development. Without such control the proposed development is permitted would be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || Having regard to the lack of adequate information submitted with respect to the proposed surface water drainage, foul drainage and water supply for the development the applicant has failed to comply with the Sanitary Services Acts 1878-1964 (as amended) and the proposed development would therefore be prejudicial to public health.

The Applicant has not submitted sufficient evidence to demonstrate to the satisfaction of the Planning Authority that the proposed surface water drainage system is adequate. The proposal in its current form would result in a substandard form of development which would be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area and is contrary to objective WQ05 of the Fingal Development Plan 2011-2017. || The Applicant has submitted insufficient information with regard to the foul sewer pumping station and in relation to the foul sewer pipeline. In the absence of satisfactory information, the development as proposed would be prejudicial to public health and contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area.

Having regard to the the juxtaposition of dwellings/ sites within the scheme, alongside the detailed design of dwellings relative to existing properties, as well as positioning of car parking spaces in unsupervised locations, and creation of unusable landscaping strips, the proposed layout gives rise to poor residential amenity for future occupants of the development, potential for significant overshadowing of private amenity space and potential for significant overlooking of neighbouring properties. The applicant has failed to demonstrate compliance with Objective RD13 of the Fingal Development Plan 2011-2017 and the proposed development would contravene materially the zoning objective RS ‘provide for residential development and protect and improve residential amenity’ of the Fingal Development Plan 2011-2017. || The quantum of public open space proposed for this development of 270 dwellings is below that required by the Fingal Development Plan 2011 – 2017. The proposed development therefore would contravene materially Objective OS02 of the Fingal Development Plan 2011-2017 and would be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The proposed substantial residential development does not provide for a sustainable mix of house unit sizes with 91% of the scheme comprising 4+ bed units. The proposed development would contravene materially Objective RD04 of the Fingal Development Plan 2011-2017: Ensure a mix and range of housing types are provided in all residential areas to meet the diverse needs of residents. || A significant proportion of the proposed dwellings fail to meet the private open space standards of the Fingal Development Plan 2011-2017 (Objective OS38). The proposed development would therefore seriously injure the amenities of the area and be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area.

Having regard to the quantum, quality and layout of the public open space provided, in addition to the proposed design and scale of SUDS features proposed, it is considered that the proposed development contravenes materially Objective OS02 and Objective OS25 of the Fingal Development Plan 2011-2017 and is therefore considered contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The applicant has failed to demonstrate to the satisfaction of the Planning Authority that the proposed development would not prejudice the provision of a strategic road proposal contained in the Fingal Development Plan 2011-2017. The proposed development is considered premature pending the determination of a road layout for the area and, having regard to the Zoning Objective RA, the adoption of a local area plan for the area. || The applicant has submitted insufficient information in relation to the proposed surface water drainage arrangements including design and storage capacity and the proposed development is contrary to the requirements of the Greater Dublin Strategic Drainage Study. In addition the proposed development contravenes materially Objective GI29 of the Fingal Development Plan 2011-2017 due to the lack of provision of a riparian corridor. The proposed development is therefore considered contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || With regard to layout and design, specifically the 3 storey design of house type A1, it is considered that the proposed development contravenes objective OS35 of the Fingal Development Plan 2011-2017 and would result in significant overlooking of neighbouring properties, impacting on the residential amenity of the area. In addition the proposed location and design of the bin storage areas for the mid-terrace units is considered contrary to objective RD26 of the Fingal Development Plan 2011-217 and would impact negatively on the residential amenity of the proposed dwellings.

The proposed development of 17 housing units is located on lands zoned ‘OS’ open space and which has the objective to ‘Preserve and provide for open space and recreational amenities’. Residential development is listed within the ‘Not Permitted’ category of the ‘OS’ zoning and therefore the proposed development is contrary to the zoning that applies to this site. The proposed development would contravene materially a development objective indicated in the Fingal Development Plan 2011 – 2017 for the use of these lands for open space purposes. || The proposed development would set an undesirable precedent for other similar developments, which would in themselves and cumulatively be harmful to the residential amenities of the area and be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area.

The proposed development by reason of: (a) The inappropriate design and location of car parking relative to the residential units intended to serve, (b) the unresolved vehicular access arrangements and (c) the potential for vehicular and pedestrian conflict would result in a substandard form of development thereby creating a poor residential environment for intending occupants. The development as proposed would therefore seriously injure the residential amenities of future residents and would be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The design and linear layout of the proposed residential blocks providing for gable frontage to St. Margaret’s Road would fail to contribute in a meaningful way to the urban fabric of the area or the enhancement of the streetscape which would otherwise be achieved by the redevelopment of this prominent brownfield site. The proposed residential scheme would be visually unsatisfactory and would seriously injure the amenities of the area and would be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the Meakstown area.

The proposed three storey apartment block located to the northern boundary of the site by reason of its design, architectural expression and limited contribution to the streetscape at this prominent town centre location would fail to provide a sufficiently high standard of development on site and would seriously injure the amenities of the area. The development as proposed would therefore be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of Donabate. || The proposed development would set an undesirable precedent for other similar developments, which would in themselves and cumulatively be harmful to the visual amenities of the area and be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area.

The proposed development is located to the west of Brackenstown House, which is a protected structure listed as RPS No. 364 and 364a. The applicant was requested to demonstrate that the proposed development would have regard to this protected structure with particular reference to the impact of the scheme on the main avenue of Brackenstown House. The applicant has failed to adequately address this issue. The proposed development has the potential to materially affect a protected structure and would contravene materially Objective CH20 of the Fingal Development Plan. || The applicant has failed to demonstrate that appropriate levels of public open space in accordance with Objective DMS57A of the Fingal Development Plan 2017 – 2023, which requires a minimum of 10% of a site area be designated for use as public open space in respect of the proposed housing scheme. The proposed development would therefore materially contravene a development objective of the Fingal Development Plan and would through a lack of public open space seriously injure the residential amenities of future and existing residents in the area. || The submitted plans are ambiguous and unclear in relation to the extent of the development proposed and in the absence of such clarity would fail to adequately inform the general public as to the nature of the development and would represent as a consequence, a substandard form of development.

The subject lands have an area of 2.79 ha and form part of the Flemington Lane Masterplan lands, a strategically important area of development land to the north of Balbriggan. The subject lands are zoned ‘RA’ in the Fingal Development Plan 2017 – 2023 and are identified as being within an area which is subject to a Masterplan (MP 4.A refers). Given the overall area of the Flemington Lane Masterplan lands i.e. c. 17.1 ha and the potential for a significant quantum of residential development, between 599 and 855 houses (based on the density guidance set out in the Sustainable Residential Development in Urban Areas), the fragmented ownership of the lands, the required improvements to local road infrastructure, the archaeological potential of the lands, the preparation of a Masterplan by the Planning Authority is considered to be an essential prerequisite to ensure an integrated and plan led approach to development of the area. The proposed development comprising a development of 74 no. dwellings in the absence of a Masterplan prepared by the Planning Authority in the manner set out in Section 11.3 of the Fingal Development Plan 2017 – 2023 entitled ‘Masterplans’ setting out the objectives for the lands in respect of density, open space, community infrastructure, and traffic calming/re-alignment of Flemington Lane would represent an ad-hoc, piecemeal approach to the development of the area and would result in an un-integrated and inequitable provision of community facilities and public infrastructure. The proposed development would therefore contravene materially Objective PM14 of the Fingal Development Plan 2017 – 2023 and would be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The proposed development has a resultant density of 27 dpha. The subject site is an ‘Outer Suburban/Greenfield Site’ under the Sustainable Residential Development in Urban Areas (DoEHLG May 2009) and a density of 35 – 50 dwellings per hectare is considered appropriate for lands of this nature under the Guidelines. The proposed density of 27 dpha would not accord with the Sustainable Residential Development in Urban Areas (DoEHLG May 2009). The proposed development would, if permitted, be contrary to the Sustainable Residential Development in Urban Areas (DoEHLG May 2009). || The Childcare Facilities (Guidelines for Planning Authorities) June 2001 published by the DoHLG provides for the provision of an average of one childcare facility per 75 no. dwellings in new residential areas. Noting the scale of the proposed development (i.e. 1 no. dwelling below the 75 no. houses which triggers the requirement for a childcare facility) and the role of the subject site within the Flemington Lane Masterplan lands where there is a clear requirement for a commensurate level of childcare facilities, permitting the development would not accord with the principles set out in the Childcare Facilities (Guidelines for Planning Authorities) June 2001. The proposed development would, if permitted, be contrary to the Childcare Facilities (Guidelines for Planning Authorities) June 2001. || The provision of an underground attenuation tank under the public open space is not considered acceptable. Objective DMS74 of the Fingal Development Plan 2017 – 2023 provides that ‘underground tanks and storage systems will not be accepted under public open space, as part of a SuDS solution’. Accordingly the surface water drainage design for the proposed development would contravene materially Objective DMS74 of the Fingal Development Plan 2017 – 2023 and would be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area.

The application site is located within a part of the County with the zoning objective RA – Residential Area which seeks to ‘Provide for new residential communities subject to the provision of the necessary social and physical infrastructure’ as set out with the Fingal Development Plan 2017 -2023. In addition the application site forms part of Streamstown Local Area Plan 2009 which has been extended until 9th February 2019. Under Section 5.1.3. Childcare Facilities it states ‘A minimum of two childcare facilities are to be provided, in accordance with the standards set out in the Childcare Facilities Guidelines and in consultation with the Planning Authority. Under this application it is proposed to omit the previously permitted stand-alone creche and associated car parking area and replace it with an area of open space. The proposed development, would materially contravene an objective indicated in the local area plan for the area and would materially contravene objective PM76 of the Development Plan 2017-2023 and due to the removal of necessary social infrastructure for a new residential area under development, would materially contravene the 'RA' zoning for the land and would be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || Under Objective WT12, Fingal Development Plan 2017-2023 it states ‘Establish an appropriate buffer zone around all pumping stations suitable to the size and operation of each station. The buffer zone should be a minimum 35 metres – 50 metres from the noise/odour producing part of the pumping station to avoid nuisance from odour and noise’. The applicant is proposing to locate residential housing within 15m of a proposed pumping station and is therefore contrary to Objective WT12. The proposed development would be prejudicial to public health. || Under the Streamstown LAP, lands directly to the rear of Streamstown House are identified as ‘indicative open areas’ and a circular symbol on the map centred on this house was to ensure that ‘on-site residential amenity is protected’. The proposed development given its two storey nature and depth of garden would lead to overlooking of that property. Moreover, the scale and form of the three houses proposed would impact on the design height and character of Streamstown House and impact on its setting and amenity. The proposed development would impact negatively on the existing house and impact on the residential amenity of the occupants. || The changes to the layout of the open space provision as a result of the proposed new housing will have a negative impact on the quality of that open space. Currently the open space provision on site can be viewed as a single area with adults/children freely able to access all of the open space without crossing a road once on the lands. The proposed new housing would dissect the open space by the new access road resulting in the open space appearing piecemeal, fragmented and less usable and contrary to the proper planning and development of the area. || Under Condition 12.F14A/0483 (PL 06F. 245240) it states ‘The area of open space shown on the lodged plans shall be reserved for such use. These areas shall be levelled, contoured, soiled and seeded, to a degree which maximises h their use and potential and which is acceptable to the planning authority. This work shall be completed before any of the dwellings are made available for occupation. The open spaces shall be kept free of any development, shall not be incorporated into house plots and shall be maintained as public open space by the developer until taken in charge by the local authority’. The proposed development would therefore contravene materially a condition attached to an existing permission for development.

The proposed development is accessed from a narrow shared surface that serves as a pedestrian route/ public road and is designated as an 'Indicative Cycle/ Pedestrian Route' in the Fingal Development Plan 2017 - 2023. The proposed development as submitted, with the access from the site onto Church Road would endanger public safety by reason of traffic hazard. || By reason of its design and location on this prominent site of restricted size and configuration, the proposed development of a five storey apartment block would be unduly obtrusive and out of character with the pattern of development in the area. The proposed development would, therefore, seriously injure the amenities of the area and of property in the vicinity and would be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The proposed development by reason of the excessive density would provide a substandard level of private and communal amenity space as a result of sub-standard depth of balcony space and a lack of landscaping details. The majority of the public open space provision would be unusable and would provide a poor level of amenity for future residents of the apartment block. Moreover, the proposed development would seriously injure the amenities and depreciate the value of property in the vicinity through substandard design of open space, and as such, would be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The proposed development would provide for a poor level of residential amenity due to the arrangement of access to these apartment units by means of a deck access with a single point of entry. The layout of the deck access is such that the amenity of residents in their bedrooms would be negatively impacted upon. The proposed development would therefore result in a poor quality of amenity and as such would be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || Having regard to the lack of adequate information submitted with respect to the proposed foul drainage, surface water drainage and water supply for the development, the applicant has therefore failed to demonstrate compliance with the Sanitary Services Acts and the proposed development could therefore be prejudicial to public health. || According to Fingal County Council's Strategic Flood Risk Assessment, the subject site is partly located within an area which is at risk of flooding. Having regard to the lack of a Flood Risk Assessment demonstrating compliance with the 'Planning System and Flood Risk Management - Guidelines for Planning Authorities, November 2009', the proposed development as submitted is in an area which is at risk of flooding. || The proposed development would adversely affect the setting of the Old Schoolhouse public house/ restaurant, of which it is necessary to preserve. The proposed development is therefore contrary to the direction provided in Chapter 12 - Development Management Standards of the Fingal Development Plan 2017 - 2023. || The proposed development is considered to be premature pending the assessment and completion of a route option for the indicative cycle/ pedestrian route along Schoolhouse Lane which is an objective of the Fingal Development Plan 2017 – 2023. || The proposed development is located on an area that is designated as an approved car parking area to serve the adjacent The Old Schoolhouse public house and brewery development approved under Condition no. 1 of Reg. Ref. F15A/0308. The car parking proposed at a rate of 1 space per unit does not provide for dual purpose parking serving the existing Old Schoolhouse and Brewery development permitted under F15A/0308 and the subject apartments. The proposed development would therefore materially contravene the site layout car parking arrangements approved under condition no. 1 of Reg. Ref. F15A/0308

The proposed temporary pumping station and underground foul water holding tank locations do not comply with Objective WT12 of the Fingal Development Plan 2017-2023. Objective WT12; 'Establish an appropriate buffer zone around all pumping stations suitable to the size and operation of each station. The buffer zone should be a minimum 35 metres - 50 metres from the noise/odour producing part of the pumping station to avoid nuisance from odour and noise. The development would therefore be premature by reason of the existing deficiency in the design of the development and provision of sewage facilities to cater for the development and would as a consequence be prejudicial to public health and be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development. || The applicant has not clearly demonstrated to the Planning Authority the required sightlines at this location and as such to permit the proposed entrance and vehicular roadway in its proposed form would give rise to a traffic hazard. || The proposed development would provide for a poor quality of residential amenity through a substandard site layout. Insufficient and poorly designed public open space has been provided to serve future residents, contrary to Objectives DMS57 and DMS57A of the Fingal Development Plan 2017 - 2023 and the provision of public open space to the side of Units 20 and 21 would be contrary to Objective DMS66. The proposed development would, therefore, seriously injure the amenities of the area and of property in the vicinity and would be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area.

Having regard to the scale and location of the proposed development on the edge of the rural village of Rowlestown, taking account of: • Regional Policy Objective 4.83 of the Regional Spatial and Economic Strategy for Eastern and Midlands Area 2019- 2031, which seeks to 'support the consolidation of the town and village network to ensure that development proceeds sustainably and at an appropriate scale, level and pace in line with the core strategies of the county development plans', • The policy of the Fingal Development Plan 2017-2023 for villages which states that 'villages will be managed to ensure these centres do not expand rapidly, putting pressure on services and the environment and creating the potential for unsustainable travel patterns' and that 'future growth in commuter villages should be curtailed or safeguarded so that they do not act as a catalyst to facilitate continuing expansion of unsustainable growth patterns', it is considered that when taken in the context of existing and permitted development in the vicinity, the proposed development would be contrary to the settlement hierarchy set out in the Regional Spatial and Economic Strategy for the region and the settlement strategy of the Fingal Development Plan 2017-2023 and as such, would be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || It is considered that the proposed development of 59 houses on the subject site, taken in the context of existing and permitted development in Rowlestown would result in rapid uneven growth of the Rural Village, which taking account of: • National Policy Objective 15 (NPO 15) of the National Planning Framework which seeks to "support the sustainable development of rural areas by ...managing the growth of areas that are under strong urban influences to avoid overdevelopment"; • Regional Policy Objective RPO 4.83 which seeks consolidation of rural villages • RV land use zoning objective of the Fingal Development Plan 2017-2023 which seeks to "Protect and promote the character of the Rural Village" • Objective PM18 of the Fingal Development Plan 2017-2023 which seeks to implement the village design framework, • Objective RF04 which seeks to manage the development of each village, within the RV boundaries having regard to Government Guidelines set down in the Sustainable Residential Development in Urban Areas, 2009 would result in development of the village beyond its assimilative capacity as articulated in national, regional, county and local policy. The development if permitted would negatively impact on the character of the village, place excessive pressure on local services, contribute to unsustainable travel patterns, would not be commensurate with the existing built environment and would therefore be contrary to the policy for rural villages as set out in the Regional Spatial and Economic Strategy (RSES), and the Fingal Development Plan and would therefore be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || Due to the peripheral site location, it is unlikely that adequate provision can be made for walking, cycling or public transport infrastructure between the subject site and Swords, the lack of connectivity is likely to give rise to an over reliance on private car use for both local and non-local trips across all journey purposes contrary to national policy, the provisions of the Regional Spatial & Economic Strategy and the Fingal County Development Plan, in particular Objective SS03 to prevent car dependent urban sprawl. || Taking account of the suburban character of the proposal at the edge of the small village of Rowlestown, the proposed development would negatively impact on the rural village character of Rowlestown, would not contribute to the consolidation or to the enhancement of the village and when considered in combination with recently permitted development, would contribute to excessive growth of the village within a short period of time. The proposal would therefore be contrary to the Sustainable Residential Development in Urban Areas guidelines issued by the Minster under Section 28 of the Planning and Development Act 2000, as amended.

The proposed development in itself and cumulatively would, by reason of existing deficiencies in the road network serving the proposed development including insufficient capacity to cater for the increased road traffic that would be generated from the development and poor connectivity for pedestrians and cyclists would endanger public safety by reason of traffic hazard. The proposed development is also considered premature pending the necessary upgrades of the adjoining road network and would therefore be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || Fingal County Council’s minimum requirements for public open space provision and playground provision have not been met therefore the proposed development would result in a dense suburban type development which would be out of character in this rural setting. The excessive scale of the proposed 98 residential unit development would be out of character with the amenities of this rural area. The proposed development would therefore be contrary to the proper planning and development of the area.

A significant number of the apartment units within the proposed development do not meet the minimum requirements of the ‘Sustainable Urban Housing: Design Standards for New Apartments Guidelines for Planning Authorities 2018 (Department of Environment, Community and Local Government) in relation to overall apartment area, storage provision and bedroom areas. It is the policy of Galway County Council to endeavour to promote the orderly and phased development of residential lands in accordance with the principles of the sequential approach and as set out in the Sustainable Residential Development in Urban Areas (Cities Towns and Villages) Guidelines 2009. The site is located in an area not currently zoned for development, on the outer south-western edge of Athenry town. It is the policy of Galway County Council to encourage the orderly and phased development of residential lands in accordance with the principles of the sequential approach as set out in the Sustainable Residential Development in Urban Areas (Cities Towns and Villages) Guidelines 2009. This shall include a positive presumption in favour of the sequential development of suitable serviced lands in zoned towns and villages. The development as proposed does not contribute to the compact growth of Athenry and is non- sequential in its siting at this location having regard to more suitably zoned and physically connected lands within the urban environs of Athenry. It is considered that the proposed development would be contrary to Policy Objectives CS 2, CS3, CGR 1 and PM1 of the Galway County Development Plan 2022-2028, would set an undesirable precedent for similar such development and would thus be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The proposed development does not provide satisfactory or otherwise sufficiently developed proposals for connectivity to the wider urban pedestrian and cycle network and, if granted, would pose an increased risk to the safety of pedestrians and other road users, and in addition, lead to unsustainable mobility patterns due to the impact the discontinuities in the pedestrian and cycle network will have on individual mobility choice. The proposed development would accordingly be prejudicial to public safety and contravene sustainable transport policy objectives ILUTP1 and WC3 of the current Galway County Development Plan. || The proposed developm ent would represent an inappropriate form of development at this location where the proposed density and configuration does not relate to either its context or the surrounding development in a manner consistent with sustainable urban placemaking and the siting of same results in poor quality layout with insufficient definition of character areas and definition and enclosure of a hierarchy of sufficiently sized central and usable public and communal spaces. Accordingly, to grant the proposed development wou ld be detrimental to the character of the area and would be contrary to Sections 2.2, 2.7, 4.16 and 6.8 of Sustainable Residential Development in Urban Areas – Guidelines for Planning Authorities (DEHLG 2009). It would furthermore detract from the visual a nd residential amenity of the area, would be contrary to objectives PM 1, PM 6, PM 8 and PM 10, UL2 and UL5, as well as development management standards DM1 and DM2 contained in the Galway County Development Plan 2022 -2028, as well as setting an undesirabl e precedent for similar future development, and therefore would be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. Decision to refuse the planning application

The development by reason of the proposed layout represents an inappropriate development on this existing residential site and considered out of keeping with the existing pattern of development and would represent an incongruous form of development which if approved would be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable developme nt of the area and is contrary to Policy Objectives GCMA4, BMSP1, PM8, PM10 and UL2 as well as DM Standard 2 of the Galway County Development Plan 2022 -2028 and accordingly, to grant the development as proposed , would be contrary to the principles of the p roper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The proposed development does not provide an appropriate level and quality of public open space and is contrary to Policy Objective UL5 of the Galway County Development Plan 2022 - 2028 as well as reco mmended guidance, Sustainable Residential Development in Urban Areas. Accordingly, to grant the development as proposed, would contravene a policy objective of the Galway County Development Plan 2022 -2028, and would represent a substandard provision of pri vate open space to the detriment of future occupiers and therefore, contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the local area. || Notwithstanding the indicative future road realignment masterplan, the proposed development lacks an appropr iate footpath connection to the existing footpath network and, if granted, would pose a risk to the safety of pedestrians and other road users, and in addition, contravene sustainable transport Policy Objectives GCTPS 4, ILUTP 1, WC1 and DM Standard 22 of the Galway County Development Plan 2022-2028 and would be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The applicant has not submitted a Linguistic Impact Statement and is therefore considered contrary to Policy Objective GA 4 of the Galway County Development Plan 2022 -2028 to ensure that permanent residents enhance and reinforce the development of the Irish language as the community’s primary language, and would therefore materially contravene a policy objective of the Galway County Development Plan 2022 -2028 and would be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || In the absence of any details submitted on file from Irish Water relating to consent to connect to the public waste and water infrastr ucture to serve the proposed development, it is considered that the development if permitted as proposed, would be contrary to Policy Objective WS4 and DM Standard 36 of the Galway County Development Plan, 2022 -2028, and would be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The proposed design of the dwellings, in conjunction with the lack of innovative layout, the breaking of the established building line, are considered out of keeping with the local character and identity of surrounding development and does not represent a development which is designed to be cognisant of its context. If approved, the proposed development would have a negative impact on the residential amenity of both future and existing residents and would not represent high quality design, contrary to Policy Objective PM10 and DM Standard 29 of the Galway County Development Plan 2022-2028 and therefore would be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The Planning Authority are not satisfied based on submissions received regarding the suitability of the proposed access off the L -1321 within the speed limit of 80kph and the proposed intensification of use. Having regard to the information submitted with the planning application details, the submissions received, the proximity of the site to the Galway Bay Complex SAC and Inner Galway Bay SPA, the connectivity from the project site to the aforementioned European sites in conjunction with the deficiencies and lacunae identified in the NIS submitted as identified by the planning authority, including an incomplete assessment of the entire project site, the planning authority cannot be satisfied that the proposed development will not have an adverse effect on the Galway Bay Complex SAC and Inner Galway Bay SPA, in view of their conservation objectives, alone or in combination with other plans and projects. Therefore, if permitted as proposed, the development would materially contravene NHB1, NHB2 and NHB3 of the Galway County Development Plan 2022 -2028 and would be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || Having regard to the location of the subject site situated onto the R -338 Regional Road, a heavily trafficked arterial route, where the 80kph speed limit applies, it is considered that the proposed development would result in additional traffic turning movements being generated at a point, where the horizontal and vertical alignment of the public road is restricted and whereby the intensification of use and required visibility would constitute a significant intervention on a Regional /local road, in contravention of Development Management Standards 28 and 33 and Policy Objectives NNR2 of the Galway County Development Plan 2022-2028. Therefore, in relation to safeguarding the transport function of regional & local roads and associated regional & local road junctions, it is considered that the proposed development would interfere with safety and endanger public safety by reason of traffic hazard or obstruction of road users or otherwise and therefore would be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The planning authority have serious concerns regarding the capacity of the surrounding road network to accommodate the proposed development, taking account of: - the vehicular dominated layout in conjunction with the lack of sustainable connectivity and quality of permeability measures evident; - the suitability of the proposed external and internal traffic circulation regime; - the potential for conflicting traffic movements, including rigid movements due to restricted and reversing vehicle maneuverability within and adjoining the site, which may negatively impact on road and pedestrian safety; -the geometrical parameters evident with regard to the development road layout contrary to the desirable minimum DMURS standards, TII publications and Cycle Design Manual; and -the absence of demonstrating compatible linkages with the proposed Strategic Greenway Network (preferred route of the Galway to Athlone Corridor); Accordingly, to grant permission for the development as proposed would have an unacceptable impact on the sustainable movement and transportation of the area and would materially contravene policy objectives ILUTP1, WC1, WC3, GBW1 and DM Standards 28 and 33 of the Galway County Development Plan 2022 -2028 and therefore would be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || Having regard to the general design of the proposed layout including the lack of satisfactory urban design and placemaking considerations and the similarity in the design of a significant SCHEDULE REFERRED TO - PLANNING REFERENCE NO. 24/60733 3 number of residential units, in conjunction with the absence of provision of connected green spaces/corridors within the scheme and deficiencies in the private open space provision for a number of units, it is considered that the proposal represents a substandard form of development that would also compromise the residential amenity of future occupants. Accordingly, to grant the proposed development would contravene materially Policy Objectives PM 1, PM 5, PM 6, PM 8, PM 13 and UL 2 as well as Development Management Standards DM1 contained in the Galway County Development Plan 2022 -2028, would set an undesirable precedent for similar future development and would be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The development proposal fails to satisfactorily take account of the wider Garraun Urban Framework Plan area, and does not satisfactorily demonstrate the vision, principles or objectives of the Urban Framework Plan, particularly in terms of sustainable connectivity, landscape and placemaking considerations. Therefore, if permitted as proposed the development would be contrary to Policy Objective GUFP 10 of the Garraun Urban Framework Plan as set out under the Galway County Development Plan 2022 -2028 and would therefore be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. The survey includes contours, spot levels on the site (all to Malin Head datum), site boundary, edge of road, agriculture stone wall and fence. The subject site slopes continually from the south-west corner of the site (high point) at an elevation of approximately 33.3m OD to the north-west corner of the site at an elevation of 30.3m OD (low point). There are a few localised high points on the site, however, other than localised areas of cut and fill, it is envisaged that largely existing ground levels will be retained for this development. Refer to topographical survey layout drawing number 240741-ORS-ZZ-00-DR-TII-001 and the trial pit locations included in Appendix A of this report. 2.2 Infiltration Survey Three infiltration tests were carried out by Limekin Construction at various locations throughout the site. The locations of the test pits are shown in Appendix A of this report. The results of the infiltration tests are also included in Appendix A. RECEIVED: 21/11/2025 5 A World-Class Multidisciplinary Building Consultancy The infiltration test results were input into Tekla Tedds software, which was used to size the proposed infiltration tanks serving the development. The program allows for the input of key parameters including rainfall data, catchment areas, runoff coefficients, infiltration rates, and storage characteristics, in order to calculate the required storage volume and determine the appropriate tank dimensions. This process ensures that the design of the infiltration system is in accordance with SuDS principles and complies with the requirements of BRE 365. 3 Scope of Services Report The objective of this Engineering Services Planning Report is to design the following elements to accommodate the works as follows: • Design a new stormwater network and attenuation tanks. • Design a new foul water network. • Design a new watermain network. • Design a new internal road, junction and parking facilities. 4 Design Codes & Standards The civil engineering works presented in this report and the accompanying drawings have been designed in accordance with the following codes of practice and standards: • “ Irish Building Regulations Technical Guidance Documents” Department of the Environment and Local Government • “Greater Dublin Strategic Drainage Study” published under the National Development Plan • UK SuDS Manual - CIRIA Report “C753 – Sustainable Drainage Systems” • EPA - Wastewater Treatment Manuals – Treatment Systems for Small Communities, Business, Leisure Centres and Hotels • Guidance on the Authorisation of Discharges to Groundwater (EPA, 2011) • EPA – Groundwater Protection Responses for On-site Wastewater Systems for Single Houses • EPA - Guidance on the Authorisation of Discharges to Groundwater • European Communities Environmental Objectives (Surface Water) Regulations, 2009. RECEIVED: 21/11/2025 6 A World-Class Multidisciplinary Building Consultancy 5 Wastewater Drainage 5.1 Existing Wastewater Services in Area There is existing wastewater in the public road to the west of the site that flows in a south easterly direction. Cover and Invert Levels of the upstream and downstream manholes of this network are provided on the Topographical Survey drawing 240741-ORS-ZZ-00-DR-TII-001. Figure 3: Existing Public Wastewater Drainage Network in Area It is proposed to connect to the public wastewater drainage network along the L1309 Clifden Rd. A Confirmation Of Feasibility letter has been provided by Uisce Eireann under reference Number CDS24010140 which is included in Appendix D of this Report. 5.2 Wastewater Discharge It is proposed to connect to the existing wastewater drainage network along the L1309 Clifden Rd. The existing drainage within the L1309 flows from north-west to south-east past the development site. From records this pipe is noted as an existing 225mm diameter pipe. The anticipated wastewater loading for the development, has been calculated in accordance with the Irish Water – Code of Practice for Wastewater Infrastructure (Appendix A – Wastewater Flow Rates for Design). Calculations are shown in Appendix A of this Report. The proposed internal wastewater sewer will consist of a series of 150mm diameter sewer pipes falling at 1:80. 100mm diameter pipes will be provided between access junctions enclosing dwellings and falling at a minimum grade of 1 in 60. All internal wastewater drainage pipe will be separate to surface water drainage infrastructure in accordance with IW COP. The lower ground floor block of units will require a pumping station which will be provided in the RECEIVED: 21/11/2025 7 A World-Class Multidisciplinary Building Consultancy northern corner of the site, and which will pump the wastewater effluent back to a manhole where it will rejoin the gravity network within the site as indicated on the 240741-ORS-ZZ-00- DR-TII-500 & 501. The minimum requirements of the pumping station will be in accordance with Section 5 of IW-CDS-5030-03 (Revision 2-2020) Emergency storage capacity, based on dry weather flow will be provided in the pumping station for 24 hours. All wastewater infrastructure shall be designed and constructed in accordance with Irish Water documents “Code of Practice for Wastewater Infrastructure” and “Wastewater Infrastructure Standard Details”. Refer to Foul Drainage drawings on 240741-ORS-ZZ-00-DR- TII-500 & 501 for details in Appendix B. RECEIVED: 21/11/2025 8 A World-Class Multidisciplinary Building Consultancy 6 Surface Water Drainage 6.1 Existing Stormwater Drainage There is no stormwater drainage network available in the vicinity of the proposed development. From the topographical survey it noted that the existing stormwater pipe is located within the landscaped area, to the north of the existing access road. Refer to Figure 4 below for details. Figure 4: Existing Stormwater Drainage Infrastructure. 6.1 Surface Water Discharge Guidance for the design of the surface and rainwater network has been taken from the Sustainable Urban Drainage System (SUD’s) and BRE365 Soakaway Design as per the standard practice. The following design criteria has been incorporated into the design: • All surface water pipes have been designed to achieve a minimum self-cleansing velocity of 0.75m/s. • Surface water pipework will be laid no flatter that 1 is to 150. • Minimum surface water pipe size of 225mm diameter as per LA requirements • Minimum depth of cover to pipework of 1.2m below roads without appropriate protection. • Roughness value for surface water pipework of k s 0.6mm 6.2 Proposed Surface Water Drainage Strategy The proposed site will be served via a below ground gravity pipework system which predominantly runs beneath the internal roads, landscaped areas, and car park within the RECEIVED: 21/11/2025 9 A World-Class Multidisciplinary Building Consultancy development. Surface water runoff will be collected from road gullies and building roofs via guttering and downpipes, which will enter the stormwater network and be conveyed eastwards to an outfall pipe located at the front of Block C. At this location, a non-return valve will be provided to prevent backflow. From here, the stormwater will discharge into the permeable paving system at the front of Block C, where it will percolate and flow in a northwesterly direction through the sub-base storage layer. The network will then outfall into a petrol interceptor, a catchpit manhole, and a soak pit, providing both pollutant removal and controlled infiltration into the underlying soils. Sustainable Urban Drainage Systems (SuDS) will be utilised throughout the site where practical to help mitigate the adverse effects of urban stormwater runoff on the environment by reducing runoff rates, volumes and frequencies and reducing pollutant concentrations in stormwater runoff. SuDS measures which have been incorporated in this scheme include the use of permeable paving to the car parking to the south of the buildings. As noted in UK SUDS guidance document the soil run off rates for this area is deemed to be 0.30 (soil type 2). This value has been used to calculate the greenfield runoff rate for this development. From reviewing Met Eireann SAAR values for this specific site location, it was determined that the SAAR value for this site is 1381mm This value has been used to calculate the greenfield runoff rate for this development. 6.3 Permeable Paving The private car park on site is proposed to be constructed using permeable paving, with the exception of disabled car parking spaces which will be finished in conventional surfacing to accommodate line marking and hatching requirements. Permeable paving provides a pavement suitable for pedestrian and vehicular traffic while allowing rainwater to infiltrate through the surface and into the underlying structural layers. The water is temporarily stored beneath the surface before controlled discharge to the downstream drainage system. For this development, an impermeable liner will be installed beneath the permeable paving system to prevent uncontrolled infiltration into adjacent ground and to control hydrocarbons . Stormwater will be collected within the permeable pavement and directed under a minimum fall of 1:200 north-westerly discharging first into a petrol interceptor and then to Infiltration Tank A. The paving build- up and construction detail are provided in Drawing 240741-ORS-ZZ-00-DR- TII-510 in Appendix C. 6.4 Compliance with Sustainable Urban Drainage Systems To reduce and attenuate the flow, the proposed development has been designed in accordance with the principles of Sustainable Urban Drainage Systems (SUDS) as expressed in the recommendations of the Greater Dublin Strategic Drainage Study (GDSDS). The GDSDS addresses the issue of sustainability by requiring designs to comply with a set of drainage criteria which aim to minimise the impact of urbanisation by replicating the runoff characteristics of a greenfield site. The criteria provide a consistent approach to addressing both rate and volume of run-off as well as ensuring the environment is protected from pollution that is washed off roads and buildings. RECEIVED: 21/11/2025 10 A World-Class Multidisciplinary Building Consultancy The requirements of SUDS are typically addressed by provision of the following: • Interception storage. • Treatment storage (not required if interception storage is provided). • Attenuation storage. • Long term storage (not required if growth factors are not applied to Qbar when designing attenuation storage). In the case of the subject site, interception storage will be provided, and growth factors will not be applied to the allowable discharge for the 100- year event. This means that both treatment storage and long-term storage (neither of which would be practical on this site) are not required. Refer to Storm Drainage drawings in 240741-ORS-ZZ-00-DR-TII-500 & 502 and details contained within Appendix C of this report. 6.5 Petrol Interceptors To provide treatment, the surface water that flows through the permeable paving will pass through a petrol interceptor before discharging to a manhole and infiltration tank A. Kildare 1 July 2018 51720 Final EXECUTIVE SUMMARY Verde carried out a Tier 2 hydrogeological assessment in relation to the proposed Sustainable urban Drainage System (SuDS) design and associated discharge of stormwater to groundwater for a proposed residential development at Dunmurray Road, Co. Kildare. The proposed development will be serviced by mains water and foul drainage system present in the area. A series of detailed site investigations were undertaken by IGSL Ltd on the existing greenfield site in April and May 2018 to determine the suitability of the site for a surface water drainage system from the proposed development. The development greenfield site is located 800m north-west of Kildare town. The site is bounded to the north and west by agricultural land and residential housing. There are no surface watercourses in the immediate vicinity of the site with the nearest ecologically sensitive designated site being the Pollardstown Fen SAC, 4km north-east of the site. Detailed percolation and BRE365 infiltration testing of the subsoils showed favourable ground conditions across most of the development site with higher permeability rates in the western region. The Tier 2 site investigation work shows a thick unsaturated zone of over 14metres indicating moderate vulnerability, which allows high infiltration capacity of stormwater prior to reaching groundwater in the deeper subsoils and underlying limestone bedrock aquifer. From the three groundwater monitoring wells drilled on-site it can be seen that the groundwater flow direction follows the site topography in a south to south-easterly flow direction, as presented in Figure 3. During drilling groundwater strikes were not encountered until deep in the sand and gravel subsoils or top of limestone bedrock from 16.8mBGL. No groundwater was detected in the shallow subsoil wells to 5mBGL. There is therefore a thick unsaturated zone with good capacity to accept storm water from the proposed development and allow for attenuation of any potential runoff contaminants. Overall it can be seen from the summary of permeability tests that the western half of the greenfield site has significantly more permeable subsoils compared to the eastern half. The western subsoils are seen to consist of sandy silty GRAVEL with predominantly silty CLAY on the eastern side of the site, which coincides with a pond like feature in a depression in this area of the site and is related to poor drainage through these clays. Information from the detailed site investigation, infiltration and permeability values have been used to design the discharge of stormwater to ground via infiltration trenches in five of the six sub catchments. A designed infiltration blanket is to be placed in sub-catchment 6 located in the north-east portion of the site where lower permeability subsoils are present. All three monitoring wells were sampled in May 2018. Hydrocarbons were undetected in all of the three groundwater monitoring wells on-site. Overall the baseline groundwater quality analysis shows some localised recent faecal impact in the central region of the site related to livestock activity with the chemical quality having some elevated naturally occurring parameters. Overall is can be seen from the summary of permeability tests undertaken in the subsoils from the IGSL T/P & BRE365 percolation tests and Verde borehole permeability tests that the western half of the greenfield site has significantly more permeable subsoils compared to the eastern half. Meath CC, Planning Department, Viewing Purposes Only! 25 5.0 Step 4: Determination of Significance 5.1 Impact prediction Under Article 6 of the Habitats Directive a ‘significant effect’ must be measured against the conservation objectives for the SAC or SPA in question. Unlike Environmental Impact Assessment for instance, there are no degrees of significance and where an effect is determined to be significant a stage 2 AA must be undertaken, where mitigation or avoidance measures can be considered. In order for an impact to occur there must be a pathway between the development (the source) and the SAC or SPA (the receptor). Where a pathway does not exist then an impact cannot occur. The subject site is not located within, or directly adjacent to any SAC or SPA. However, pathways for impacts do exist via surface water and treated wastewater to SACs and SPAs in the Boyne Estuary. The development cannot result in direct impacts to habitats within any designated area, either through habitat removal or disturbance, due to the significant separation distances involved. Site specific conservation objectives have been set for all of the aforementioned SACs or SPAs with the exception of the River Boyne and River Blackwater SAC and none of these objectives relates to water quality. There is no evidence that unsatisfactory water quality is negatively affecting habitat or bird populations. Pollution is in any case undesirable and this development will not infringe upon efforts to enhance water quality under the Water Framework Directive. Following on from steps 1 – 3 of this process a number of specific impacts are considered: 5.1.1 Habitat loss This development will not result in the loss of any habitat within or adjacent to any SAC or SPA. 5.1.2 Habitat disturbance No habitats will be directly disturbed within or directly connecting to Natura 2000 areas. Indirect disturbance is unlikely to occur through amenity pressures on coastal areas. 5.1.3 Pollution during construction There are no water courses on the lands although surface drainage pathways are likely to lead ultimately to the Stagrennan Stream and thereon to the Boyne Estuary. Although temporary, it is considered that the loss of construction pollutants to the estuary could result in impacts to invertebrate communities within estuary and mudflat habitats. Significant effects to the Boyne Coast and Estuary SAC therefore cannot be ruled out. These measures are standard features for all development projects and are not introduced here to avoid or reduce an effect to a Natura 2000 area. Therefore the use of SUDS is not considered to be mitigation in an AA context. The Drogheda wastewater treatment plant is not in compliance with prescribed treatment standards and however ample capacity exists to accept the likely additional loading from this development. No significant effects to Natura areas are likely to arise from these sources. 5.1.5 Abstraction There is no evidence that abstraction from the River Boyne is resulting in ecological pressures. This aspect of the project is not considered to be significant. 6.0 Conclusions of Stage 1 Screening Hydrological pathways exist to the Boyne Coast and Estuary SAC and the Boyne Estuary SPA; significant effects have been ruled out to the Boyne Estuary SPA and the River Boyne and River Blackwater SAC and SPA. No significant effects will occur to these Natura 2000 sites either alone or in combination with other plans and projects. No significant effects will occur to the Clogher Head SAC or the River Nanny and Shore SPA and there are no pathways from the development site to these areas. Significant effects cannot be ruled out to the Boyne Coast and Estuary SAC The conservation objective set for mudflats and estuary in this SAC are similar and are described as “Permanent habitat area stable or increasing; estuarine muds dominated by polychaetes and crustaceans community complex maintained in a natural condition.”. Given the potential effects to water quality during construction (particularly sediment and other construction pollution) significant effects to these qualifying interests cannot be ruled out. It is therefore concluded that a Stage 2 AA will be required. To assist in this decision, a separate Natura Impact Statement (NIS) has been submitted to An Bord Pleanála.
