Having regard to the provisions of the South Dublin County Council Development Plan 2022-2028, the overall layout and design of the development as currently proposed is poor and fails to make the most of the existing green infrastructure and the ecosystem services it provides, as well as the amenity potential of the site. More particularly, the open space layout and the siting of existing green infrastructure within private rear gardens, loss of green infrastructure, failure to meet the Green Space Factor score, inadequate provision of nature-based SUDS amount to a poor layout and design. As such, the proposals are contrary to the provisions of Policy GI1 Green Infrastructure Overarching, Policy GI2 Biodiversity, Policy GI3 Sustainable Water Management, as well as contrary to GI1 Objective 4, GI2 Objectives 1, 2 and 4 and GI4 Objective 1 of the South Dublin County Development Plan 2022-2028 and would therefore be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area and if permitted would set an undesirable precedent for similar unsatisfactory development.

(a) The proposed development has not been shown to have been designed with due regard to the adjoining Annex 1 woodlands and would materially contravene Policy NCBH5 and Policy GI7 Specific Local Objective 2 of the South Dublin County Development Plan 2022 - 2028, which is an objective for the conservation and preservation of an Annex I natural habitat on a site prescribed in the County Development Plan. The applicant has also failed to show compliance with Policy GI7 Objective 3 of the County Development Plan.The applicant has failed to demonstrate – due to lack of appropriate surveys and assessment – that the development would not have an adverse effect on that area and habitat. The scheme as currently proposed would not accord with the proper planning and sustainable development of the area and cannot be favourably considered by the Planning Authority. (b) The planning authority does not concur with the conclusion of the applicant’s Natura Impact Statement, that the development will have will have no significant adverse effects on the QIs, SCIs and on the integrity and extent of … European sites., due to apparent omissions in the Statement, relating to the Woodlands which are the subject of part (a). The hydrological connection between the subject site and European sites in Dublin Bay runs through the woodlands and then the Camac and Liffey Rivers, and this connection is the basis on which the applicant determined that a Stage 2 Appropriate Assessment was required (this was also the result of the SDCC screening determination). The submitted Natura Impact Statement does not envisage or assess local impact to the Woodland habitat as contributing to the risk of significant likely effects downstream. It is the Planning Authority’s view that potential impacts relating to ecological damage to the woodlands are as likely as impacts arising directly from construction and operation phase activities on the site. As such, and considering that no exceptional circumstances arise under Article 6(4) of the Habitats Directive, the planning authority has not been able to ascertain that the development would not adversely affect the integrity of any European site, and to grant permission would therefore be in contravention of Policy NCBH3 ‘Natura 2000 Sites’ of the South Dublin County Development Plan 2022 – 2028, and Objective 3 of that policy (being an objective for the conservation and preservation of a European site) and would not accord with the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || In relation ecological impacts on the subject development site, the submitted EcIA is incomplete and does not include the results of the following: breeding bird and bat activity surveys of the development site, and bat emergence surveys of the buildings on the development site. Having regard to the requirements of the Rathcoole Local Area Plan (April 2002) and Policy 2.2.2 regarding the high quality of design and layout in new residential development, as set out in the South Dublin County Development Plan 1998, it is considered that the site layout, quality and location of the open space in relation to the dwelling units, parking arrangements, inconsistencies with the linkage pattern of the Action Area Plan and monotonous building design and inadequate mix of unit types in the proposed development would be contrary to the standards of the South Dublin County Development Plan 1998 and Rathcoole local Area Plan 2002 required to achieve the zoning objective of this new residential area. The proposed development would constitute a material contravention of the zoning objective, would materially contravene objectives (particularly those in Sections 7.2.1, 7.3.2 and 7.8) of the Rathcoole Local Area Plan 2002) and would be inconsistent with the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The reservation line for the Stoney Road Improvement is incorrectly shown on the lodged plans. The creation of a new access to Main Street (entry point no.3 on drawing 01-008-01) would lead to a multiplicity of accesses to a very busy street where vision splays would be impaired by the dedicated car parking spaces on the street. The proposed access point would thereby endanger public safety by reason of a traffic hazard and would be contrary to the proper planning and development of the area. The density of the proposed development would be excessive and would be contrary to the recommendations of the Residential Density Guidelines for Planning Authorities and the provisions of the South Dublin County Development Plan, 1998, and would therefore be contrary to the proper planning and development of the area. || The proposed development would be out of character with the area by reason of its' height, design, materials, scale and massing and would be visually obtrusive on this site close to the centre of the village of Rathcoole. The proposed development would be seriously injurious to the visual amenities of the area and be contrary to the proper planning and development of the area. || The proposed location of the rear elevation of apartment block 'B', containing fenestration to habitable rooms, within 5 - 6.5 metres of the rear gardens of residential properties would excessively intrude on and invade the privacy of the said properties. The proposed development would therefore seriously injure the amenities and depreciate the value of property in the vicinity. || The proposed development would, by reason of lack of adequate usable open space and the poor disposition of the open space provided constitute a sub-standard form of development and would therefore be contrary to the proper planning and development of the area. || Having regard to the provisions of the South Dublin County Development Plan, 1998, in relation to the area, it is considered that a development of the scale proposed without an adequate mix of residential unit types, when combined with the existing, permitted and proposed developments in Rathcoole Village, would be excessive in size. As such the proposed development would endanger public safety by reason of traffic hazard.

The application form, site notice and newspaper notices submitted with the application are considered misleading and incomplete, as the description given did not refer to the proposed development being within the curtilage of Protected Structures. || The proposed development, by virtue of its scale and bulk, would be visually obtrusive and inconsistent with the character and appearance of Whitechurch Cottages, which are Protected Structures. || The existing public sewer to which the applicant is proposing to connect the foul drainage from this development does not have the capacity to cater for the proposed development. The proposed development is premature pending the adoption of the Local Area Plan for A1 zoned lands at Rathcoole, including the application site. || The proposed access to the site via an existing laneway that is substandard in width and construction, has no footpaths, drainage or public lighting, and forms an unsafe junction with the Kilteel Road, would endanger public safety by reason of traffic hazard. || Council standards require a minimum setback of 30m between residential units and boundary fence of the Naas Road but site layout plan shows only a 20m setback. || The proposed layout of the development is unacceptable because of its proximity to the existing public 225mm diameter foul sewer in the adjoining field. It is a requirement of the Environmental Services Department that no buildings be located within 5m of a public foul sewer of this size. The proposed development would therefore be prejudicial to public health. || The proposed development is premature pending the implementation of the recommendations of the consultant's report into the existing foul sewer network in Saggart, and pending the implementation of the Boherboy Water Supply Scheme. The proposed development would therefore be prejudicial to public health. || Insufficient details have been submitted to show how the applicant proposes to deal with the surface water run-off from the development. The proposed development would therefore be prejudicial to public health. || The public notices submitted do not refer to demolition of the bungalow, a habitable dwelling , as required in accordance with the relevant sections of the Local Government (Planning and Development ) Regulations, 1994, and the application is therefore deficient in this regard. || Inadequate separation distance has been provided from the adjoining site to the east to ensure satisfactory residential amenity for the proposed development and potential future development on the adjoining site.

The proposed development, by virtue of its excessive density and its height, and the inadequate parking provision proposed, would result in a cramped form of development which would be out of character with the pattern of development in the area. Therefore, the proposed development would provide inadequate residential amenity for the prospective occupants and would seriously injure the amenities of property in the vicinity. || The application did not contain a statement as to how the proposal would comply with the Housing Strategy of South Dublin County Council, prepared in accordance with Part V of the Planning and Development Act 2000, as referred to in Section 2.2.7(ii), and as set out in Appendix F of the South Dublin County Development Plan, 1998. As such, the proposed development would be contrary to an objective of the Development Plan. || No information was supplied in relation to drainage arrangements or water supply. As such, the proposed development must be considered prejudicial to public health. As such, the application does not comply with Article 23 of the 1994 Local Government (Planning and Development) Regulations. || The proposed development, by virtue of its inadequate car parking provision, would result in on-street parking which would endanger public safety, by reason of obstruction of road users.

The site is located in an area zoned 'A' in the Dublin County Development Plan 1993 where it is a stated objective 'to protect and/or improve residential amenity'. The development as proposed would result in a density of development which is well in excess of the density of existing development in the vicinity of the site. The proposal does not provide for adequate levels of open space provision or off street car parking as required by the Development Plan. The proposed development would materially contravene the zoning objective for the area and would thereby seriously injure the amenity of property in the vicinity of the site and depreciate the value of property in the vicinity. || The applicant has not provided adequate off street car parking facilities. The limited size of the site combined with the restrictions imposed by the site conditions e.g. the location of stream and river, the substandard provision of car parking facilities and the location of the access to the site at a bend on a busy distributor road means that the proposed development would endanger public safety by reason of a traffic hazard. The applicant has provided for 1 car park per unit. The Planning Authority consider that 2 spaces per units should be provided at this location. || The applicant has submitted insufficient information with regard to the proposed foul and surface water drainage arrangements. The proposed development would be contrary to the proper planning and development of the area. A private pumped system serving more that one unit is unacceptable to the Environmental Services Engineer. || The proposal does not make adequate private/public open space provision. || The proposed 4 storey development is incompatible with the scale of development in the vicinity and would be seriously injurious to the amenity value and property value of developments in the vicinity.

The proposed development would represent poor standard piecemeal development on a single site within a substantial area of land zoned for development between Main Street, Rathcoole, and the Naas Road and, as such, would be contrary to the proper planning and development of the village. The area requires a comprehensive approach that would identify suitable, limited number, of accesses off Main Street and that would generate development that would contribute positively to the development of the village and protect the amenities of existing properties. || Development of the kind proposed on the land would be premature by reference to the existing deficiency in the capacity of the foul sewerage system serving Rathcoole and the period with in which this constraint can reasonably be expected to cease. There is insufficient capacity for any additional hydraulic loading in the local sewage treatment works. || The proposed development would seriously injure the amenities of residential property in the vicinity through excessive overlooking from Block B of the adjacent bungalow to the west. || The proposed public open space within the development is not properly distributed for the benefit of future residents. || The proposed development would tend to create serious traffic congestion in the village due to a serious deficiency in the provision of on site parking spaces. || The proposed development does not provide for proper integration with the recently installed traffic calming measures and street tree planting on Main Street. The entrance layout appears to provide for the removal of a tree on the street in front of the site and this would be contrary to the proper planning and development of the area. || The application as submitted is inadequate in the following respects: (i) The newspaper and site notices do not refer to the proposed demolition of two habitable houses; (ii) The scale of the site plan is incorrectly stated; (iii) No details have been submitted in relation to surface water drainage or water supply; (iv) No provision has been made for proper secure bicycle storage or fuel storage in the development.

The development of the kind proposed, by reason of excessive scale, bulk and physical dominance and by reason of overlooking and overshadowing would be seriously injurious to the amenities of the future residents of the proposed and permitted development and would materially contravene the zoning objective for the area which is 'to protect and/or improve residential amenity'. The proposed development would therefore be contrary to the proper planning and development of the area. || The proposed development by reason of its excessive scale and density would seriously alter the established character of development in this suburban area in a manner which would be seriously injurious to the amenities of and depreciate the value of property in the vicinity. || The proposed development would be substandard by reason of inadequate provision for open space which is functional and accessible to the future residents of the proposed and permitted developments on the subject site and which is not overshadowed. The proposed development would therefore be contrary to the proper planning and development of the area. || The proposed development has made no provision for refuse bins, fuel storage, clothes drying and cycle storage, facilities which are considered fundamental to the basic amenities of the development. The proposed development would therefore contravene the provisions of the Development Plan in this regard as set out in section 3.4.17 of the written statement and would be contrary to the proper planning and development of the area. || The proposed development would be contrary to the Draft Guidelines for Planning Authorities on Residential Density (PD 4/98) as the high density proposed would be achieved at an unacceptable amenity cost to the future residents of the proposed development. The proposed development would therefore be contrary to the proper planning and development of the area. || The proposed development would set an undesirable precedent for further similar developments in the area. The proposed development would therefore be contrary to the proper planning and development of the area.

The proposed development which would incorporate a substantial two storey extension, by reason of its scale, location and additional volume of building proposed, would result in overdevelopment of the site and an unacceptable level of overlooking of adjacent properties and would thereby seriously injure the amenities and depreciate the value of property in the vicinity. The proposal would thus be contrary to the proper planning and development of the area. || The proposed development which would incorporate a substantial two storey extension, by reason of its scale, bulk and design, would be unduly overbearing and out of character with adjacent buildings and the existing pattern of development in the vicinity. The proposed extension which would extend beyond the established building line of the adjacent properties, would represent a serious intrusion on the character of the area and would seriously injure the amenities of these properties and would be visually obtrusive when viewed therefrom. Accordingly, the proposed development would be contrary to the provisions of the South Dublin County Development Plan, 1998, and the proper planning and development of the area. || The proposed development, by reason of inadequate internal floor areas and room dimensions as well as the design of the proposed apartments, would constitute substandard development. The proposed development would therefore be contrary to the provisions of the South County Development Plan, 1998, and the proper planning and development of the area. || The proposed development would, by reason of inadequate provision of private amenity open space, constitute a substandard development and would contravene the objectives of the South Dublin County Development Plan, 1998, in regard to apartment developments. The proposed development would therefore be contrary to the proper planning and development of the area. || The proposed development, owing to the location of car parking spaces on the public footpath verge and the lack of adequate and appropriate on-site parking provision, would impede vision at a junction and would thereby endanger public safety by reason of a traffic hazard/obstruction of road users and would impede the movement of pedestrians. The proposed development would therefore contravene the objectives of the South Dublin County Development Plan, 1998, in relation to parking and would thus be contrary to the proper planning and development of the area.

The proposed development would result in piecemeal and poorly co-ordinated backland development and would be premature pending the adoption of an appropriate action plan for the area. It would therefore, be contrary to the proper planning and development of the area. || The site of the proposed development is likely to be reuqired by the South Dublin County Council to facilitate the improvement of local centre facilities and the enhancement of the environment at Templeogue Village. The proposed development would therefore be contrary to the proper planning and development of the area.

Development of the kind proposed on the land would be premature by reference to an existing deficiency in the public foul sewerage facilities in the area. || The provision of percolation areas in public open space areas is unacceptable to the Planning Authority. The development as proposed would be prejudicial to public health. || The open space provision is of a type which will not be taken in charge by the Local Authority due to the high maintenance requirements. A grant of planning permission for the development as proposed would be contrary to the proper planning and development of the area. || It is considered that the layout and design of the proposed development does make full use of the site area available. This is especially so in respect of the large area of land which has been dedicated as private rear garden areas especially at the north western end of the site. The development is considered to be contrary to the provisions of the South Dublin County Development Plan 1998 in respect of the sustainable development of the area and is considered to be contrary to the proper planning and development of the area. || The proposed development does not meet the requirements of the Development Plan in respect of the provision of off street car parking and does not meet the requirements of the Planning Authority in respect of the provision of vision splays. The development would be contrary to the provisions of the Development Plan and would endanger public safety by way of traffic hazard. || The proposed development would not accord with Specific Local Objective 36 of the South Dublin County Development Plan which requires that any development in Kingswood Village be structurally and aesthetically to the highest standard. || Insufficient details are submitted in respect of the filter based treatment plant and percolation tests. As such the proposed development must be considered prejudicial to public health.

The proposed development would result in a substantial impact on the views/setting of Primrose Hill and its associated gardens, and as such would materially affect a protected structure which would be contrary to the proper planning and development of the area. || The details submitted are not considered adequate to facilitate a proper assessment of the proposal, in particular the impact of the development on the western boundary of the site; the implications for the stability of the lands to the west, which includes a Protected Structure;; RPS Ref. 2/061 Primrose Hill. and the absence of a detailed level survey which includes levels on adjoining sites. In the absence of such information, and the fact that the applicant is unable to guarantee the stability of the protected structure and the land lying within the curtilage of that structure, the proposed development would seriously injure the amenties and depreciate the value of property in the vicinity.. || Having regard to the deficiency in off-street car parking provision within the proposed development, it is considered that the proposal would result in the over-development of the site and would materially contravene a development objective of the South Dublin County Development Plan, 1998, with regard to car parking provision and would be seriously injurious to the amenities of both the proposed apartments and other property in the vicinity.

The proposed development would tend to create serious traffic congestion by creating a new traffic light controlled junction in close proximity to the existing roundabout. The desirable junction spacing on District Distributor Routes is 800 metres whereas the proposed junction is just 280 metres from the roundabout to the north. The Fonthill Road is on an embankment here and a major junction is unacceptable. Thus the proposed development would be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || Fonthill Road is a District Distributor route and is a major North/South route connecting the National Primary N4 to the N7 at Newlands Cross. When it was constructed a few years ago a roundabout was provided at the junction with the Newlands Road (i.e. on Fonthill road at Ronanstown). This roundabout would also facilitate the development of the subject lands as an East West distributor road is planned which will join the roundabout to the proposed outer ring road to the west. This is considered the way to develop this site and the applicant should negotiate an access to the Fonthill Road via the proposed East West distributor. Thus the proposed development would be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || A railway station with the main plaza constructed over the motorway reservation is shown. No indication of any agreement with Iarnrod Eireann has been submitted. Office buildings are also proposed over the motorway reservation as well as a link bridge. The Roads Department would not be in favour of permitting construction over the motorway reservation, of the station/plaza or the office buildings. The location of the station also may not be the optimum one as access for buses would be difficult. The Roads Department would require that buses should be able to access the station easily from the surrounding road network. Thus the proposed development would be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The carparking layout provides for approximately 2,300 spaces which is approximately 50% of the 1998 South Dublin County Development Plan requirement. However the provision of car parking at a rate of 1 per 125 sq. metres of offices is not acceptable particularly as the public transport infrastructure serving the site will not be in place if the proposed development proceeds. Thus the proposed development, due to a significant shortfall in car parking provision would be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || Development of the kind proposed would be premature pending the determination by the planning authority or the road authority of a road layout for the area or any part thereof (namely, the Motorway reservation and road linkages to surrounding sites). || The applicant/developer is not in a position to gain access to the site from the Fonthill road as land between the site and the road is not in his ownership. Thus the proposed development would be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || In view of the large scale of the development proposed, the podium form adopted throughout most of the project is an inappropriate urban model for this site. The form chosen is inconsistent with the development of a sustainable town- centre in an outer-urban location and will result in serious overdevelopment of a limited site. Thus the proposal would be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The residential amenity of the apartment blocks proposed would be seriously compromised by the overall layout submitted. Thus the proposed development would seriously injure the amenities of property in the vicinity. || The vehicular circulation system proposed, at the entrance to and within the site, has not been properly integrated into the urban design of the proposed centre and will result in congestion and lack of amenity. Thus the proposed development would seriously injure the amenities of property in the vicinity and be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The proposed development would be premature pending: · adoption by South Dublin County Council, of the Retail Planning Strategy for the Greater Dublin Area 2002 · an integrated plan for the area, given the scale and extent of development proposed · exact locations of the metro and rail station and interchanges with Quality Bus Corridors · availability of the report on the Integrated Framework Plan for Land Use and Transportation (not available until c.September 2002) and would therefore be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area.

The height and bulk of the proposed development to the adjoining property would lead to a loss of daylight, privacy and overlooking. It is therefore contrary to policies in the South County Dublin Development Plan 1998 regarding design of new developments and the protection of existing character, enhancement of amenity and would this seriously injure the residential amenity of property in the vicinity.. || The visibility splay on the left hand side when exiting the junction of Convent Lane/Grange Road and the width of the lane is severely substandard therefore the generation of additional traffic/turning movements at this location would endanger public safety by reason of a traffic hazard. || The proposed development, by virtue of its location within metres of a 75mm and 100mm diameter public watermain would be prejudicial to public health. || By virtue of its height and site coverage, the proposed development constitutes over development and would thus materially contravene the achievement of the zoning objective for residential amenity which is considered reasonable. The proposed development would therefore be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The proposed development does not comply with minimum standards of internal spaces, open space provision and car parking referenced in the Residential Density Guidelines and the South Dublin County Development Plan 1998. Therefore it is considered that the proposed development would not provide a satisfactory level of residential amenity.

The proposed development is situated within an area zoned A1 in the South Dublin County Development Plan 1998, the objective of which is 'To provide for new residential communities in accordance with approved Action Area Plans'. No Action Area Plan for Newcastle has yet been adopted. The proposed development is therefore premature pending adoption of the Action Area Plan. || The proposed development by reason of its design and lack of permeability within the scheme would be detrimental to the development potential of adjoining lands to the west and south which are zoned A1 and as such would contravene materially a development objective indicated in the development plan for the zoning of land for residential use to provide for new residential communities in accordance with Action Area Plans and would therefore be contrary to the proper planning and development of the area. || Public open space has been provided at a rate of 12% (09ha). The South Dublin County Development Plan Plan 1998 (as set out in paragraph 3.4.14.ii) requires a minimum of 14% within A1 zoned areas. The purpose of this allocation is to provide small open spaces within an estate and to form large neighbourhood parks to serve the wider community. Therefore where appropriate, 65% of the allocated open space should be located in a position where it can be amalgamated with similar portions from adjoining developments. If such amalgamation can not be achieved, then an alternative allocation of land in the vicinity may be accepted in lieu of the required open space. The proposal would, with regard to the provision of public open space within A1 areas, contravene this requirement of the Development Plan. || The proposed development by reason of inadequate parking provision would be contrary to the proper planning and development of the area. || The proposed development by reason of excessive overlooking of adjoining lands would result in a negative impact on development potential and any future residential amenity of the adjoining lands. || The proposed development would seriously injure the amenities and depreciate the value of property in the vicinity.

The proposed development by virtue of its density, inadequate separation distance from side and rear boundaries, the public/private open space arrangement, inadequate private open space, the visual intrusion of the proposed parking upon the streetscape of Oldcourt Road and the piecemeal development of this area would materially contravene the zoning objective "A" for the area in accordance with the South County Dublin Development Plan 1998 and the Guidelines for Planning Authorities on "Residential Density" 1999.

The density of the proposed development is excessive due to the restricted nature and size of this elongated site. Also the proximity of the adjoining groups of dwellings would present an overcrowded and disorderly appearance. The proposed development would set an undesirable precedent for similar development and would seriously injure the amenities and depreciate the value of property in the vicinity. || The proposed development by reason of its design, would be out of character with the existing pattern of development in the area and would thereby seriously injure the amenities and depreciate the value of property in the vicinity. || The proposed development does not provide adequate private amenity open space for all the units, nor does it provide adequate public/communal open space. The proposed development is thereby contrary to the provisions of the South Dublin County Development Plan 1998 Development Plan and accordingly would be contrary to the proper planning and development of the area and would seriously injure the amenities and depreciate the value of property in the vicinity. || The proposed development by reason of inadequate separation distance, overlooking , and overshadowing would seriously injure the amenities and depreciate the value of property in the vicinity. || The proposed development which is located with a conservation area would have a negative impact on the existing amenities, character and heritage of the area and as such would be contrary to the provisions of paragraph 2.7.2.i of the South Dublin County Development Plan 1998.

The generation of significant additional turning movements on the National Secondary Route (N81) at the junction where there is a break in the median would endanger public safety by reason of traffic hazard or obstruction of road users or otherwise. || The proposed development is excessive in its scale and extent and would result in the site being developed in a manner that is inconsistent with the high amenity character of the lands, having regard to the specific local objective providing for limited residential development at this location. || It is considered having regard to the existing pattern of development in the area, which is characterised by semi-detached/ detached dwellings that the proposed development would constitute overdevelopment of this site and would seriously injure the amenities of and depreciate the value of property in the vicinity. The proposed development would, therefore be contrary to the proper planning and development of the area.

The subject site of the proposed development is required for the M50 Up-Grade. Development of the kind proposed would be premature pending the determination by the Planning Authority or Road Authority of a road layout for the area or any part thereof. || The proposed development would be under a public road. || The current application requires an extra 40 no. car spaces for the proposed increase in the number of apartments. The cumulative requirement for the site is now 258 spaces against a provision of 181 spaces only (70% of the total requirement). This is not acceptable. It is considered that the provision of extra units without a corresponding parking provision would lead to on street parking which would endanger public safety by reason of traffic hazard and obstruction of road users.

The height, scale and design (reminescent of an urban Georgian architectural style) does not take account of the low density character of the open space zoning objective. Therefore the proposed development would contrarty to the zoning objective and inconsistent with the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The proposed site is located within an area zoned 'Objective GB' which seeks to 'preserve a Green Belt between development areas'. Having regard to the zoning objective for the area, existing development on the green belt lands, together with that permitted but not yet constructed,it is considered that any further development on this site would materially contravene the zoning objective for the area and would be inconsistent with the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The proposed development if permitted would lead to an intensification of use of the proposed access point onto a District Distributor road, which forms part of the strategic roads network. The proposed development would reduce the safety and capacity of this route and would endanger public safety by reason of traffic hazard. || The applicants have not submitted a tree survey of the site nor have they made any provision for public/private/communal open space in association with the residential use of the building. This is considered unacceptable and inconsistent with the proper planning and sustainable development.

The proposed site is located within an area zoned 'Objective F' which seeks to 'preserve and provide for open space and recreational amenities'. The proposed development is of a significant scale on the undeveloped Naas Road boundary of the overall site and would significantly compromise the open aspect of this area. Taking into consideration the zoning objective for the area, existing hotel/aparthotel development on the lands and further developments permitted on the lands but not yet constructed, it is considered that the proposed development would contravene materially a development objective indicated in the Development Plan for the zoning of land for the use solely or primarily of particular areas for particular purposes and would be inconsistent with the proper planning and sustainable development of the area.

The development as proposed is considered excessive in residential density. A grant of permission in this instance would be contrary to ministerial guidelines on residential density as issued by the Dept of Environment and Local Government (1999), and therefore contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The proposal, because of its internal design is considered unacceptable in regard to internal amenity . A grant of permission in this instance would therefore set an undesirable precedent for other similar forms of development in the area. || The height and density of the proposed development on an infill site in a predominantly 2 storey semi detached area of residential development would be seriously injurious to the residential amenity and depreciate the value of property in the vicinity and would therefore be contrary to the zoning objective. It is considered that the proposal would be inconsistent with the proper planning and sustainable development of the area.

Development of the kind proposed on the land would be premature due to an existing deficiency in the provision of water supplies and sewerage facilities. Development of this kind is premature pending the completion of Saggart/ Rathcoole & Newcastle Drainage Collection Improvement Scheme, and the completion of the Lucan/Palmerstown and the Boherboy Water Supply Schemes. || The proposed development would endanger public safety by reason of traffic hazard as a result of additional traffic/turning movements on the heavily trafficked regional route (R405), and the generation of pedestrian/cycle trips by the development on the heavily trafficked regional route which is very narrow in places particularly at the canal and railway bridges and which has no facilities for pedestrians or cyclists || Development of the kind proposed would be premature pending the determination by the Planning Authority or the road authority of a road layout for the area or any part thereof. || The layout as proposed does not provide adequate passive supervision of the proposed private gated gardens and as such would be detrimental to the residential amenity of those occupying the adjacent units.

The site of the proposed development is located on an elevated site where the zoning objective as set out in the current development plan for the area is 'to protect and/or improve residential amenity'. It is considered that the proposed development due to its mass, scale, density, and location would be injurious to the visual amenities of the area and visually incongruous with existing development in the vicinity. Therefore, the proposed development would seriously injure the amenities and depreciate the value of property in the vicinity. || The proposed development would constitute overdevelopment of a restricted site. Together with a lack of variety in the type of residential unit proposed, this overdevelopment would set an undesirable precedent for similar development in the area and would seriously injure the amenities and depreciate the value of property in the vicinity. || The proposed development would pose a serious threat to a stand of mature trees in the adjoining public open space. The South Dublin County Development Plan 1998 contains an objective to preserve trees and woodlands in this public open space. The loss of those trees would be harmful to the appearance of the locality and as such the development would seriously injure the amenities and depreciate the value of property in the vicinity.

The proposed arrangement of 7 No. detached houses fails to comply with Development Plan Standards regarding private open space, rear garden depth, and provision of on site parking. It is considered that the site area of 0.3ha is significantly below the recommended standard in the Residential Density Guidelines (DOE 1999) of 0.5ha and therefore cannot determine a higher density in a location remote from public transport. Therefore it is considered that the proposed development would materially contravene ministerial guidelines and would be contrary to proper planning and sustaniable development. || The location of an entrance to site has failed to provide adequate vision splays and would endanger public safety by reason of a traffic hazard.

Having regard to the area of the site, which is less than 0.5ha and its location in a relatively low density area of detached and semi-detached houses,( being flanked to the east by a single storey building), it is considered that the density and height of the building is excessive and would be inconsistent with standards of the Residential Density Guidelines (DOE) and guidelines as set out in the South Dublin County Development Plan (1998). Therefore, the proposed development would materially contravene the zoning objective which is ' to protect and provide for residential amenity and would be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The applicant has failed to provide a full archaeological assessment of the site,in the context of it's identification as a recorded monument which has Ecclesiastical Remains under Ref. A grant of planning permission would therefore be contrary to the proper planning and development of the area.

No. 323). The proposed development would give rise to an unacceptable loss of historic fabric and would contravene the terms of the County Development Plan, 2004-2010, in relation to the conservation of protected structures, (section 8.3 refers). decision: REFUSE EXT. OF DURATION OF PERMISSION
reasons_joined: Section 42 (a) (ii) (iv) states that the authority shall be satisfied that - ‘where the development has not commenced, that an environmental impact assessment, or an appropriate assessment, or both of those assessments, if required, was or were carried out before the permission was granted.’ Having regard to the following: • An Appropriate Assessment was not carried out prior to permission being granted for the development. • The applicant has failed to demonstrate that an Appropriate Assessment was not required for the development. It is considered that the development on the subject site requires an Appropriate Assessment, in this instance. It is considered that the application fails to fully comply with Section 42 of the Planning and Development Act 2000 to 2010. Note to Applicant: This decision, pursuant to Section 42 of the Planning and Development Act 2000 (as amended), refers only to the extension of duration of the planning application. The decision to refuse an extension of duration will have no consequences for the assessment of a future application for permission under Section 34 of the Act and should not be interpreted as a negative disposition towards a future application for a dwelling on the site.

The proposed development would be prejudicial to public health and safety due to its close proximity to the Poddle River and would be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The proposed development would materially contravene policies and objectives of the South Dublin County Council Development Plan 2004-2010 as indicated in Section 11.7.ii of the Plan as the proposed residential density would be equivalent to circa. 124 per hectare (49 per acre) - when the average net residential density normally permitted in this area is in the range of between 35-50 dwellings per hectare (14-20 per acre net). The proposed development would therefore be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || Having regard to the pattern of development in the area and the restricted size of the site, in close proximity to surrounding properties, the development would by reason of it's scale, siting, size, and design, be seriously injurous to the amenities and depreciate the value of property in the vicinity. || Having regard to the layout, height and scale of the proposed development and the size of the site in an infill location, the development would represent overdevelopment of the site, would result in overlooking, overshadowing and have an overbearing effect between both the proposed apartment blocks and surrounding properties, would be seriously out of character with development in the area, and would be visually obtrusive when viewed in the streetscape. The proposed development would, therefore materially contravene the Development Plan zoning objective for the area which is to 'protect and/ or improve residential amenity', and as such would be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The proposed development would set an undesirable precedent for further similar developments, which would in themselves and cumulatively be harmful to the residential amenities of the area and be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area.

It is considered that the bulk and overall size of the proposed development would have a negative impact on existing properties in the vicinity through loss of light and amenity. The proposed development would seriously injure the amenities and depreciate the value of property in the vicinity. || The use of balconies as open space areas which are less than 22m from opposing windows would result in overlooking and a consequential loss of privacy of neighbouring properties. The proposed development would seriously injure the amenities and depreciate the value of property in the vicinity. || The proposed development of a block of 12 apartments on a site of 1714 sq.m. would result in a density of 69.9 units to the hectare, which would be out of significantly out of character with the existing pattern of development in the area. It is considered that the proposed development would be contrary to Section 3.3.1 Infill Residential Development of the Residential Density Guidelines for Planning Authorities. || The proposed development would set an undesirable precedent for other similar developments, which would in themselves and cumulatively be harmful to the residential amenities of the area and be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area.

Having regard to the 'A1' zoning objective for the site, "to provide for new Residential Communities in accordance with Approved Area Plans", which is considered reasonable, the proposed development of 180 no. dwellings is considered to be premature pending the preparation and approval of an area plan for these lands. Therefore the proposal materially contravenes the zoning objective for these lands. The proposed development would therefore, be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area and would set an undesirable precedent for the development of other 'A1' zoned lands in the County. || In overall design terms, the proposed residential layout is considered contrary to the key design principles set out in Section 11 of the 2004-2010 County Development Plan. The scheme lacks interconnectivity and permeability, key frontage and a legible block pattern and there are excessive incidences of blank gable and flank walls along internal roadways and siding open spaces. The proposed open space provision is poorly distributed and non-integrated, there is a lack of incidental (kick about) areas with overhead lines and cables traversing open areas. It is considered that the overhead lines and cables traversing the open space would seriously injure the amenity of these open areas and of properties in the vicinity. The proposed development would contravene the design standards set out in Section 11 of the County Development Plan and would represent a substandard form of residential development. The proposed would therefore be contrary to the proper planning and development of the area. || Having regard to the absence of an approved Area Plan or Design Framework for this area, it is considered that the proposed 4-5 storey residential blocks by reason of their scale and mass would be inconsistent with the established pattern of development at this location and unduly prominent at this outer suburban location. The development would contravene terms of the South Dublin County Development Plan in relation to building heights (S11.11.3 refers) and set an undesirable future precedent, which would seriously injure the amenity of the area. The proposed development would therefore be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The proposed provision of childcare facilities within an adjoining commercial development is unacceptable. The proposed development would contravene the terms of the 'Childcare Facilities, Guidelines for Planning Authorities' issued to planning authorities under Section 28 of the Planning and Development Act 2000 and incorporated into the South Dublin County Development Plan 2004-2010. Therefore it is considered that the proposed development would be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || Proposed residential blocks fail to maintain the required safety clearance from ESB transmissions lines of 23 metres from the centre line. The proposed development would therefore endanger the health and safety of persons occupying the proposed residential blocks within the safety clearance area.

The junction design as shown is not implementable and is hazardous. A number of attempts have been made to provide an acceptable junction design without success. The submitted junction design is seriously deficient and would endanger public safety by reason of a traffic hazard and is therefore contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area.

Having regard to the number of existing trees and hedgerows to be lost to development and the difficulty of protecting even those trees proposed for retention in the context of such a high degree of proposed excavation, the proposal would be contrary to the objective in the South Dublin County Development 2004- 2010 to protect and preserve trees and woodland on the site. The proposed centrally located area of public open space would be a minimum of 4m above the ground level of adjoining roads and the layout as such would be unuseable, would form a barrier between the east and west of the site, and would contravene objective 5.2.4 of the Ballycullen-Oldcourt Action Area Plan which states that 'new residential layouts should incorporate all natural features worthy of retention as detailed in section 3, including, trees, hedges, sterams and boundary features. Culverting of watercourses should be avoided'. The proposed development would therefore be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || Notwithstanding the A1 zoning of the site and having regard to the elevated and exposed nature of the site and to the development already permitted in the vicinity, it is considered that the proposed development by reason of the scale, height and massing would be unduly obtrusive on this part of the urban fringe. The proposed development would also contravene Objective 5.10 of the Ballycullen Oldcourt Action Area Plan (2000) which states that 'Building heights should be no greater than two storeys, except where it can be clearly demonstrated that it would not impinge on the 120 metre contour, or be unduly obtrusive on this portion of the urban fringe". Therefore, the proposed dvelopment would materially contravene the zoning objective for the area which is 'to provide for new residential communities in accordance with approved Action Area Plans" and would be contrary to the proper planning and development of the area. || It is considered that the proposed development which involves considerable excavation of the site to level the hillside into a platform punctuated by spines of open space areas which will be at a significantly higher level bears little regard to the existing contours and landforms of the site and fails to have regard to Specific Local Objective 110 of the South Dublin County Development Plan 2004 - 2010 by not having due regard to the high amenity value and close proximity of the Dublin Mountains. || Having regard to the 'Residential Density Guidelines' it is considered that the proposed development by reason of its design and layout including provision of public open space, rear separation distances between units, provision of car parking, provision of bin storage areas, level differences between front and rear areas, and provision of blank walls, would provide a substandard level of residential amenity for future residents and would seriously injure the residential amenity of property in the vicinity. The proposed development would therefore be contrary to the proper planning and development of the area.

The quantity and quality of Open Space provision and community infrastructure including play areas is substandard and would not comply with the requirements set out in S11.9 and Section 11.10 of the 2004-2010 County Development Plan. Open space should form an integral part of the residential layout and should be well defined and integrated within the scheme (No development to include underground services, are permitted within the clearance of the E.S.B overhead and the rear gardens of the residential units to the south of the site are encroaching onto the River Walk Park). A hierarchy of open space, providing an aesthetic and recreational function including childrens playground allowing for pedestrian permeability throughout the scheme is required. The public open space provision materially contravenes the objectives of the County Development Plan, and would therefore be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The proposed development excludes the Proctor's Cottage to which Specific Local objective 101 applies, whereby it is proposed to facilitate the development of the cottage as a tourist facility featuring industrial heritage and to include live-in accommodation for a manager and that this be carried out in consultation with Saggart Arts & Heritage Group. In a previous application by the same applicnt this site is shown within the applicnts ownership. To exclude this element is not in accordance with the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The separation between windows and balconies at upper levels are susbstandard in some instances and would not meet the 22 metre seperation standard set out in Section 11.11.5 of the County Development Plan. In addition, the configuration of rear gardens in duplex units would result in direct overlooking from first floor windows and balconies of adjoining properties and would if permitted be injurious to residential amenity and would therefore be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. NOTE: Any future application on this site must address any cumulative deficits in terms of community infrastructure - ie: schools, creche, public open space, playground, arising from the development of phases 1 and 2 of the 'Millrace' housing development. || The current proposal is the final phase in the development of these lands (under Phase 1, 325 housing units were permitted and under Phase 2, 144 housing units are currently under-consideration). A site has been reserved for a primary school on lands of the subject application (the need for at least an eight-classroom has been identified, as the existing National School is at capacity and occupies a constrained site with no scope for expansion). It is Council policy to develop community facilities in tandem with housing and the applicant is proposing housing on the reserved school site. The proposal therefore materially contravenes objective 5.6.2 of the Saggart Local Area Plan 2000 and the provisions of the South Dublin County Council Development Plan 2004-2010 (the reserved school site is identified on Map 21), and would therefore be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area.

The massing and scale of the proposal for a mixed use development on a key site fronting the Main Street within the village of Saggart subject to Specific Local Objective 98 regarding the possible designation of Saggart as an Architectural Conservation Area, is considered to be premature and may be contrary to recommendations in a future feasibility study. || Having considered the shadow analysis submitted in response to a request for further information it is considered that the rear gardens of units 1-8 and the habitable 1st level rooms would be negatively impacted upon and this would present a substandard level of amenity for intended occupants. In addition the shadowing impact on the communal open space in Block 1would reduce its amenity value. Therefore, it is considered that the proposed development is contrary to Section 12.4.2 of the South Dublin County Development Plan (2004 – 2010) and would therefore be contrary to the proper planning and sustianable development of the area. || Having regard to the cumulative impacts of the following; (i) the incorporation of the existing parking spaces and the strip from the open space which would imapct negatively on the amenity of residents in the area (ii) the juxtaposition of the contemporary and traditional architecture (iii) the density of development on a village site, which is poorly served by public transport (iv) the excessive overshadowing from buildings on the southern elevation (v) Specific Local Objectives No. 98, regarding the possible designation of Saggart as an Area of Architectural Conservation and No. 100, regarding the retention of the rural character of Saggart village; it is considered that the proposed development would be out of character in this location, provide substandard accommodation and constitute overdevelopment of the site. Therefore it is considered that the proposed development would be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area.

Section 3.3.15.iv of the South Dublin County Development Plan 2004-2010 states that 'Within areas designated with Zoning Objective G', dwellings will only be permitted where; (a) The applicant can demonstrate a genuine need for housing in the area and; (b) The development is directly related to the area's amenity potential or its use for agriculture. The applicant has failed to demonstrate compliance with any of the above criteria for housing in the 'G' zone. The proposed development would therefore directly contravene the zoning objective for the area and would be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The proposed development would result in an additional vehicular access onto the Firhouse Road, which is classified as a District Distributor Road. As such the proposed development would result in additional turning movements onto this already heavily trafficked road, and would lower the capacity of said road. The proposed development would therefore endanger public safety by reason of traffic hazard and would be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The proposed development would result in overlooking of neighbouring dwellings to the west, at Dodder Green, by reason of the balconies on the northern elevations of Block B, at second floor level. Furthermore, the proposed second floor balconies of Blocks A and B would result in direct overlooking of the rear gardens of the townhouses of both blocks. Said overlooking is considered unacceptable and would impact negatively upon the residential amenities and privacy of neighbouring dwellings at Dodder Green and of the occupants of the townhouses of the proposed development. As such the proposed development would be seriously injurious to residential amenity and would be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || For reasons 1, 2 and 3 outlined above, it is considered that the proposed development on this sensitive site, would seriously injure the amenities and depreciate the value of property in the vicinity, and would impact negatively upon the amenities of the Dodder Valley and the Proposed Natural Heritage Area to the north. || The proposed development would set an undesirable precedent for other similar developments in the area, which would be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area.

The proposed development would result in a density of 52 units to the hectare and this density is in excess of the 30-50 units per hectare as recommended in Section 11.7 of the South Dublin County Council Development Plan and it is considered that this development would materially contravene the zoning objective for the area and would be contrary to the proper planning and development of the area. || The proposed development would represent over-development of the site by reason of inadequate separation distances between boundaries and between the rear elevations of existing buildings and proposed buildings, and insufficient private amenity space, and would materially contravene the South Dublin County Development Plan 2004-2010 and the zoning objective for the area ' to protect and/or improve Residential Amenity'. || The proposed car parking provision for the development is insufficient and therefore would tend to create serious traffic congesion. || The proposed development would not comply with the minimum setback required from the boundary of the site to the M50 Motorway and therefore a grant of permission would be contrary to proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The proposed development is unsatisfactory in terms of layout in particular in relation to the footprint and building height of the dwellings, the presentation of flank walls, the lack of bin storage facilities and the lack of cognisance taken of the existing built environment and therefore the lack of integration of the proposal with said environment. It is therefore considered that the proposal would be contrary to the zoning objective for the area and would be contrary to proper planning and sustainable development of the area.

The proposed development would be seriously deficient in the provision of off-street car parking spaces. By virtue of the intensification of use on the site, the lack of any off-street car parking for the proposed retail element, and the under-provision of additional off-street car parking for the residential element of the proposal, would lead to on-street parking on the roads adjoining this corner site, which would endanger public safety by reason of traffic hazard, obstruction of road users and would tend to create serious traffic congestion. || It has not been adequately demonstrated that the applicant has sufficient legal entitlement to carry out all of the material works required in and around the site to facilitate the proposed development. || The proposed development would set an undesirable precedent for other similar developments, which would in themselves and cumulatively be harmful to the residential amenities of the area and be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The proposed development would represent an overdevelopment of the site in terms of density and scale and would be out of character with development in the area and would therefore seriously injure the amenities and depreciate the value of property in the vicinity.

Section 11.11.1.iii of the South Dublin County Development Plan states that in locations outside Town and District centres and more than 400m from railway stations, the Council will require that all new large-scale housing schemes shall provide not less than 30% of the proposed dwelling units in the form of semi-detached and/or detached houses with gardens, and not more than 20% of units shall be apartments. Should permission be granted for this development it would result in a reduction of detached or semi-detached houses to 12% of the overall development and in an increase in apartments to 55% of the overall development. It is considered that this would materially contravene an objective of the development plan and would be contrary to the zoning objective for the area. || It is considered that the provision of 80no. two bedroom apartments within a single development would provide a residential mix that is unacceptable in terms of housing mix and would be contrary to sustainable development and would set an undesirable precedent for similar development. || It is considered that the proposed development would result in a poor form of residential amenity, by reason of a separation distance of 25m between three and four storey buildings, and therefore would contravene the zoning objective for the area 'to provide for new Residential Communities in accordance with Approved Area Plans' and would be contrary to proper planning and sustainable development of the area.

The proposed development, by reason of the proposed unsuitable servicing of and access to the site, is considered to be inadequate in relation to the development of the entirety of the residential zond lands and a grant of permission for the development as proposed would lead to piecemeal development of the area and prevent any future comprehensive redevelopment of the area. The proposed development would therefore be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || From the information submitted it is considered that the proposed development could cause serious water pollution to the Whitechurch River. || The proposed development would not comply with the minimum setback required from the boundary of the site to the M50 Motorway and therefore a grant of permission would be contrary to proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The proposed residential units fall within the path and safety clearance of ESB transmission lines on site. Although it is stated that this 110kv line is to be removed no details of same have been submitted and it is considered that the proposed development would endanger health and safety. || Development of the kind proposed on the land would be premature by reference to the existing deficiency in the provision of sewerage facilities in the area. Having regard to the remainder of residential zoned land in this area and the location of a salmonid stream on site, the proposed pumping station and rising mains are not an acceptable method of draining this site and would be potentially prejudicial to public health. || The proper planning and development of the area requires that the site be developed in co-ordination with development on adjoining lands which are zoned for residential development in the County Development Plan. It is considered that development of this part of the overall future development area is premature in the absence of a comprehensive vision for the future development of the entirety of the zoned lands. || Development of the kind proposed would be premature pending the determination by the Planning/Road Authority of a road layout for the area. || The proposed development, by reason of the design, scale and bulk of the proposed dwellings, does not take any cognisance of the existing character and pattern of residential development in the area and would thereby seriously injure and depreciate the value of property in the vicinity. || The proposed development does not take cognisance of the existing features on site including topography, existing pattern of development, hedges, stone walls, stone outbuildings, stream, and the environs of the site and it is considered therefore that the development would not take advantage of creating a unique sense of place based on existing features and the proposal would be contrary to proper planning and sustainable development.

The proposed development would result in a density of 120 units per hectare and this density is in excess of the 30 - 50 units per hectare as recommended in Section 11.7 of the Development Plan and as such the proposed development would be contrary to the objectives of the Plan and the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The proposed development of 12 residential units is on a site zoned 'F' to preserve and provide for open space and recreational amenities in the South Dublin County Development Plan 2004 - 2010. Under this zoning residential development is only open for consideration. Having regard to the fact that the proposed development would effectively develop the entirety of the site for residential development, it is considered that the proposal would materially contravene the zoning objective of this land primarily for a particular purpose. || The proposal would represent over-development of this small, narrow site by reason of the proposed density, separation distance between proposed ground floor rear patios and the site boundary to the north, and insufficient public and semi-private amenity space provisions. The proposed development would result in a cramped form of residential development at this location and would result in poor residential and visual amenities for future occupants. Furthermore, the proposed development would establish an undesirable precedent for other such similar developments in the area. The proposed development would therefore contravene the South Dublin County Development Plan 2004-2010 and the proper planning and sustainable development of the area.

Having regard to the 4.5 metre separation distance of Block B from the existing tributary of the Griffeen River, access for channel cleaning and maintenance would be impaired which would result in a development that would be prejudicial to public health and would be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area.

The proposed development would materially contravene the Tallaght Town Centre Local Area Plan by reason of the proposed building height, plot ratio, provision of open space and provision of residential accommodation above the 5th floor (6 storeys). The development would therefore contravene the zoning objective for the area 'to protect, improve and provide for the future development of the County Town of Tallaght' and would be contrary to proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The proposed development by reason of its building height, plot ratio, and provision of open space would result in over-development of the site and would set an undesirable precedent for other similar developments which would in themselves and cumulatively be harmful to the residential amenity of the area and would be contrary to proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The generation of traffic movements created as a result of the proposed egress onto the Belgard Road would endanger public safety by reason of a traffic hazard and would reduce the traffic capacity of this section of the Belgard Road thereby creating traffic congestion.

decision: REFUSE EXT. OF DURATION OF PERMISSION
reasons_joined: The application does not comply with Section 42(1)(a)(ii)(II) of the Planning and Development Act, 2000 (as amended), for the following reasons. • Section 42(1)(a)(ii)(II) of the Planning and Development Act, 2000 (as amended): The development is at variance with objectives contained in the County Development Plan 2010-2012 as detailed in the Fortunestown Local Area Plan 2012, which was drafted and approved in accordance with the Development Plan Objectives and Policies. In particular, with regard to its accessibility and movement strategy; green infrastructure strategy; land use and density strategy; built form strategy; frameworks strategy; phasing strategy; and the neighbourhood strategy for the subject site. Therefore, there have been significant changes in the development objectives in the development plan and in the local land use and planning context since the date of the permission such that the development would no longer be consistent with the proper planning and sustainable development of the area.

It is the policy of the Planning Authority, as set out in the current Development Plan for the area, when considering new housing development in this area, to have due regard to the high amenity value and proximity to the Dublin Mountains. Having regard to the prominent, elevated location of the site and to the layout proposed, which entails an undue degree of excavation into the mountain slope with consequent large scale retaining structures, it is considered that the proposed development would be excessively obtrusive and would seriously injure the visual amenities of the area. The proposed development would, therefore, be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || It is considered that the proposed gradients of 8% for estate roads, which is 3% in excess of the Council standard of 5%, in an area where altitudes are conducive to heavy frosts and icy conditions in winter, and a number of proposed perpendicular car parks on these roads, which fail to provide adequate sight lines for safe reversing, would constitute traffic hazards.

The proposed development by reason of its mass and bulk would be at variance with the existing scale and character of the area and therefore the proposed development if permitted would result in a serious negative impact on existing visual and residential amenity of the area and would depreciate the value of property in the vicinity. || The residential element of the proposed development would have a density of 127 units to the hectare and it is considered that notwithstanding the sites location along a QBC given the layout and orientation of the units, the amenity level of the open space associated with the development, and the unsatisfactory level of the traffic that would be generated as a result of the development that the proposal would result in over- development of the site and would provide a poor level of residential amenity for future residents. Therefore the proposed development would be contrary to the zoning objective for the area 'to protect and/or improve Residenital Amenity' and to proper planning and sustainable development. || Having specific regard to the fact the proposed development includes a retail element and also having regard to the quantum of development proposed it is considered that the development would greatly increase the numbers of vehicles accessing Loreto Terrace and Grange Road to an unacceptable level and would therefore tend to create serious traffic congestion.

The development would contravene materially condition 2 attached to an existing permission for development Reg. Ref. SD04A/0953 as it would not facilitate future linkages to adjoining lands and integration as required by the Newcastle-Lyons Local Area Plan 2003. || Having regard to the pattern of development in the area, it is considered that the proposed development of 10 no. dwelling units represents over-development of a restricted site, would be out of character with development in the area and would be visually obtrusive when viewed from adjoining properties. Thus the proposed development would seriously injure the amenities of and depreciate the value of property in the vicinity. || The proposed development of a 2/3 storey apartment block, containing a roof garden within 10 metres of an adjacent residential property is contrary to Section 11.11.4 of the South Dublin County Development Plan (2004 – 2010) and would have a negative impact on the privacy of neighbouring residential properties and would cause an unacceptable loss of light and privacy; therefore the proposed development would seriously injure the amenities and depreciate the value of property in the vicinity. || The proposed development is visually out of character with the existing houses and dwellings under construction in the area, in terms of style, roof profile and bulk. Having regard to (i) the future land use assumptions for the Village Green and Blessington Road precinct as outlined in the Tallaght Town Centre Local Area plan which state that : "Buildings should be medium scale within the Village Green. The location of a creche (with an excessive capacity for phase 3) on lands under the zoning objective B, is considered premature having regard to the boundary of the Action Area Plan Lands and it is considered that such a use should be accommodated within the Action Plan Lands, in order to provide planned services in tandem with housing and prevent the incremental encroachment of such uses and the unplanned extension of urban uses outside the boundary of Saggart village and it is considered therefore were the proposed creche permitted it would be contrary to the proper planning of the area and sustianable development of the area. || The proposal will result in the construction of an access road across an area identified within the Saggart Action Area Plan as proposed open space. The public open space provision contravenes the objectives of the County Development Plan, and if permittted would be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The current proposal is the final phase in the development of these lands (under Phase one, 325 housing units were permitted and under Phase two, permission is sought for a 144 housing units currently on a clarification request).
