Therefore, the proposed development would contravene said zoning objective and would be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The Planning Authority would have serious concerns with regard to the detailed design of the proposed development, particularly with regard to bulk, scale, elongated form, orientation of balconies, separation distances, public / private open space provision, and void related noise / odour emission concerns. For reasons outlined above, the proposed development would impact negatively upon the visual and residential amenities of the residents of the proposed development, would constitute over-development of the site and would set an undesirable precedent for similar developments in the area. As such, the proposed development would be contrary to the Development Plan, Ministerial Guidelines - Residential Density - Guidelines for Planning Authorities', and would be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || For reasons (1) to (3) above, the proposed development would set an undesirable precedent for other similar developments in the area, which would in itself and cumulatively be harmful to the amenities of the area, which would be contrary to the zoning objective for the area and the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The basement car-park associated with the proposal cannot be accessed from within the red-line of the subject site, and is reliant on the outcome of a current application on the adjoining Firhouse Shopping Centre site. As such the proposed access arrangements to said basemaent are considered pre-mature pending the outcome of said application. The proposed development would therefore be contray to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area.

The proposed basement level car park to serve the employment-intensive office development, located in an area zoned 'E' for enterprise and employment and related uses, is contrary to Section 12.3.2 of the County Development Plan; this requires that in lands zoned 'E', basement level car parking shall only be permitted on sites within specified distances from a QBC, LUAS or heavy rail stop. On sites located outside these walking distances car parking shall be provided at surface level only. The proposed development is therefore is contrary to the provision of Section 12.3.2 of the County Development Plan 2004 - 2010. || The proposed development of 21 no. own door office units with a combined floor area of 3,810m2 comprising 66% of the total proposed development and served by an associated basement car park together with 1,953m2 of warehouse units with ancillary offices, would represent an excessive concentration of employment intensive uses and overdevelopment of an out of centre site, away from good public transport services and other facilities. Trip generation associated with the proposed development is likely to be reliant on private transport in a manner that would serve to reinforce unsustainable patterns of car commuting and undermine the role in the County Development Plan 2004-10 of designated centres and employment sites in close proximity to public transport, where employment intensive uses should more appropriately be located and would therefore be contrary to the proper planning and development of the area. || The layout of the proposed development would involve the removal of a substantial portion of the existing earth berm along the north eastern boundaries of the site. This berm contributes significantly to the visual amenity of Baldonnell Business Park; its retention was required by Condition 10 of the previous grant of permission for 2 industrial/warehouse blocks on this prominent site (SD06a/1057). The proposed development would therefore negatively impact on the visual amenities of the area and be contrary to proper planning and sustainable development. || The proposed employment intensive development at this location would set an undesirable precedent for other similar developments, which would in themselves and cumulatively be harmful to the development of Baldonnell Business Park and be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area.

The overall design and elevational treatment of the proposed apartments are considered to be unacceptable and inappropriate in this area. The Old Nangor Road is an important approach into Clondalkin village and buildings of a high quality standard are required at this location. The proposed development would represent substandard development in this prominent location and would seriously injure the amenities and depreciate the value of property in the vicinity, through the poor quality of design. || South Dublin County Council is the freehold owner of the south east part of the property. A leasehold interest for a term of 150 years was granted to Mr. N. Nolan subject to the demised property being used for garden purposes only. The disposal was subject to restrictions on the further use of the lands. The proposed development is totally at variance with the terms of the disposal of these lands, which were based on the fact that the lands being disposed of were to be subsidiary and ancillary to Raheen Cottage and to be used for garden purposes only. The proposed development would contravene this lease; the applicant does not therefore have sufficient legal interest in the site to carry out the proposed development. || The proposed development does not comply with the Planning Authority and the Department of the Environment, Heritage and Local Government requirements in relation to bedroom floor areas and internal storage areas for apartments. The proposed development would therefore represent substandard development, providing insufficient space forfuture residents. The proposed development would therefore be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The proposed development would set an undesirable precedent for other similar developments, which would in themselves and cumulatively be harmful to the visual and residential amenities of the area and be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The proposed development would necessitate the removal of a number of trees along the roadside boundary and within the site. The existing trees are an important feature on the approach to Clondalkin Villag and would have a negative visual impact and would interfere with the character and amenity value of this area. The proposed development by virtue of its negative visual impact on the site and the surrounding area would seriously injure the amenities of the area and depreciate the value of property in the vicinity. The proposed development would therefore be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable of the area.

The development, as proposed, would materially contravene policy 9.4.7.i,- “to protect and preserve trees and woodlands”; would result in a substantial negative impact on a protected structure by virtue of the loss of associated, contemporaneous trees of significant landscape and amenity value and would result in a major loss of amenity to the existing residential developments in the vicinity and would therefore constitute a material contravention of the zoning objective which seeks 'to protect and/or improve residential amenity.' || The proposed development is located in the curtilage of a Protected Structure (Silveracre House) as designated in the current Development Plan for the area, Map Reference No. 277. It is considered that the proposed development by reason of the overall design and scale of the proposed units, when taken in conjunction with their location proximate to the Protected Structure, would severely compromise the architectural and remnant landscape integrity of the building and its treed context, would seriously detract from the character and setting of special interest of the Protected Structure and therefore, be contrary to the proper planning and development of the area, including the protection of its architectural heritage. || The omission of an impact assessment of the proposed development on the curtilage of a Protected Structure, including the boundary walls and mature trees, is considered to be contrary to Section 12.11.13.ii of the South Dublin County Council Development Plan 2004 - 2010, which states that applications relating to Protected Structures shall include a comprehensive assessment of the likely effects of the proposal on the special character of a Protected Structure. || On the basis of the information submitted with the application, the Planning Authority is not satisfied that significant overlooking of adjacent property has been avoided. Therefore, it is considered that the proposed development may seriously detract from the existing residential amenity of the area and depreciate the value of property in the vicinity.

Having regard to: (i) the proposed plot ratio of 1.67:1 which exceeds the performance criterion of 1.5:1 as set out in the Tallaght Town Centre Local Area Plan for buildings in this precinct, (ii) the relationship, with regard to height and massing adjacent to the Architectural Conservation Area and setback at ground and 4th storey level on Main Street/Blessington Road, which is a transition zone to a more sensitve area, as identified in the Tallaght Town Centre Local Area Plan and (iii) the excavation of the basement encroaching under the public realm area at surface level between the facade of the building and the site boundary, which would compromise the achievement of an objective to establish street trees along Main Street/Blessington Road it is considered that the proposed development would constitute overdevelopment of the site which would materially contravene the objectives of the Tallaght Town Centre Local Area Plan, as outlined in chapter five of the said plan, would seriously injure the visual amenities of the area and would be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || Having regard to: (i) the inadequate provision of high quality communal open space, (ii) the inappropriate location, in constant shadow, of the children's play area and (iii) the failure to provide for functional public open space, it is considered that the proposed development would provide substandard public and private amenity and would therefore materially contravene the zoning objective, "CT", as set out in the South Dublin County Council Development Plan 2004 -2010, which seeks "to protect, improve and provide for the future development of the County Town of Tallaght". || The proposed development would materially affect the character of the existing historical village of Tallaght and the adjoining Architectural Conservation Area. It is considered that any new development within the village core should respect the scale and character of the existing building stock. The proposed development would therefore be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || Information submitted with the application failed to comply with documentation required pursuant to Section 11.2 of the South Dublin County Council Development Plan 2004 -2010 and Section 5.1.9 of the Tallaght Town Centre Local Area Plan, regarding site analysis, design statement, including a shadow analysis to demonstrate levels of shading to habitable and communal spaces, and/or consistency in plans and details for parking, waste mangement, and open space levels. It is considered that of itself, and by the undesirable precedent these omissions would set for applications for simliar scale developments, the proposal failed to provide adequate information on which to recommend a grant of permission.

The alterations to the development as proposed would result in a development which does not meet the requirements or thrust of Section 11.11.1 iii of South Dublin County Development Plan 2004-2010, which requires a mix of dwelling units in the interests of promoting new residential accommodation which is suitable for families. Furthermore the proposed apartments do not provide for internal storage areas as required and set out in the 'Quality Housing for Sustainable Communities-Best Practice Guidelines' Department of the Environment, Heritage and Local Government (2007). As such, it is considered that this proposal would create a form of development which would be detrimental to the residential amenity of future residents and would not be in line with the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The proposed development would set an undesirable precedent for other similar developments, which would in themselves and cumulatively be harmful to the residential amenities of the area and be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area.

The proposed development would materially contravene Specific Local Objective 111 of the South Dublin County Development Plan 2004 – 2010 by failing to facilitate sensitive development within the site of Edmondstown || In particular the proposed development would adversely impact the Owendoher river and the roadside elevation, bulk and height of Building B would be visually obtrusive in this High Amenity zoning. || The proposed development would materially contravene Specific Local Objective 103 of the South Dublin County Development Plan 2004 – 2010 by failing to provide an acceptable riverside path with adequate permeability and connectivity to the surrounding public footpath network. The proposed pedestrian bridge at the southern end of the walkway links to a very steep river bank and no rationale has been given for the provision of this bridge. || The proposed development would contravene materially a development objective indicated in the Development Plan for the zoning of the land for high amenity, due to the removal of a significant amount of the riverside vegetation to facilitate the proposed development of the underground car park and pedestrian walkway, the significant impact on the Owendoher river, the narrowing of the river bank, and the unacceptably narrow riverside path proposed. || The proposed development fails to provide adequate parking. Furthermore, by failing to provide adequate sight lines the proposed development would endanger public safety by reason of traffic hazard. || The proposed roadside elevation, height and bulk of Building B is considered visually obtrusive and would adversely impact the character of the Protected Structure. Thus the proposed development would seriously injure the amenities of property in the vicinity. || The proposed development would materially contravene policy WD7 of the County Development Plan to protect, improve and enhance the natural and organic character of an important salmonid watercourse in the County and would therefore be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area.

The proposed development of a terrace of five houses and a three storey block of six apartments to rear to replace an existing dwelling would represent serious over development of a residential site area. The proposed residential density of the development would be 58 dwellings per hectare. This exceeds the South Dublin County Council Development Plan standards as set out in Section 11.7 of the South Dublin County Council Development Plan 2004-2010, which indicates density thresholds to achieve the zoning objective, which is "to protect and/or improve residential amenity". Therefore, the proposed development would contravene said zoning objective and would be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || By reason of layout and design, including private balconies on first / second floors of Block 2 and associated overlooking of Block 1, the proposed development would be contrary to Section 11.11.5 of the Development Plan and Section 5.6.1 of the Residential Density Guidelines. The proposed development would have a negative impact on the privacy and residential amenities of the existing and proposed dwellings. As such, the proposed development would be seriously injurious to the amenities and would depreciate the value of properties in the vicinity and would be contrary to the zoning objective for the area, which seeks to 'protect and / or improve Residential Amenity'. || Having regard to the size of the site, the design of the proposed development, the width of the proposed townhouses, sub-standard public and semi-private open space provision and overlooking, it is considered that the proposed development would be significantly out of character with the pattern of development in the area, would impact negatively upon the visual and residential amenities of the residents of the proposed development and those of the surrounding area, and would constitute over-development of the site. As such, the proposed development would materially contravene the zoning objective for the site, which seeks to 'protect and / or improve Residential Amenity' and would be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The proposed development would set an undesirable precedent for other similar developments in the area, which would in itself and cumulatively be harmful to the residential amenities of the area, which would be contrary to the zoning objective for the area and the proper planning and sustainable development of the area.

Having regard to the density of units granted on this site, which is in excess of Section 11.7 of the South Dublin County Development Plan 2004 - 2010, and the loss of associated surface car parking spaces, it is considered that the proposed development would constitute over development of a restricted site and would materially contravene the zoning objective which seeks 'to protect, provide for and/or improve Local Centre facilities'. Thus the proposed development would be inconsistent with the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The proposed development would constitute piecemeal and incremental alteration of an already permitted development which would further erode the dwelling mix in this development. This is contrary to Development Plan policy to promote dwelling mix and would create an undesirable precedent for similar developments in the County.

The proposed development would of itself and by undesirable precedent for other similar be harmful to the amenities of the area and be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The original application on the site, Planning Register Reference S02A/0096, was granted permission by way of a material contravention of the County Development Plan. The proposed development comprising the demolition of the existing golf retail outlet and the construction of 56 no. golf lodges, would constitute development beyond the terms and conditions of the material contravention granted under S02A/0096. These terms included a mix of uses including a golf shop and 91 Golf Lodges (i.e. short term tourist accommodation). It is considered that the omission of a golf shop and its replacement with 56 golf lodges would intensify a non-conforming use in the Greenbelt which would not comply with the quantum and mix of uses of the development permitted by way of material contravention under S02A/0096. As such, the proposed development would materially contravene the stated zoning objective for the area and would not be in line with the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || Having regard to provisions as set out in South Dublin County Council's Development Plan 2004-2010 regarding residential use in ''GB'', (Green Belt) zone, it is considered that the proposed development would constitute a material contravention of this zoning objective. || The encroachment of the proposed development into the golf course would constitute a material contravention of Condition No. 1 S99A/0205, which shows the layout of the golf course.

The proposed development would have insufficient off-street parking space and turning space for the public accessing the scale of retail units proposed and given the location proposed within the development and having regard to the close proximity of the proposed retail units to a busy junction, the proposed development would endanger public safety by reason of traffic hazard, would cause obstruction of other road users and create congestion which would interefere with the freeflow of traffic along the Knocklyon Road. The proposed development would therefore be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The proposed development, by reason of its fragmented and undesirably located public open space, would result in a poor standard of layout, has minimal passive surveillance and provides no variety in size or use potential. The proposed development would materially contravene the standards set out in Section 11.9 of South Dublin County Council Development Plan 2004-2010, would constitute a sub-standard form of development for future residents and would, therefore, be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. Thus, the proposed development would seriously injure the amenities of property in the vicinity.

decision: REFUSE EXT. OF DURATION OF PERMISSION
reasons_joined: Permission for this development was granted under the South Dublin County Development Plan 2004-2010. In the interim a new County Development has been adopted - South Dublin County Council Development Plan 2010-2016. This Development Plan introduces a series of new policy objectives including a specific objective that makes a significant change to the development objectives relating to this proposed development. It is considered that the proposed development does not comply with Section 2.3.12.ii Policy WD6: Sustainable Urban Drainage Systems (SuDS). It is the policy of the Council to ensure that all development proposals incorporate Sustainable Urban Drainage Systems (SuDS). As such the proposed development would no longer be consistent with the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The permission does not comply with national Ministerial Guidelines, The Planning System and Flood Risk Management – Guidelines for Planning Authorities (2009), which were issued by the Minister under section 28 of the Planning and Development Act, 2000 (as amended). Thus, the Planning Authority considers that the proposed development would not be consistent with the proper planning and sustainable development of the area having regard to any guidelines issued by the Minister under Section 28, notwithstanding that they were so issued after the date of the grant of permission in relation to which an application is made under this Section.

decision: REFUSE EXT. OF DURATION OF PERMISSION
reasons_joined: The development is not in accordance with Section 42(1)(a)(ii)(II) of the Planning and Development Act, 2000 (as amended), for the following reasons: The development does not comply with the Built Form Strategy of the Fortunestown Local Area Plan 2012 by reason of the omission of a secondary street built frontage running in a north/south direction through the site. It is at variance with para. 6.5.5 (Built Form) which requires that ‘residential development across the Saggart-Cooldown Commons Neighbourhood shall be laid out in a grid like format that incorporates perimeter blocks and a hierarchy of streets’. The western site boundary of the proposal has a park and development backing onto the site boundary which is at variance with the requirement for perimeter blocks. Furthermore, due to the high proportion of apartments/duplexes, the proposal would not accord with the requirements of Section 6.5.3 ‘Density and Land Use’ in the Fortunestown Local Area Plan 2012 which requires that: • A minimum of 85% of all dwellings be provided as own door houses on their own site and that a maximum of 15% of all dwellings across the Plan Lands be provided as apartments/duplexes……… (Objective SCCN4a) Thus, there have been significant changes in the development objectives in the development plan for the area (due to the Fortunestown Local Area Plan 2012) since the date of the permission such that the development would no longer be consistent with the proper planning and sustainable development of the area.

The proposed development by reason of its scale, height and design would be at variance with the existing scale and character of the area. Thus the proposed development would seriously injure the amenities and depreciate the value of property in the vicinity. || The proposed development would result in a residential density of 61 units to the hectare and this density is in excess of the 35-50 units per hectare as recommended in Section 11.7 of the South Dublin County Council Development Plan 2004-2010, for this site. As such the proposed development would contravene the zoning objective for the area which seeks to, 'to protect, provide for and / or improve Local Centre facilities'. Furthermore, given the scale, design, layout and orientation of the residential units, the amenity level of the open space associated with the development, the proposal would result in over-development of the site and would provide a poor level of residential amenity for future residents. The proposed development would also set an undesirable precedent for other such similar developments in the area, which would by itself and cumulatively detract from the amenities of the area, and would be contrary to the zoning objective for the area and the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || Inadequate provision has been made for internal storage facilities to serve the residential element of the proposal as provided for in the 'Sustainable Urban Housing:Design Standards for Apartments' Consultation Guidelines of the Department of the Environment Heritage and Local Government and the requirements of the Council's Development Plan 2004-2010. The proposed development would, therefore, be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The proposed shared access for a common patio area is not acceptable for the residential units, in particular, as a number of bedrooms front directly onto this common area where there could be significant noise resulting in a loss of residential amenity to the occupants. The proposal would, therefore, be contrary to the zoning objective for the area. || The Planning Authority is not satisfied that the 5 key urban design principles detailed in Section 11.2.lV of the County Development Plan have been fully addressed particularly in respect of the visual impact of the proposed 4-storey development and the 16 metre high structure accommodating only a lift and stair on the streetscape and the potential impact on adjoining properties in terms of overlooking and overshadowing. The proposal would, therefore, be contrary to the zoning objective for the area. || Having regard to the mixed use nature of the proposed development and the quantum of development proposed it is considered that the development has insufficient, off-street car parking spaces for the public. As a result, the proposed development would endanger public safety by reason of traffic hazard,would cause obstruction of other road users, and create congestion which would interefere with the freeflow of traffic. The proposed development would therefore be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area.

Having regard to the pattern of development in the Dodsboro area, it is considered that the proposed development, consisting of 17 residential units in one block, ranging from three to four storeys in height above basement level carpark to replace two existing dwellings, would represent serious over development within an established residential area. The proposed residential density of the development would be 98 units per hectare/40.4 dwelling units per acre. This significantly exceeds the density range of 35 - 50 dwellings per hectare/14 - 20 per acre net outside designated Town & District Centres, as set out in Section 11.7 of the South Dublin County Council Development Plan 2004-2010. Therefore, the proposed development would be contrary to the provisions of Section 11.7 of the South Dublin County Development Plan and would be contrary to the zoning objective for the area, which seeks to 'protect and / or improve Residential Amenity'. As such, the proposed development would seriously injure the amenities and depreciate the value of property in the vicinity and would be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The overall design of the proposed residential development is considered unacceptable and inappropriate in this area. Having regard to the established pattern of development in the area and existing streetscape of Dodsborough Road, it is considered that the proposed development would be unsympathetic and significantly out of character with development in the area, would impact negatively upon the visual and residential amenities of the surrounding area, and would be visually dominant and obtrusive in the area, particularly when viewed from existing properties to the east, west and south of the subject site. As such, the proposed development would seriously injure the amenities and depreciate the value of property in the vicinity and would be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The proposed development would set an undesirable precedent for other similar developments in the area, which would in itself and cumulatively be harmful to the residential amenities of the area, which would be contrary to the zoning objective for the area and the proper planning and sustainable development of the area.

The proposed development, which seeks to increase the number of units on the site from 98 units to 112 units would contravene the terms of Condition No.14 Registered Reference S00A/0639 which restricts the density of the development on the site to 50 units per ha i.e. 98 units. || The proposed development provides significantly substandard residential amenity through failures to comply with minimum criteria as set out in ministerial guidelines for planning authorities "Sustainable Urban Housing: Design Standards for New Apartments 2007" and Chapter 11 of the South Dublin County Council Development Plan 2004-2010 regarding internal amenity, range of dwelling types and the quantum and location of communal open space. As such it is considered that (i) the granting permission or retention of development would authorise development which is materially contrary to the zoning objective, which seeks to protect and/or improve residential amenity; and (ii) which would of itself and by undesirable precedent for other similar developments in the area incrementally undermine the achievement of the zoning objective.

The application site is zoned 'Objective B', which sets out 'To protect and improve Rural Amenity and to provide for the development of Agriculture.' Under this zoning objective residential development (described as a 'retirement accommodation') that accords with council policy for development in rural areas is listed as 'open for consideration' but 'retirement accommodation/ complex of independent units is not included in the zoning matrix. The proposed development would provide for a comprehensive residential development of 100 dwellings, which would not accord with Council Policy (Policy H15) to restrict housing in the Rural 'B' zone and could not comply with the Development Pan's rural housing needs criteria that restricts housing in the 'B' zone to those that have a genuine need to reside in proximity to rural related employment or have close family ties with the rural community. The proposed development would therefore materially contravene the rural and agricultural zoning objective of the application site and would be contrary to proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || Section 12.12.7 of the South Dublin County Council Development Plan (2004) sets out an objective to limit the development of residential or commercial clusters to areas below the 120 metre contour in the Dublin Mountains area, (except where A1 zones are shown in this Plan above the 120 metre contour and also where specific objectives so permit in this Plan), in the interest of pursuing the policy of sustainability in both high amenity and rural areas. The proposed development described as 'retirement accommodation' would provide for the insertion of a cluster of residential development with a commercial element (public restaurant and health centre) between the 140 metre and 160 metre contour. Such a development would adversely impact on views (including protected views) and the rural character of the Dublin Mountains, which is of high passive and visual amenity value to the surrounding area. The proposed development would therefore be at variance with the Development Plan Objective to protect the visual and passive open amenity of areas above the 120 metre contour in the Dublin Mountains and would materially contravene the 'B' zoning objective of the application site, which sets out to (inter alia) protect and improve Rural Amenity. || The proposed development would adversely impact on the character and sylvan setting of Woodstown Manor (Protected Structure), which is of regional importance, by reason of the removal of important boundary features; the loss of walled gardens; extensive development within existing woodlands; excessive height that would overbear and dominate the primary (front) elevation of the house and the substantial extent and inappropriate location of surface car parking and set down area. The proposed development would therefore be contrary to recommendations of the Architectural Heritage Protection Guidelines for Planning Authorities (2004), which were issued to Planning Authorities under Section 28 of the Planning and Development Act 2000 (as amended). The proposal for retirement accommodation in a complex of clustered units would also be at variance with a Specific Local Objective (SLO 116) to facilitate a hotel development and associated leisure uses at Woodtown Manor by reason of the nature of the proposed development and failure to provide for a use that is akin to a hotel development, failure to adequately provide for the conservation of historic features that relate to the Protected Structure, the inappropriate sprawl of development across the application site and its extensive site coverage. || The proposed apartment buildings and houses (described as 'requirement accommodation) to the north-east, east and south-east of the application site would result in the substantial removal of existing mature trees, hedgerows and vegetation. The crown spread of a number of retained trees would also be located within the footprint of proposed new buildings and hard landscaping where it would be unlikely for trees to survive in the medium to long term. The application site is subject to an objective under the South Dublin County Council Development Plan (2004) to protect and preserve Trees and Woodland and within this context this aspect of the proposal would contravene Policy LHA 9 of the Development Plan, which sets out to preserve trees, groups of trees or woodlands, which form a significant feature in the landscape, or are important in setting the character of an area. Furthermore, the 4 no. proposed 3 storey apartment blocks on the site would reach a maximum height of 160 metres OD and would be highly visible from parts of Stocking Lane, which rises in tandem with the site from circa 130 metres OD to circa 170 metres OD and along which protected views are designated under the Development Plan. On the basis of the above the proposed development would interfere with the rural character of the landscape and protected views of special amenity character. The proposal would also contravene the ‘B’ zoning objective of the application site, which sets out to (inter alia) protect and improve Rural Amenity. || The proposed development would cover circa 6,000 sq.m to provide for a site coverage of circa 9% on a site area of circa 6.8 Hectares (excluding access driveway) and would include 3 no. 2 storey apartment blocks and 4 no. 3 storey apartment blocks, which would reach circa 10 metres in height. Due to its upland positioning on a hill side, the proposed 2 and 3 storey apartment blocks would be visually prominent in the landscape and the proposal would include a substantial number of platforms created by cut and fill into the hillside throughout the application site in order to provide for the significant quantum of new buildings and surface car parks. Such a development (described as 'retirement accommodation) would be at variance with Section 12.4.10.i of the Development Plan, which states that dwellings in rural areas should generally be single storey in height and should not be intrusive or incongruous in the landscape and the guidelines on the Siting and Design of Rural Dwellings as contained within Appendix 3 under which it is stated that dwellings should be built into a slope and should avoid creating a platform. The proposal would therefore materially contravene the 'B' zoning objective, which sets out to (inter alia) protect and improve Rural Amenity, by reason of excessive scale, height and site coverage. || Given the independent nature of the proposed 'retirement accommodation' units it is considered appropriate to use the minimum standards of relevant ministerial guidelines. All of the proposed dwellings would fail to meet the recommended standards for storage space as set out under the 'Sustainable Urban Housing: Design Standards for Apartments' (2007) and 'Quality Housing for Sustainable Communities' (2007) and would be substandard in this regard. The 12 no. proposed 2 bedroom Duplex units (Type H and J) and all of the proposed 25 no. single storey 2 bedroom houses would also be substandard in terms of private amenity space by reason of failure to meet the minimum private amenity space standards as set out in Table 11.2 of the South Dublin County Council Development Plan (2004) and the recommendations of the apartment guidelines, which states that apartment should comply with the relevant Development Plan standards on private amenity space. The proposed development (apartment element) would therefore be contrary to the recommendations of 'Sustainable Urban Housing: Design Standards for Apartments' (2007), which were issued to planning authorities under Section 28 of the Planning and Development Act 2000 (as amended). || The proposal would provide for a total of 100 dwellings (described as 'retirement accommodation') on a site of circa 6.8 Hectares (excluding access driveway), which would represent an excessive density of circa 15 dwellings per hectare on a rural backland site. Such a development would materially contravene the rural 'B' zoning objective of the application site and would set an undesirable precedent for similar low density suburban type development on rural zoned lands throughout the County of South Dublin, which would in themselves and cumulatively be harmful to the rural and upland amenities of the County.

decision: REFUSE EXT. OF DURATION OF PERMISSION
reasons_joined: No Appropriate Assessment or Screening report was carried out despite proximity to Natura 2000 sites.

By reason of its design, scale and bulk and location on this prominent site of restricted size and configuration, the proposed development would be unduly obtrusive and out of character with the pattern of development in the area. The proposed development would, therefore, seriously injure the amenities of the area and of property in the vicinity and would be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The Owendoher River is an important part of the salmonid system and has an extensive ecological system. It is also a stream that is subject to flooding. The applicant has failed to provide details relating to the impact of the proposed development on the current biodiversity resource of the site or a detailed flood risk assessment which includes designs for mitigating measures against flooding. In the absence of this information, the proposed development, if permitted, could have a negative impact on the surrounding environment and would be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The proposed development, by reason of the quantum of office and residential space proposed, does not comply with the ‘A’ zoning objective of the site which seeks to protect and / or improve Residential Amenity’ and would represent overdevelopment of a restricted site. The proposed would also set an undesirable precedent for other similar developments, which would in themselves contravene the zoning objective of the area. The proposed development would, therefore, be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area.

The Tallaght Town Centre Local Area Plan 2006 objectives for the Cookstown North Precinct states that no significant changes are envisaged for the area in the short-medium term and the pedestrian environment along Cookstown Road should be upgraded to provide a safe night time link between the Cookstown South and Belgard Station Precincts. The overall Masterplan outcome for the area further states that high intensity development within the area would not be in accordance with the principles of sustainable development whilst access to services and public transport are constrained (Section 4.6). The Tallaght Town Centre Local Area Plan 2206 is current to 2012. While this period exceeds the operational life of the current Development Plan 2004 - 2010 by 2 years, it is proposed to incorporate the Local Area Plan into the Development Plan 2010 - 2016. Within this plan-making context, the timescale for major development in the area of the application site is envisaged to take place between 2011 and 2014 under Section 6.3 of the Local Area Plan. It is stated that redevelopment of sites in the vicinity of the Cookstown Luas and Belgard Luas precincts will not be granted permission until the key road infrastructure is in place including the Belgard Square East/North connection to Fourth Avenue, the Airton Road extension to Cookstown Road, the Embankment Road Extension and new access to the Cookstown Industrial Road from this extension. The proposed development would therefore be piecemeal and premature pending the key road infrastructure and pedestrian improvements identified for the area, by reference to the order of priority for development indicated in the Local Area Plan. Such a development would therefore contravene the Local Area Plan objectives on the phasing and implementation of development throughout Tallaght Town Centre and the specific objectives for the Cookstown North and Belgard Station Precincts. || Availing of the land-uses prescribed in the Tallaght Town Centre Local Plan 2006 is dependent on strictly adhering to the relevant land use objective and the order of priority for development as prescribed in the Local Area Plan (LAP). Within the context of the proposal’s failure to comply with the LAP objectives on land use and phasing of development; the proposal would materially contravene the Development Plan ‘E’ zoning objective of the application site by reason of the inclusion of residential uses and an excessive quantum of retail floorspace (3,410 sq.m) that would constitute major sales outlets, which are not permitted under the zoning objective. || The proposal would materially contravene the urban design objectives of the Tallaght Town Centre Local Area Plan 2006 (Section 5.2.1) in terms of the Scale, Land Use and Solar Access by reason of: - Excessive building heights that would be inconsistent with existing surrounding building heights and those that are envisaged for the surrounding area; - The orientation and 6 storey maximum height of Building 3, which would fail to ensure that solar access to the open space courtyard partially enclosed to the north of the building is maximised; - The excessive proportion of single aspect units (circa 27%), which would fail to ensure that solar access to internal living areas is maximised. - The excessive quantum of retail units (16 no.) and retail floor area (circa 3,410 sq.m) that would conflict with recently completed retail developments within the core shopping area of Tallaght Town Centre to the south. || The plot ratio of Building 4 (1.3:1) and the combined plot ratios of adjacent Buildings 2 and 3 (1.3:1) would, including an allowance for a floorspace bonus of 20% for proposed public realm improvements, exceeds the area specific plot ratio thresholds designated on Map 5.2.1 of the Tallaght Town Centre Local Area Plan (2006). All 4 of the proposed buildings (Buildings 1-4 inclusive) would also exceed the relevant Building Height Thresholds designated on Map 5.2.2 of the Local Area Plan (LAP). The proposal would therefore result in excessive overdevelopment of the application site and would materially contravene the LAP objectives on building heights and plot ratios. || Table 11.1 of the South Dublin County Council Development Plan (2004) sets out a maximum density of 75 units per hectare for sites within 400 metres (walking distance) of a Luas Stop. The proposed development would be located within 400 metres of the Belgard Luas stop and the density of the proposal (217 units) on a site of 2.04 Hectares would equate to 106 dwellings per hectare. Therefore the density of the proposal is excessive and would represent over development of the application site and, in the context of the material contravention of the Local Area Plan in terms of height, plot ratio, land use and phasing; would be contrary to the 'Residential Density Guidelines for Planning Authorities' (1999) and the draft guidelines on 'Sustainable Residential Development in Urban Areas' (2008). || The majority of the proposed apartments would, excluding built in bedroom storage presses, fail to meet the floorspace standards as set out in the ‘Sustainable Urban Housing: Design Standards for Apartments’ (September 2007) in terms of storage. Some 2 bedroom apartments would also fail to meet the standard on aggregate floor areas for bedrooms. The proposed development would therefore fail to provide an acceptable standard of residential amenity and would be contrary to the apartment guidelines. Furthermore, the proportion of 1 bedroom apartments at 26% would result in an oversupply of such apartments and would materially contravene the Tallaght Town Centre Local Area Plan 2006 objective (Section 5.3.2) to provide a range of dwelling types and ensure a range of housing options are available within any given development. || The proposed staggered traffic light junction at the junction between the proposed link road, the Cookstown Estate Road and First Avenue would endanger public safety by reason of traffic hazard due to the prospect of northbound vehicles entering the southbound lane as they cross the junction. || The overall proposed quantum of retail floorspace (3,410 sq.m total) and size/type of retail units (reaching 372 sq.m in size) would exceed the area’s normal local shopping requirements (i.e. local employees and residents) and would attract a wider catchment. The intensity, scale and nature of the proposed retail elements would therefore contravene the Tallaght Town Centre Local Area Plan 2006 objectives for the area (Section 4.6 - Cookstown North Precinct and Section 4.4 - Belgard Station Precinct), which set out to provide for small local retail shops and car dependant bulky goods retail units only. The retail and commercial floorspace composition of Building 4 would also materially contravene Section 4.6.3 of the Local Area Plan (LAP) in terms of the industrial land use objective designated for the area of the application site occupied by Building 4. Furthermore, Building 3 would include an excessive proportion of residential floorspace (98%) that would materially contravene Section 4.6.3 of the LAP in terms of the land use objective (Mixed Use B - up to 70% residential) designated for the area of the application site occupied by Building 3.

The dwelling mix proposed of 87% apartments, 4% semi-detached houses and 9% duplexes is not in accordance with Section 11.11.1(iii) of the South Dublin County Council Development Plan 2004-2010. As such, the proposed development would be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area || The site is located within a Zone of Archaeological Potential surrounding Newcastle village, included in the Record of Monuments and Places in the South Dublin County Council Development Plan 2004-2010 DU020-003. An Archaeological Assessment has not been submitted with this application. It has, therefore, not been satisfactorily demonstrated that the proposed development would preserve and articulate the planimetric layout of surviving burgage plots and would not injure or interfere with any archaeological remains which may be present on site. The proposed development would therefore be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The Newcastle - Lyons Local Area Plan 2003, sets out a detailed vision for expansion of the existing village of Newcastle, to facilitate development that integrates with the character and built form of the village. Section 6.3 of the Plan describes in detail the main organising elements for development within the 'village core' having specific regard to block layout, building heights, architectural styles, and street types. Figure 6.1 of the Plan sets out the overall development strategy with regard to principal acess roads, link roads, service roads, walking and cycling routes and landscape squares. In particular, the proposed location of Block A fronting onto Main Street takes no cognisance of the proposed main Newcastle village Square detailed in Local Area Plan. The proposed development would therefore be contrary to the provisions and objectives of the Newcastle /Lyons Local Area Plan, adopted 2003. || The proposed development would set an undesirable precedent for other similar developments, which would in themselves and cumulatively be harmful to the visual and residential amenities of Newcastle village and be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The proposed layout would give rise to a poor quality substandard form of development with inadequate provision of semi-private amenity space and poor provision of public open space. The open space proposed is poorly distributed and not easily accessible; there is a lack of provision for incidental (kick about) areas and adequate provision has not been made for children's play areas throughout the scheme. The proposed development would, therefore provide a poor standard of amenity space for future residents. The proposed development would be contrary to the South Dublin County Development Plan 2004-2010, and as such would be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The position of the proposed north-south link road adjacent to the western boundary of the site and the layout and block pattern at the southern end of the site, would compromise the ability to comprehensively develop the zoned lands surrounding the site in a manner that would meet the objectives of the Newcastle - Lyons Local Area Plan, adopted 2003. It is considered that in particular, the exclusion from the site of a very narrow strip of land located between proposed north-south road edge and adjoining lands to the west, would prejudice the development of lands to the west and the provision of frontage development on both sides of the street. The proposed development would result in a piecemeal development with a multiplicity of accesses on to Main Street. The proposed development would therefore be contrary to the provisions and objectives of the Newcastle - Lyons Local Area Plan, adopted 2003, and would not be consistent with the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || Having regard to design and location of Block A, the proposed development would result in significant overshadowing and overlooking of neighbouring two-storey dwellings located to the east of the site. The proposed development would seriously injure the amenities, and depreciate the value, of these properties, and would not be consistent with the proper planning and sustainable development of the area.

Having regard to the A1 zoning objective for the site, ‘to provide for new Residential Communities in accordance with Approved Area Plans’, the fact that the lands are not within the boundaries of the Rathcoole Local Area Plan 2002 as adopted and the central location of the development within a landbank of similarly zoned lands, the proposed development of 54 no. dwellings is considered to be premature pending the preparation and approval of an area plan for these newly zoned lands. Therefore, the proposal materially contravenes the zoning objective for these lands and is contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || Having regard to the Sustainable Residential Development in Urban Areas published by the Department of the Environment and Local Government in 2008 and the South Dublin Development Plan 2004 – 2010, it is considered that by reason of its design and layout (including public open space and private amenity areas) that the proposed development would provide an unacceptable quality of residential environment for future residents of the development. The proposed development would, therefore be contrary to the Sustainable Residential Development in Urban Areas and the South Dublin Development Plan 2004 – 2010 and the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || Access arrangement to the site is via a roundabout and spur from the proposed Rathcoole Distributor Road. Construction has not commenced on the proposed new distributor road and no start date for this road has been set. The development of the kind proposed would be premature pending the construction and operation of the Distributor Road for the area. Additionally, the section of roadway from the junction with the proposed roundabout to the proposed vehicular access to the site is not shown on any approved road plans for this area. As such, the proposed development is premature pending the determination by the Planning Authority of a road layout for the area, including link roads from the approved Distributor Road. The proposed development would, therefore be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area.

The proposed development would extend across lands at the foothills of the Dublin Mountains that rise from circa 115 metres over datum (OD) to circa 125 metres OD. The ridge height of 2 storey dwellings along the uppermost (south-east) boundary of the site would range from between 128 metres to 132 metres OD and the ridge height of 6 no. 2.5 storey dwellings located adjacent to the 120 metre contour would be circa 129 metres over datum. In the context of the prominent positioning of the site on an elevated hillside and the quantum of dwellings proposed above the 120 metre contour (within an area of circa 1.5 hectares) the proposed dwellings would be visually dominant and excessively obtrusive when viewed from the surrounding area. The proposal would also result in an inappropriate abrupt transition in scale at the interface between the suburban fringe and the Dublin Mountains area. The proposed development would therefore be at variance with the South Dublin County Council Development Plan (2004-2010) Objectives to protect the visual and passive open amenity of areas above the 120 metre contour in the Dublin Mountains, avoid abrupt transitions in scale in transitional areas especially those that would be detrimental to environmentally sensitive zones and safeguard protected views (especially those designated along Killakee Road and Stocking Lane). This would also be at variance with the objectives of the Ballycullen-Oldcourt Area Plan, which sets out to limit the height and scale of development around the 120 meter contour to an extent that it would not be unduly obtrusive on this part of the urban fringe. On the basis of the above, the proposed development would materially contravene the ‘A1’ Development Plan zoning objective of the site, which sets out ‘to provide for new Residential Communities in accordance with Approved Area Plans’, and would interfere with the rural character of the landscape and protected views of special amenity value. || The extended area of the application site rises from the north-west to the south east across a relatively steep hillside with a slope of circa 12.5% (1:8). The proposed development would provide for the extension of 2 no. permitted cul-de-sacs (Road 12 and Road 10) and the creation of 2 no. new cul de sacs (Road 14A and Road || that would all run perpendicular to and through the contours of the site along a north-west south-east axis. Each road would include large areas of surface parking (2 no. for each house) on either side and would be flanked by rectangular arrangements of dwellings that would also be orientated through the contours of the site. The proposal would involve significant alterations to the topography of the site including the cutting of significant and intrusive platforms into the hillside. Engineering drawings submitted also indicate that extensive embankments and retaining walls would be placed at the end of each of the extended and new cul- de-sacs. It is also proposed to remove the entire of a hedgerow that traverses the extended area of application site and remove the majority of a common hedgerows and trees located along the western boundary, which is the subject of a South Dublin County Council Development Plan 2004-2010 objective to protect and preserve. Such a development would be at variance with the Development Plan Objectives to protect the visual and passive open amenity of areas above the 120 metre contour in the Dublin Mountains and contravene Policy LHA 9, which sets out to preserve trees, groups of trees or woodlands that form a significant feature in the landscape or are important in setting the character of an area. This would also be at variance with the Ballycullen-Oldcourt Area Plan (2000) objective to retain and augment mature trees surrounding the lands of the Former Cats and Dogs Home (DSPA). On the basis of the above the proposal would materially contravene the zoning objective of the application site, which sets out ‘to provide for new Residential Communities in accordance with Approved Area Plans’. || The proposed development fails to comply with the urban design criteria as identified in Chapter 3 of the guidelines on ‘Sustainable Residential Development in Urban Areas’ (2008) in terms of context, inclusivity, distinctiveness, layout, public realm, and detailed design by reason of: - The orientation of the proposed development through the contours of the steep site and the subsequent cutting of significant and intrusive platforms into the hillside with the erection of extensive embankments and retaining walls along the uppermost (south-east) boundary; - The repetitive mock ‘Tudor’ design of proposed dwellings, which would fail to contribute to the character and identify of the area; - The visual obtrusiveness of palisade fencing proposed along the majority of the south-east boundary; - The grouping of dwellings around long cul-de-sacs that would create monotonous streetscapes with no urban structure/hierarchy of spaces, form barriers to movement, fail to achieve a sense of place and fail to achieve active surveillance; - The provision of residual open spaces with no clear role or function; - The provision of pedestrian routes that would not be adequately surveyed; - The arrangement of dwellings (2 no.) along the western boundary of the site that would gable with blank elevations and blank rear garden walls onto open space to the west, which would create a negative aspect onto said area with a lack of passive surveillance and articulation. The Guidelines clearly state that where design is of such poor quality as to result in a substandard housing environment, permission should be refused. On this basis the proposed development would be contrary to said Ministerial Guidelines, which were issued to Planning Authorities under Section 28 of the Planning and Development Act, 2000 (as amended), and would materially contravene the 'A1' South Dublin County Council Development Plan (2004) zoning objective of the application site, which sets out ‘to provide for new Residential Communities in accordance with Approved Area Plans’. || The proposed 10 year permission would alter and extend Precinct 4 as permitted under the application site's extant 10 year parent permission (SD04A/0393 & PL 06S.212191). Condition no. 2 of that permission specifically stated that precinct 4 shall form Phase 1 (of 3) of the overall development. The parent permission was granted in April 2005 and there are approximately 6 years remaining to complete the Phases. The applicant has failed to justify the duration of permission (up until 2019) for the subject area of the application site (Precinct 4), which would be at variance with said condition and would allow for the piecemeal development on the applicants lands. Within this context the proposed duration of permission would be contrary to the achievement of orderly development and would contravene materially a condition attached to an existing permission for development. || The proposal includes for dwellings that would not meet the relevant standards under Section 11.11 of the South Dublin County Council Development Plan (2004) in terms of minimum required dwelling unit sizes (90 sq.m for 3 bedroom houses) and minimum required private amenity space (60 sq.m for 3 bedroom houses and 70 sq.m for 4 bedroom houses). The proposed dwellings (16 no. total) that fail to meet the requirements would therefore be substandard in terms of residential amenity and would materially contravene the zoning objective of the application site, which sets out ‘to provide for new Residential Communities in accordance with Approved Area Plans’. || A large proportion of additional proposed public open space (0.283 hectares) would be located on the opposite side of a Stocking Avenue (primary distributor road) and over 300 metres (as the crow flies) from the nearest of the proposed new dwellings. This area of public open space would be isolated from the proposed new houses and would not contribute to their public open space requirements. Circa 8.9% (0.187 hectares) of the extended area of the application site would relate to usable public open space located in and around the proposed new dwellings. Within the context of the South Dublin County Council Development Plan 2004-2010 minimum public open space requirement of 14% of gross area on lands zoned 'Objective A1’, the proposed development would fail to provide the quantity and quality of amenity that is necessary to serve the proposed new dwellings. The proposal would also result in an imbalance in terms of the distribution of public open space across the overall development lands with the larger quantum of dwellings located on the south side of Stocking Avenue having a smaller share of public open space. This aspect of the proposal would therefore materially contravene the ‘A1’ zoning objective of the application site, which sets out ‘to provide for new Residential Communities in accordance with Approved Area Plans’. || The proposed development would increase the number of dwellings on the applicant’s overall lands by 64 no., which would generally be of a size and type that caters for families. Based on the requirements of the ‘Childcare Facilities – Guidelines for Planning Authorities, 2001', the proposal would generate a minimum demand for an additional 17 childcare spaces (20 childcare places per approximately 75 dwellings). It is noted that the applicant has been granted permission for an amended 2 storey commercial/community centre (SD07A/0628) as part of the development of the overall application lands, which includes for a crèche facility that would provide for 112 childcare spaces. The childcare requirement of the dwellings permitted (799) on the overall application lands, however, equates to circa 213 childcare spaces and significantly exceeds the existing permitted childcare provision. Within this context, the proposal fails to provide for the additional quantum of childcare spaces that would be required under the Childcare Guidelines to serve the proposed additional houses and would therefore be contrary to Ministerial guidelines, which were issued to planning authorities under Section 28 of the Planning and Development Act, 2000 (as amended). Such a development would also materially contravene the 'A1' South Dublin County Council Development Plan (2004) zoning objective of the application site, which sets out ‘to provide for new Residential Communities in accordance with Approved Area Plans’. || The proposed and extended cul-de-sacs would cut through/ run perpendicular to the contours of the site along a north-west south-east axis and would all have longitudinal gradients of CIRCA 8%. In the context of the recommendations of the ‘Design Manual for Roads and Bridges’ (NRA; 1992), which sets out a minimum gradient as 5%, the proposed road gradients would be hazardous to road users especially in the area of the application site where altitudes are conducive to heavy frosts and icy conditions in winter. The proposed development would therefore endanger public safety by reason of traffic hazard.

The applicant has failed to provide details relating to the impact of the proposed development on the current biodiversity resource of the site. In the absence of this information, the proposed development, if permitted, could have a negative impact on the surrounding environment and would be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The proposed development adjoins a number of dwellings which are protected structures under the South Dublin County Development Plan 2004–2010 (Reference 306). It is considered that the visual impact of the proposed development, by reason of its height, size, bulk, scale and design, would interfere with the architectural integrity of the protected structures and detract from the established character and setting. The proposed development would, therefore, be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || Inadequate information has been submitted regarding the exact location and separation distance of the proposed building from the 24inch diameter public watermain owned by Dublin City Council that traverses the site and also with regards to a written agreement allowing future access to the watermain for inspection and maintenance. Thus the proposed development may be prejudicial to public health. || The proposed pharmacy would be located approximately 0.5 metres from a 4inch public watermain when the minimum required setback is 3 metres. Furthermore the diversion of the existing public 150mm foul sewer, which is already at capacity, to facilitate the location of the proposed pharmacy, would reduce the capacity of the sewer. The proximity of the proposed pharmacy to a public watermain and the proposed diversion of the foul sewer would be prejudicial to public health and contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The subject site is located in an area zoned ‘A’ in the South Dublin County Development Plan 2004–2010, the objective of which is to ‘protect and/or improve residential amenity’. It is considered that the proposed development, by reason of its proximity to adjoining dwellings, significant height, scale and mass, its orientation and its poor quality open space for future residents/visitors/employees, would seriously injure the established residential amenity of adjoining property owners as well as the residential amenity of future occupants of the development. The proposed development would, therefore, contravene the zoning objective for the site and be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The applicant has failed to provide information relating to the trip generation associated with the proposed development to allow the Planning Authority to assess the impact of the proposed development on the adjoining road network. In the absence of this information, it is considered that the proposed development could therefore endanger public safety by reason of a traffic hazard and could give rise to serious traffic congestion.

Having regard to the established pattern of development in the area and the character of Cloverhill Road, it is considered that the design, height and scale of proposed development on the eastern portion of the site, annotated 'Cloverhill Estate' and 'Eastern Estate' on site layout map, would be inappropriate, unsympathetic and significantly out of character with development in the area. The proposed development on the eastern portion of the site would fail to respond to its context or integrate successfully with its immediate and surrounding built environment. The proposed development on the eastern portion of the site does not integrate with adjoining area of Palmerstown Woods. The proposed three-storey development with external access stairs along Cloverhill Road frontage, with the external staircases fronting the street, would be visually dominant and obtrusive in the area. As such, the proposed development on the eastern portion of the site would seriously injure the amenities of the area and would be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The South Dublin County Council Development Plan 2004-2010 seeks to promote high quality residential development of appropriate density and design. The design and quality of development proposed at 'Cloverhill Estate' and 'Eastern Estate' on the eastern section of the overall site are poor and would provide a poor living environment for future residents, with unacceptable layout and external stair access, inadequate private open space provision and very long walking distances between car parking spaces and residential units. || The proposed development on the eastern portion of the overall site, annotated 'Cloverhill Estate' and 'Eastern Estate' on site layout map, would set an undesirable precedent for other similar developments, which would in themselves and cumulatively be harmful to the residential amenities of the area and be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area.

Inadequate information has been submitted regarding the foul and surface water provision for the proposed development. Thus the proposed development, if permitted, may be prejudicial to public health and contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || Having regard to the pattern of development in the area, it is considered that the proposed development, by reason of the scale, mass and bulk, would seriously injure the residential amenity of the adjoining properties by reason of overbearing impact. Furthermore, taking into consideration the location of the proposed play area, the overlooking of private amenity space of future occupants of Silveracre House, the mix of dwelling units proposed, the proposed development would provide a poor level of amenity of future occupants. The proposed development would therefore seriously injure the amenities of and depreciate the value of property in the vicinity and would be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area || The proposed development is located in the curtilage of a Protected Structure (Silveracre House) as designated in the current Development Plan for the area, Map Reference No. 277. It is considered that the proposed development by reason of its excessive scale, mass and bulk, when taken in conjunction with its location proximate to the Protected Structure, would severely compromise the architectural integrity of the building, would seriously detract from the character and setting of special interest of the Protected Structure. Furthermore, in the absence of further details regarding the proposed underpinning of Silveracre House to accommodate the basement car parking, the proposed development, the proposed development may undermine the existing built fabric of the Protected Structure and therefore, be contrary to the proper planning and development of the area, including the protection of its architectural heritage.

The site of the proposed development is zoned objective ‘A’ - “to protect and/or improve residential amenity”, and also has a Local Zoning Objective LC - ‘to provide for and/or improve Local Centre facilities’, as detailed in both the current South Dublin County Council Development Plan 2004-2010, and also in the South Dublin County Council Draft Development Plan 2010-2016. The proposed development comprising of an exclusively residential development would preclude the comprehensive development of Local Centre facilities at this location and would therefore materially contravene this Local Centre Objective. The proposed development would, therefore, be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The proposed development does not comply with the urban design criteria as identified in the ‘Sustainable Residential Development in Urban Areas’ Guidelines (Department of Environment, Heritage and Local Government, 2008) in terms of context, inclusivity, distinctiveness, layout, public realm, and detailed design by reason of the following: (a) The visual and physical barrier of the proposed perimeter wall to the development which would preclude the provision of an active street frontage onto Willsbrook Road and Mount Bellew Way, (b) Lack of permeability within the scheme and between the proposed development and surrounding area, (c) Arrangement of public open space provision within the proposed development. The proposed residential development would, therefore represents a substandard form of development for future residents. The proposed development would seriously injure the amenities of the area and would be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The proposed development would set an undesirable precedent for other similar developments, which would in themselves and cumulatively be harmful to the residential amenities of the area and be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area.

The proposed development provides a 6 storey elevation to its northern elevation. Given that the application site is located in an outer suburban area that does not have access to high quality public transport the proposed development would be contrary to the policy requirements of Section 11.11.3 of the Development Plan 2004 – 2010 which states that ‘Baseline building height should be not greater than five storeys, including penthouse setbacks. Deviations from the baseline may be considered within designated Town and District Centres and where there is high quality public transport (Luas and Rail) where amenities can be maintained’. The proposal would therefore materially contravene the South Dublin County Council Development plan 2004 - 2010 and would be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The proposed development is located on an elevated site and on a prominent corner junction. The scale and overall height of the proposed development, Block 13, would be visually dominant and excessively obtrusive when viewed from the surrounding streetscape, particularly when viewed on approach in a southerly direction along the Ballycullen road and on approach in a westerly direction along the east/west distributor road. || Having regard to the elevated topography of the site, the increase in the building height of Block 13 would impact significantly on the public realm to the north of the proposed development Block 13 and the amenity value of the area of public open space to the north-east of the application site as required under SD03A/0972 by way of seasonal overshadowing and overbearing impact. Such development would be contrary to the policy requirements Section 11.11.4 of the Development Plan 2004 – 2010 which refers to Overshadowing and Overlooking and states that ‘The height and/or bulk of a proposed development may not compromise the existing amenity of adjoining sites’. The proposed development would, therefore, seriously injure the amenities of the area and of property in the vicinity and would be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area.

Proposed nursing home not located in existing premises, materially contravening zoning objective to protect high amenity area. || Development fails to protect and enhance wildlife habitat diversity, lacks ecological survey, and disrupts Dodder Valley Linear Park objectives. || Site contamination from unauthorized waste disposal with no acceptable remediation plan or risk assessment provided. || Scale, extent, and massing of building is excessive and visually obtrusive, eroding character and amenity of Dodder Valley.

decision: REFUSE EXT. OF DURATION OF PERMISSION
reasons_joined: Since December 2012, the Newcastle Local Area Plan is the basis for South Dublin County Council to consider future development in this area. The Plan provides detailed guidance relating to the proper planning and sustainable development of Newcastle Village, including density, dwelling mix, building height and burgage hedges. The development permitted under SD10A/0017 (PL06S.237827) would materially contravene specific objectives of the Local Area Plan as follows: (i) The site is not identified as being a location for apartments, (ii) the dwelling mix of houses and apartments does not comply with the requirement to largely provide terraced houses (with opportunities for detached and semi-detached houses) (Objective PN12), (iii) building heights are greater than the maximum permissible in the village (Objective BF8), (iv) the layout does not adequately retain existing burgage hedges (Objective BN1), (v) A specific objective is required to provide a connection to the Glebe Estate (Objective PN7). Therefore, there have been significant changes in the development objectives in the Development Plan (Newcastle Local Area Plan) since the date of the permission (30th June 2011), such that the development would no longer be consistent with the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. Thus, the proposed development would materially contravene Section 42(1)(a)(ii)(II) of the Planning and Development Act, 2000 (as amended).

On the basis of the infromation submitted with the application the Planning Authority is not satisfied that the management and disposal of surface water on the site is appropriate for the scale and quantum of the proposed development. Therefore the proposed development is considered to be prejudical to public health, the protection of the environment and contrary to the proper planning and development of the area.
