1) The subdivided apartments that the applicant proposes to retain fail to meet the current minimum standards as set out under 'Sustainable Urban Housing: Design Standards for Apartments' (2007) in terms of aggregate living areas, aggregate bedroom areas, storage space and main apartment balconies. The subdivided apartments therefore provide a poor standard of residential amenity and permission for the retention of such would be contrary to Ministerial Guidelines issued under Section 28 of the Planning and Development Act 2000 (as amended) and would also materially contravene the 'A' zoning objective of the application site, which sets out to protect/and or improve residential amenity under the South Dublin County Council Development Plan (2010 - 2016). || The proposed retention of sub-divided apartments would increase demand on existing sparse semi-private amenity space on the application site that is of a substandard quality and would also result in the removal of an internal communal seating and balcony areas in a manner that detracts from the residential and semi-private amenity of the subject apartment block. Furthermore, the gated development in which the subject block is located has no access to public open space. 2) The proposed subdivision and creation of additional apartments therefore contravenes Policy SN26 of the South Dublin County Council Development Plan (2010 - 2016), which requires each dwelling to be provided with adequate usable semi-private amenity space that meets prescribed qualities, and Section 7.9 of ‘Sustainable Residential Development in Urban Areas’ (2008), which states that the provision of usable outdoor space for families in apartment schemes should be prioritised and such spaces should be provided in the form of landscaped areas. || Section 3.3.1 of ‘Childcare Facilities – Guidelines for Planning Authorities’ (June 2001) sets out a standard of 1 childcare facility providing a minimum of 20 childcare places per approximately 75 dwellings. 3) The proposed sub-division of apartments increases demand for childcare on a site where there is an absence of a childcare facility and where 100 dwellings have been permitted since the adoption of the said Childcare Facilities Guidelines. An increase in the number of apartments on the application site in the absence of a childcare facility would therefore be contrary to Ministerial Guidelines issued under Section 28 of the Planning and Development Act 2000 (as amended) and the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. Such a development would also materially contravene the 'A' zoning objective of the application site, which sets out to protect/and or improve residential amenity under the South Dublin County Council Development Plan (2010 - 2016).

Having regard to the location of the proposed development within an existing established residential area, in a cul de sac with a narrow approach road, and to the provisions of the South Dublin County Development Plan in relation to car parking requirements, it is considered that the inadequate car parking provision would result in on-street car parking which would endanger public safety by reason of traffic hazard and its layout would result in car parking crossing an area of walkway which would create traffic congestion and obstruction of road users of roads within the area. The proposed development would, therefore, endanger public safety by reason of traffic hazard and would be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The proposed development would set an undesirable precedent for other similar developments, which would in themselves and cumulatively be harmful to the residential amenities of the area and be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || Having regard to the provisions of Section 1.4.29.ii of the South Dublin County Council Development Plan 2010-2016 and the Quality Housing for Sustainable Communities-Best Practice Guidelines (DOEHLG 2007) and ‘Sustainable Urban Housing: Design Standards for New Apartments’(2007), with particular reference to proposed internal layout, and floor areas and also having regard to inadequate car parking provision, it is considered that the proposed residential development represents a substandard form of development, and would be unacceptable with regard to the residential amenity of future residents. In addition the proposed development of 11 residential units to replace existing bungalow would constitute overdevelopment of the site and would fail to integrate with existing residential development in the vicinity. The proposed development would seriously injure the residential amenities of the area and would depreciate the value of property in the vicinity and would be contrary to the A zoning objective of the site 'to protect and improve residential amenity' as set out in South Dublin County Development Plan 2010-2016 . The proposed development would therefore, be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area.

When viewed from the graveyard to the north, the proposal would be visually obtrusive and out of character with surrounding buildings (which are no higher than two storey) and the graveyard context. This is due to the three storey height of the proposal and its proximity (4 to 5m) from the graveyard wall. || Having regard to the Quality Housing for Sustainable Communities-Best Practice Guidelines, (Department of the Environment, Heritage and Local Government, 2007) and the South Dublin County Council Development Plan 2010 - 2016, the proposed private amenity space provision would be significantly less than the minimum requirements for duplex units. The proposed dwellings, therefore, represent a substandard form of development, and would be unacceptable with regard to the residential amenity of the future residents of the dwellings. The proposed development would be contrary to this Ministerial guideline issued to planning authorities under section 28 of the Planning and Development Act 2000 (as amended). Thus, the proposed development would, therefore, be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The proposed residential development on a backland village centre location does not comply with the urban design criteria as identified in the ‘Sustainable Residential Development in Urban Areas’ Guidelines (Department of Environment, Heritage and Local Government, 2008) in terms of context, inclusivity, distinctiveness, layout, public realm, and detailed design by reason of the following: (a) Lack of permeability within the scheme and between the proposed development and surrounding area as a result of a gated entrance, (b) Poor location and amount of public open space, (c) over dominance of car parking in the centre of the scheme which erodes any creation of a sense of place. The proposed residential development would, therefore seriously injure the amenities of property in the vicinity and would be contrary to the ‘LC' zoning objective of the site, ‘to protect, provide for and/or improve Local Centre facilities’, as set out in South Dublin County Council Development Plan (2010-2016) and would, therefore, be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area.

The 63 dwellings proposed would represent residential large scale development in the form of long term rental accommodation. The area in which the site is located is zoned B – "To protect and improve Rural Amenity and to provide for the development of Agriculture". These rurally zoned lands are also a part of the future land bank for the sustainable growth of the Dublin Metropolitan Area as outlined in Section 2.2 of the Regional Planning Guidelines for the Greater Dublin Area, and Section 0.2 - Core Strategy of the County Development Plan 2010 – 2016. Having regard to the absence of compliance with the Rural Housing Strategy which applies to all forms of residential development on B-zoned rural lands, it is considered that the proposed development of 63 dwellings would represent an uncontrolled form of urban generated residential development in that occupants are not proposed to be or could not be restricted to those who have close links to the rural community. This would represent provision of relatively large scale residential development on rurally zoned lands that would be an unsustainable use of the future land bank as identified in the Regional Planning Guidelines for the Greater Dublin Area. The proposed development would therefore materially contravene the Core Strategy of the County Development Plan 2010 – 2016 which seeks to control rural housing in order to allow for more compact and sustainable urban form in the future as set out in both the Regional Planning Guidelines for the Greater Dublin Area and the South Dublin Development Plan . The proposed development would, therefore, not be in accordance with the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The proposed development of 63 dwellings would represent long term residential development which would not be compliant with Policy H30 Rural Housing Policies and Local Need Criteria of the County Development Plan which seeks to control urban generated rural housing and Policy H31 Rural Amenity and Agricultural Zone which controls the relevant persons to whom rural housing can be permitted. These policies are the effective planning control on unsustainable development of the rural land bank of the Metropolitan Area as defined in the Regional Planning Guidelines for the Greater Dublin Area. The proposed development which provide for long term rental accommodation to persons who would not comply with Policy H31 would undermine the effective implementation of the Planning Authorities rural housing policy which would materially contravene the zoning objective and set an undesirable precedent for rural development within the B –zoned lands in the County. The proposed development would, therefore, not be in accordance with the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The proposed development of 63 dwellings would allow for a development of 14 units to the hectare on a 4.49 hectare rurally zoned site. Having regard to the sub-urban appearance of the bungalow housing units which display a large floorplate and the clustering of the dwellings in the northern section of the site, thereby extending the urban edge of Newcastle, it is considered that the development of 63 dwellings would represent an incongruous sub-urban type development on rural landscape and which would impact on the rural landscape character as reflected in the zoning of the land. The proposed development would, therefore, be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The proposed development would result in the provision of leisure facilities which are an intrinsic part of the development. The proposed accommodation of the leisure facilities on B – rural zoned lands outside of the Specific Local Objective lands is an indication of the overdevelopment of these lands and would extend the visual impact of the development further into the rural landscape, with consequent erosion of the landscape character of the rural area and the zoning of the lands. The proposed development would, therefore, be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The proposed development of 63 dwellings would represent a large scale and long term residential development which would not be compliant with Specific Local Objective 94 adopted as a variation to the County Development Plan on the 12th December 2011. The minutes of Special Meeting (Planning) of South Dublin County Council held on 12th December 2011 during which the variation was debated and adopted state that clarification was requested during the debate by the Mayor, Cllr. C. Jones in respect of assessment of any future planning application as a result of the adoption of the variation. The minutes clearly report the response of the then Director of Services for Planning:- "Director of Services, Mr. F. Nevin confirmed that the variation did not change the underlying zoning of the land and the zoning and the relevant policies relating to same would form part of the assessment of any such planning application." The proposed development of 63 dwellings would be of a form, scale and in a location considered to materially contravene the policies referred to in the public record of the meeting, i.e.; Policy H30 Rural Housing Policies and Local Need Criteria of the County Development Plan which seeks to control urban generated rural housing and Policy H31 Rural Amenity and Agricultural Zone which controls the relevant persons to whom rural housing can be permitted. These policies are a key planning control on unsustainable development of the rural land bank of the Metropolitan Area as defined in the Regional Planning Guidelines for the Greater Dublin Area. The proposed development would undermine the effective implementation of the Planning Authority’s rural housing policy which would materially contravene the zoning objective and set an undesirable precedent for similar rural development within the B –zoned lands, would not comply with policy H31 and would undermine the effective implementation of the Planning Authority's rural housing policy which would materially contravene the zoning objective and set and undesireable precedent for rural development with the B zoned lands in the County. The proposed development would, therefore, not be in accordance with the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || Inadequate details regarding drainage or SuDS have been submitted. Given the scale, location and form of the proposed development of 63 dwellings the Planning Authority considers that without satisfactory details on the sizes of the impermeable areas or details that the proposed surface water attenuation storage facilities are sufficiently sized to cater for the development in addition to the proposed removal of substantial amounts of existing land drains, the applicants have not demonstrated that the proposed development would not give rise to seriously adverse surface water drainage impacts downstream of the site. The proposed development would, therefore, not be in accordance with the proper planning and sustainable development of the area.

Having regard to the objective for reservation of a site for a primary school contained in the South Dublin County Development Plan 2010-2016 and the Saggart Action Area Plan (2000), it is considered that the development as proposed would not be in accordance with the proper planning and sustainable development of the area as the reserved site shown on the submitted revised drawing PP01H is inadequate for a 16 classroom school as required by the Department of Education and Skills. The proposal would therefore contravene an objective of the South Dublin County Development Plan 2010-2016. || The proposed layout does not facilitate removal of a lesser number of units to achieve the required 1.2ha school site without resulting in a disjointed urban block with exposed gable ends and rear gardens and which would not achieve acceptable standards of urban design as required under the Guidelines for Planning Authorities on Sustainable Residential Development in Urban Areas, 2009. Removal of the stated units allows for the submission of a future planning application for residential development which provides a suitable interface with the school site.

Council policy states that any change of use permitted for purpose built childcare facilities in new developments will be temporary in nature and for community purposes only. Such policy is set out in Policy SCR33: Change of use of Purpose Built Childcare Facilities of the South Dublin County Council Development Plan 2010 - 2016. The proposed dwellings will be a permanent change of use of a purposely designed childcare facility and this will not result in a community purpose use. The proposed change of use would materially contravene this policy. Therefore, the proposed development would be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The proposed development of residential units at locations where residential use was considered unacceptable in terms of traffic safety, residential and visual amenities, would materially contravene Conditions 2(b) and 2(d) of the permission granted by Bord Pleanála Ref No PL06S.217573 SD06A/0107 and extended by SD06A/0107/EP. || Council policy seeks to ensure single aspect dwelling units and associated private amenity spaces are not exclusively north facing. Such policy is set out in the South Dublin County Council Development Plan 2010 - 2016 in Sections 1.4.18.i Layout and Orientation and 1.4.18.iv Dual Aspect, and Policy SN27: Private Amenity Space. Such policy is also set out in the Tallaght Town Centre Local Area Plan 2006, in Section 5.3.4 Dwelling Size and Layout and Section 5.3.6 Energy Efficiency, Passive Solar Design and Recycling. Having regard to the significant proportion of apartments which are single aspect and with a north orientation, the proposed development represents a substandard form of development, and would be unacceptable with regard to the residential amenity of the future residents of the dwellings and would materially contravene the above polices and objectives in both the County Development Plan and Local Area Plan. Therefore, the proposed development would be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area.

The proposed residential development does not comply with the urban design criteria as identified in the ‘Sustainable Residential Development in Urban Areas’ Guidelines (Department of Environment, Heritage and Local Government, 2008) in terms of context, inclusivity, distinctiveness, layout, public realm, and detailed design by reason of the following: (a) Its isolation from surrounding communities (b) The lack of connectivity to basic services (c) High levels of car dependence (d) Poor interface with adjoining lands and the lack of security and surveillance to adjoining lands (e) Low levels of amenity for future residents The proposed residential development would, therefore represent a substandard form of development and would seriously injure the amenities of the area. The proposed development is of poor quality and would materially contravene the South Dublin County Council Development Plan (2010-2016) 'A' zoning objective of the application site, which sets out ‘to protect and/or improve residential amenity’; and would, therefore, be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || Having regard to the provisions of Section 1.4.29.ii of the South Dublin County Council Development Plan 2010-2016 and the Quality Housing for Sustainable Communities-Best Practice Guidelines (DOEHLG 2007). The proposed private amenity space provision for Dwellings 9, 8 and 7 would be significantly less than the minimum requirements for two- storey four bedroom houses. Furthermore having regard to the provisions of the South Dublin County Development Plan, with particular reference to car parking requirements, the proposed development would, therefore, be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. The proposed development therefore, would represent a substandard form of development, and would be unacceptable with regard to the residential amenity of the future residents of the dwellings. As such the proposed development would be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area.. || The development as proposed would have a detrimental impact on the 225mm diameter watermain which is located along the southern boundary of the site and would therefore, prejudicial to public health and would be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The proposed development would set an undesirable precedent for other similar developments, which would in themselves and cumulatively be harmful to the residential amenities of the area and be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area.

The proposed development would provide 10 no. duplex dwelling units on a site of 0.124 hectares, this equates to a gross density of approximately 80 dwellings per hectare. Section 1.2.14.viii Policy H8 Outer Suburban/ ‘Greenfield’ Sites Densities of the South Dublin County Council Development Plan 2010 – 2016 requires density values far less than this. Furthermore, Section 5.11 of the Sustainable Residential Developments in Urban Areas - Guidelines for Planning Authorities 2008 recommends that a density of 35-50 dwellings per hectare be provided in outer suburban sites. Given the location of the proposed development outside of a designated Town or District Centre in the South Dublin County Council area and the existing density of development in the surrounding area characterised by low density housing comprised of detached and semi-detached dwellings, the density of the proposed development at approximately 80 dwellings per hectare is excessively high. Such density would be contrary to the density requirements of Section 1.2.14.viii of the Development Plan and Section 5.11 of the Sustainable Residential Developments in Urban Areas Guidelines 2008. || Having regard to the established pattern of the development immediately adjacent to either side of the subject site which comprises single storey dwellings and the separation distance provided between the proposed development and adjacent dwellings to either side of the subject site, it is considered that the height of the proposed 3 storey duplex units would be visually obtrusive and would detract from the character and visual amenity of the surrounding streetscape. Such development would be contrary to the policy requirements of Section 1.4.16 of the South Dublin County Council Development Plan 2010 – 2016 which refers to ‘Building Heights’. || (a) Having regard to the context, configuration and orientation of the site and the height, scale and extent of the proposed blocks along the western side boundary of the site shared with existing dwellings; the proposal would adversely impact on the residential amenities of the dwellings by way of overshadowing and overbearing impact. Such development would materially contravene the requirements of Section 1.4.18.i Layout and Orientation of the South Dublin County Council Development Plan 2010 – 2016 (b) Given the narrow separation distance between the front and rear elevations of the proposed blocks and the opposing retaining walls at lower ground floor level and the depth of the lower ground floor units 1.4 metres below existing ground level, such development would adversely affect levels of daylight and sunlight which would reach habitable rooms associated with the proposed duplex units at lower ground floor level. This would result in a sub-standard form of development. (c) A separation distance of 11.6 metres is proposed between the rear/southern elevation of the proposed block containing duplex units no.’s 5 & 6 and the front/northern elevation of the proposed block containing duplex units no.’s 7 – 10. This materially contravenes the requirements of Section 1.4.18.iii of the South Dublin County Council Development Plan 2010 – 2016 which states ‘A distance of 22m is required between opposing above ground floor windows’. (d) Insufficient private amenity space has been afforded to each unit. Table 1.4.2 of the South Dublin County Council Development Plan 2010 – 2016 states that duplex units are assessed as ‘houses’. The proposed units do meet the requirement to provide the minimum required private amenity space of 48 sq.m. for a 1 bedroom house and 55 sq.m for a 2 bedroom house. The private amenity space provided for the proposed duplex units materially contravene the minimum private amenity space requirements of Policy SN25 of the South Dublin County Council Development Plan 2010 – 2016. Such development would adversely impact the residential amenity of existing properties and the future occupants of the proposed dwellings. All of these factors contribute to a poor standard of design and such development would materially contravene the requirements of Section 1.4 Sustainable Neighbourhoods of the South Dublin County Council Development Plan 2010 – 2016 and would contravene the zoning objective of the area which seeks ‘To protect and/or improve Residential Amenity’.

The submission does not form part of an overall proposal for the provision of retail and roads infrastructure, etc., which was stated as being a requirement of any further planning applications under Condition 3 of SD14A/0057. The proposed development would therefore represent further ad-hoc development of a residential estate, would materially contravene Condition 3 of SD14A/0057 and would be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The proposed development, which would represent further amendments to a significantly completed estate with a large number of occupied dwellings, is premature due to the demonstrable lack of usable landscaped open space as required by Condition 5 and 6 of SD14A/0057, having regard to the total lack of any open space provision within the estate to date. The proposed development would, therefore, exacerbate the inadequate residential amenity on the estate and would be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The last assessment of noise in this section of the site took place in 2007 and related to two storey houses. The proposed amendments would result in three storey houses with greater potential for exposure to noise from the N7. The applicant has not demonstrated that the proposed amended dwelling-types would comply with Policy ES23 of the South Dublin County Development Plan, 2010-2016, through the provision of sound impact assessment and mitigation measures and that residential amenity would not be significantly negatively-impacted by development proximate to the N7. As such, the proposal would materially contravene an objective of the Development Plan. || Inadequate public lighting details for the proposed development were submitted. The Planning Authority is not satisfied that adequate provision has been made for a Public Lighting Scheme for the development to provide for high quality public lighting throughout the public realm of the site, prepared to BS5489:2013 and the SDCC Specification for Public Lighting Installations in Residential and Industrial Developments: February 1997, along with appropriate Lighting and Electrical designs for a suitable public lighting scheme.

Having regard to Draft Tree Preservation Order (Lock Road, Lucan – Planning Register Reference Number TPO/0005), initiated under Section 205 of the Planning and Development Act, 2000 (as amended), the development as proposed would necessitate the cutting down, destruction and removal of preserved specified trees and / or would have serious negative impacts on the viability of preserved specified trees, and as such would be contrary both to the provisions of the Draft Tree Preservation Order and the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The development as proposed would require the removal of specified preserved trees subject to a draft Tree Preservation Order and would compromise the viability of specified preserved trees subject to a draft Tree Preservation Order that would remain in situ, and as such, would materially contravene Policy LHA17 of the South Dublin County Development Plan 2010-2016, ‘Trees and Woodlands’. || The development as proposed would seriously compromise the amenity value afforded to the site by the specified preserved trees subject to a draft Tree Preservation Order and as such would materially contravene Policy SN3 of the South Dublin County Development Plan 2010-2016, ‘Existing Site Features’.

decision: REFUSE FURTHER EXT. OF DURATION OF PERM.
reasons_joined: Noting legislative changes since December 31st, 2023, Section 42 (4) of the Act states that a decision to extend the appropriate period of a permission shall be made not more than twice and the combined extensions of duration of permission shall not exceed 5 years in total. The applicant has already been granted a further extension of duration of permission under SD15A/0127/FEP and for a period cumulatively exceeding 5 years and therefore another further extension of the appropriate period cannot be granted.

The site is traversed by 1600mm and 200mm watermains of regional importance. The applicant was afforded a number of opportunities to address the serious concerns of the Planning Authority in this regard and to supply the correct location of the watermains in order to allow for detailed assessment of the impact of the proposal on the watermains and associated wayleaves. This information has not been provided to the satisfaction of the Planning Authority, and in this respect, full and adequate assessment of the impact of the proposed housing, roads, public and private amenity space locations, walls, foundation, foul sewers, surface water sewers and landscaping on the operation and future maintenance of the watermains cannot take place. The applicant has not, therefore, satisfied the serious concerns of the Planning Authority regarding the impact of the proposed development on these watermains and as such, any grant of planning permission must be considered to be potentially prejudicial to public health, and contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the Greater Dublin Area. || The proposed development, which is located on an elevated area of land with existing housing to the south, would not be served by adequate levels of surface water attenuation, with proposed attenuation measures being identified as being undersized by a factor of 2. The proposed development, through inadequate provision of surface water attenuation, would therefore represent a serious flooding risk to proposed and existing houses, and in this regard would materially contravene Section 2.3.21 of the County Development Plan 2010 - 2016 - 'Risk of Flooding', in that it would increase flood risk on the site and elsewhere. The proposed development would therefore materially contravene the principles of to the 'A1' zoning objective of the area which seeks to 'provide for new Residential Communities in accordance with approved Area Plans', and would be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The applicant has not demonstrated that the proposed development would not have significant negative consequences for the operation and maintenance of watermains of regional importance which traverse the site, through encroachment on the wayleaves serving the mains and which must be kept free of permanent structures. In this regard, the proposal would materially contravene the following policies of the South Dublin County Council Development Plan 2010-2016:- (a) Section 2.3.4 'Water Supply and Drainage Strategy' and Policy WD1 'Water Supply and Drainage', which seek to 'continue the sustainable development and improvement of the water supply... throughout the County'. (b) Policy WD10: 'Protection of Piped Infrastructure', which seeks to 'protect the existing and future network of major piped infrastructural services by providing for adequate setback of development'. The proposed development would, therefore, materially contravene objectives of the Development Plan and would be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area.

The proposed development, given its building height and podium level layout, contravenes the urban design criteria as identified in the ‘Sustainable Residential Development in Urban Areas’ Guidelines (Department of Environment, Heritage and Local Government, 2008) in terms of context, inclusivity, distinctiveness, layout, public realm, and detailed design by reason of the following: (a) The layout and orientation of the proposed development with regard to adjacent residential dwellings would lead to unacceptable levels of overshadowing and overbearing appearance, (b) The lack of any commercial or community uses. (c) Lack of permeability within the scheme and between the proposed development and surrounding area, (d) Arrangement of public open space provision and the provision of residual open spaces with no clear role or function, (e) Creation of a poor quality streetscape onto the Ballymount Road Lower which limits the provision of an active commercial street frontage. (f) The location at this suburban interface is incongruent and does not lead to the creation of public realm and legible urban design. The proposed development would contravene the South Dublin County Council Development Plan (2010-2016) regarding the ‘LC' zoning objective of the site, 'To protect, provide for and/or improve Local Centre facilities’, and the requirements for sustainable neighbourhoods as set out in section 1.4. Thus, the proposed development would represent a substandard form of development, seriously injure the amenities of property in the vicinity and be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The proposed development would give rise to a substandard level of residential amenity for future occupants by reason of the configuration, inadequate size and poor quality of the proposed central area of open space, which is in parts poorly overlookd and to a very large degree overshadowed by tall buildings. The proposed development would seriously injure the residential amenities of future occupants and would, therefore, be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || Having regard to the siting and orientation of the proposed apartment Blocks B and C in relation to adjacent residential properties to the west, the proposed residential development would seriously injure the residential amenity of properties in the vicinity by reason of overshadowing, overbearing, overlooking and loss of privacy, and as such would depreciate the value of these properties. The proposed development would therefore be contrary to the 'LC' zoning of the area which seeks to 'To protect, provide for and/or improve Local Centre facilities’, and would be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The proposed density at some 141 units per Ha. is significantly higher than the prevailing density in the vicinity which amounts to approximately 30-40 units per hectare. The Naas Road Development Framework (NRDF) 2010 outlines a plot ratio of 0.5 for this site and the surrounding area. The proposed plot ratio will amount to 2.2 (building floor area 12,227.28sq.m divided by site area 5,600sq.m), which is significantly in excess of the plot ratio envisaged for the area. In addition the Area Brief for Greenhills in the NRDF states: Residential developments with a sufficient mix of supporting functions and of a density no higher than the existing residential use are proposed for this relatively well connected area. Due to the significantly higher density than the receiving environment and the significantly greater plot ratio than that envisaged by the Naas Road Development Framework, the proposal constitutes overdevelopment of the site. The proposed development would, therefore, be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The Planning Authority is not satisfied that the need to demolish 4 habitable houses has been demonstrated or that proper consideration was given to any option to retain these houses in a proposed residential development of the site.

Having regard to the siting and orientation of proposed dwellings 5 - 10 in relation to the part 3, part 4 storey Primary Health Care Centre permitted under An Bord Pleanala Ref. PL06S.239890, and particularly to the 17m - 22.75m separation distance from the north-west elevation of this building as permitted, it is considered that seriously inadequate levels of residential amenity would result. The identified units within the proposed residential development would be overshadowed for significant periods of the year, would be overlooked and would experience loss of privacy, in addition to suffering from very significant levels of overbearing impact. The proposed residential development would therefore materially contravene to the 'A' zoning of the area, as set out in the South Dublin County Development Plan 2010-2016, which seeks to 'protect and/or improve Residential Amenity’, and would be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The proposed development would set an undesirable precedent for other similar developments, which would in themselves and cumulatively, be harmful to the residential amenities of the area and would be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area.

The proposed residential development on a sensitive site, adjoined alongside on three boundaries by High Amenity Zoned land, does not comply with the urban design criteria as identified in the ‘Sustainable Residential Development in Urban Areas’ Guidelines (Department of Environment, Heritage and Local Government, 2008) and Section 4 Sustainable Neighbourhoods of the South Dublin County Council Development Plan 2010-2016 in terms of context, inclusivity, distinctiveness, layout, public realm, and detailed design by reason of the following: (a) The failure to repond to the field patterns and in particular the removal of the centrally located hedgerow/tree clusters, contrary to Policy LHA18 (Hedgerows) which sets out to protect hedgerows in the County from development which would impact adversely upon them and to enhance the County’s hedgerows by increasing coverage, where possible, using locally native species (Section 4.3.7.xvi). (b) The lack of a high quality and direct connection between the Dodder Valley Park and Firhouse Road, (c) The arrangement of dwellings (particularly the eastern block) would result in predominantly high and blank boundary walls of proposed dwelling units onto open space to the side, resulting in a lack of passive surveillance and a visually unattractive environment (d) The fragmented layout of the 'northern cluster' and creation of 'stand- alone' or pavilion-type apartment blocks that are poorly secured and do not offer an adequate degree of privacy and security for residents, (e) The lack of Sustainable Urban Drainage Systems and integration of Green Infrastructure methods throughout the entire design and layout, (f) The lack of viable planting along the internal streets and to the front of dwellings, (g) The inharmonious architectural language, (h) The provision of a pedestrian route that would not be adequately overlooked, (i) the creation of a poor quality streetscape onto the road which separates the pavilion-type apartment blocks on one side and the corner apartments on the other which would comprise of wall and railings and a swathe of car parking spaces, which will create a visual and physical barrier along the street that would preclude the provision of an active street frontage on both sides of the street. The proposed development would, therefore represent a substandard form of development and would seriously injure the amenities of property in the vicinity. The proposed development is of poor quality and would contravene the ‘A' zoning objective of the site, ‘to protect and/or improve residential amenity’, as set out in South Dublin County Council Development Plan (2010-2016) and would, therefore, be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || Having regard to the layout of the proposed residential development, which would: (a) necessitate the removal of a significant row of trees for vehicular access, a field boundary and ditch system in the centre of the site, a section of a historic townland boundary to the north west of the site (due to road and parking incursion) in the immediate vicinity of High Amenity Zoned lands, (b) have a negative impact on biodiversity, in particular on protected species including bats and badgers through the loss of habitat (trees and hedgerows) and the disturbance arising from additional lighting in a currently dark corridor along the River Dodder, (c) isolate a piece of this High Amenity Zoned land (proposed to be ceded to the Local Authority) behind a 1.8 metre high wall and railing, the proposed development would be visually obtrusive, would seriously injure the amenities of property in the vicinity and would be out of character with and negatively impact upon the adjoining High Amenity Zoned lands. Thus, the proposed development would contravene the ‘G’ zoning objective ‘to protect and improve High Amenity Areas’ in the South Dublin County Development Plan 2010 – 2016 and would, therefore, be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The proposed development would give rise to a substandard level of residential amenity for future occupants by reason of : • six single aspect north facing apartments, • the shape and location of the proposed linear strip of open space along the south east site boundary, which primarily acts as a pedestrian walkway, with a significant section of this open space not being passively surveilled. • the most eastern section of the site which is heavily shaded by coniferous trees and fails to integrate with the existing open nature of the immediately adjacent lands which are zoned High Amenity. Thus, the proposed development would seriously injure the residential amenities of future occupants and would, therefore, be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The proposed residential development does not comply with the basic standards as identified in the Design Manual for Urban Roads and Streets Guidelines (Department of Environment, Community and Local Government, 2013) in terms of layout, car parking, distinctiveness, public realm, and detailed design by reason of the following: (a) the use of standard ‘black top’ surface materials in a highly sensitive location within the immediate vicinity of the Dodder High Amenity zoned lands (b) the carriageway widths and corner radii which exceed the minimum standards (c) the lack of self-regulating low speed environment (d) the predominance of in-curtilage car parking and the lack of provision for visitor car parking Thus, the proposed residential development represents a substandard form of development and would seriously injure the amenities of property in the vicinity. The proposed development is of poor quality and would materially contravene the South Dublin County Council Development Plan (2010-2016) 'A' zoning which sets out ‘to protect and/or improve residential amenity’; and would, therefore, be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || This application proposes to construct a new junction to this development adjacent to the Morton’s pub entrance and the Ballycullen Avenue signals. The proposed junction is a priority junction with no right turning facility. It is also situated very close to the Morton’s pub entrance and the Ballycullen Avenue signals, which will increase the confusing road layout at this location. While the Firhouse Rd is nominally a 50kph speed limit, due to its width, the traffic speeds are potentially higher than this. A right turning lane would need to be provided in order to protect right turning traffic. This would require the removal of large section of the existing bus lane, which is a key piece of public transport infrastructure in the area. Therefore, the proposed entrance is unacceptable and would endanger public safety by reason of traffic hazard or obstruction of road users or otherwise.

The proposed development adjoins a number of dwellings which are Protected Structures under the South Dublin County Development Plan 2010-2016 (Schedule 2 ref. 306) and also adjoins the residential area of Pearse Brothers Park to the west. decision: REFUSE EXT. OF DURATION OF PERMISSION
reasons_joined: The application was made after changes in the Planning and Development Act which have removed the statutory basis for an extension of duration of permission where works have not commenced, and substantial works have not taken place. In precise terms, the criteria set down in s42(1)(a)(i) or s42(1B)(b)(v) are not met in this instance, and the Planning Authority therefore cannot grant permission for an extension of duration of permission.

The wayleave on the site, for the arterial watermains from Ballymore Eustace to Saggart Reservoir, which are operated by Dublin City Council on behalf of Irish Water, has not been satisfactorily addressed. Inadequate care has been taken in ascertaining the position of pipes, with an insufficient wayleave applied, based on mapping which has not been demonstrated to be accurate. The proposal to develop children's play equipment on the wayleave is also unacceptable. The required offset will not be relaxed for this critical infrastructure, which supplies a large population with fresh water, due to potential damage to structures in the event of a burst, and the area required for subsequent repair works. As such, the proposed development would be prejudical to public health. || There is no capacity for the existing 150mm foul sewer on Kilteel Road to accept a foul drain connection from the proposed development. Furthermore, there is no capacity in Tay Lane Pumping Station to accept sewerage from the proposed development. The applicant has not adequately addressed these issues. As such, the proposed development would risk pollution from wastewater overflow and would therefore be prejudicial to public health. The proposed development is also premature, pending upgrades to the Tay Lane pumping station and the 150mm foul sewer on Kilteel Road. || The applicant has not satisfactorily demonstrated that sufficient surface water attenuation is provided for the proposed development. The proposed development must therefore be considered prejudicial to public health and the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The Traffic Impact Assessment submitted is inadequate in that it does not take into account the cumulative impact of traffic from the proposed development with that of developments already granted on the Kiilteel Road. The application is therefore deficient in this regard.

Insufficient details have been lodged with the Planning Authority in relation to the surface water attenuation system, foul drain layout, watermain layout and invert levels which are required to ensure compliance with the objectives and policies of the South Dublin County Development Plan 2016 - 2022, such as Policy 1 Water and Wastewater, Policy 2 Surface Water and Groundwater, Policy 3 Flood Risk, Policy 5 Sustainable Urban Systems, Section 11.6.1 (ii) Surface Water, Section 11.6.1 (iii) Sustainable Urban Drainage Systems. The proposed development is non-compliant with Irish Water Standards and Building Regulations 2010 and Greater Dublin Regional Code of Practice for Drainage Works and the proposed development would be prejudicial to public health. || The proposed development includes proposed attenuation systems which are undersized by 16% for 30 year storm and by 50% for 100 year storm. T || The proposed development does not include provision for crèche facility in accordance with the 'Childcare Facilities, Guidelines for Planning Authorities'. The Planning Authority is not satisfied with the design orientation of 6 single aspect (one bed apartments) which are proposed in apartment Blocks F1 and F2. Each of these six apartments are north facing only which is not considered to be in the interest of residential amenity of future occupants and therefore is not in the interest of proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The Planning Authority has serious concerns with regard to the poor urban design demonstrated throughout the proposed development including the following: • The positioning of the 3 apartment blocks, specifically F1 and F2 in the centre of the site, and G1 in the south west corner, on island type layouts, together with the provision of minimum and poor quality open space is not acceptable for future residents of the scheme. The applicant has also failed to provide perimeter blocks with semi private open space for future residents. • The pedestrian access to the east of Block F1 leading to the refuse storage area and bicycle sheds are considered poor in design and layout, as the walkway leading to the bin storage area and bicycle area may become a point for anti-social activities. • The positioning of Block G within 6 metres of the site boundary with existing residential properties is considered to be over-bearing and would adversely impact upon the residential amenity of the existing homes along this boundary. • The design has not appropriately accommodated pedestrian accessibility. The circuitous route of the footpaths throughout the site, which includes sharp corner bends, manoeuvring around car parking spaces and grass verges is not considered acceptable in terms of walkability and accessibility through the site and encourages restricted pedestrian flow. The variation of footpath widths throughout the site is also of concern, particularly 1 metre wide proposed footpaths along Road 4, which is considered extremely restrictive to users, in particular persons with prams or wheelchair users. • The proposed design omits pedestrian connectivity between the proposed pedestrian footpath to the southwest of the site (adjacent to apartment Block G1) and internal development scheme footpaths, thereby inhibiting connectivity. • The proposed location and layout of the shop and crèche on an island surrounding by internal road network demonstrates poor urban design. • The proposed open space is not designed as an inclusive landscape suitable for recreational for all future residents, little passive or active opportunities have been provided. • The design of the pedestrian link between the subject site and Springvale is poor, considering that the ramp must be usable by pedestrians, wheelchair users and cyclists. The gradient at the turning point of the ramp seems very steep for users. • On Road 5, areas of grass are proposed between the boundary of the houses and the public footpaths. No design rationale has been provided. The provision of the grassed areas is to the detriment of the footpath width whilst also reducing the potential allocated space of each of the residential units. Maintenance of these grass verges may also prove challenging. This space may be better served provided to each of the respective dwelling. • No rationale is provided as to why a shared surface is proposed for house units A1/38 and A1/39. • Proposed areas allocated for private driveways of some units are considered deficient in some instances, with apparent difficulty for 2 cars to adequately park, for example in units A1/38 to A1/45, A2/4, A2/5. More detailed site layout plans have not been provided and these would be required to comprehensively assess if sufficient provision has been made. • On-street landscape planting within the development scheme is considered sparse and would result in a hard landscape character for the development which is undesirable. • The proposal to locate 2 refuse storage areas adjoining the rear gardens of housing units, specifically house type A2/16 and house type D2/1 would adversely impact upon the enjoyment of the private amenity space of future residents of unit nos. A2/16 and D2/1 by way of odour, noise, and potentially rodents. • Deficit of information in relation to the elevation and finishes of the external bin storage areas associated with the proposed apartment blocks. • Details of the proposed pedestrian access points leading to Stocking Lane have not been provided. • Some of the drawings have inconsistencies and are poorly presented, inhibiting the comprehensive assessment of the overall design, for example the width of car parking spaces differs in some instances and are not completely rectangular in shape. (b) Failure to meet minimum apartment space requirements The proposed development does not comply with the National and Regional guidelines - ‘Sustainable Urban Housing: Design Standards for New Apartments – Guidelines for Planning Authorities 2018’ and Section 11 of the South Dublin County Development Plan 2016-2022 in respect of the provision and specification for internal space requirements for minimum storage and minimum bedroom floor area in some of the apartment units. Therefore, the development would materially contravene Council Policy for dwelling standards and would seriously injure the amenities of future occupants of the proposed dwelling, be contrary to the proper planning and development of the area, and would contravene the zoning objective 'to protect and /or improve residential amenity'. || The applicant has submitted a basic landscape plan prepared by Matt Barnes Architects drawing no. 2183-13. The proposed plan is unsatisfactory as it has not provided sufficient details such as appropriate cross sections, planting plans, levels, boundaries, SuDS, maintenance plans, street trees, etc. Key concerns include: • Insufficient quantities of street trees have been proposed, at various locations there are upwards of 30m to the nearest tree. There are numerous locations in the development site that can facilitate street tree planting. • No street trees have been proposed in the West of the development site near the shared surface and shops. This creates a very hard, urban landscape and is unwelcomed by SDCC. • Street trees have been proposed within private open space this is not acceptable, SDCC require street trees to be planted in public open space, with a constructed tree pit and structural root soil to enable tree longevity for future residents. • London Plane (Platanus Acerfolia) have been proposed as street trees, this specie has a tendency to uplift pathways and grow excessively large. This is an unsatisfactory location for London Plane. • The landscape plan doesn’t detail where lighting columns will be located, all lighting columns should be located a minimum of 5m away from any tree. • CMK Hort + Arb has submitted a tree survey and tree protection plan, it has been outlined in the Arboriculture Impact drawing no. TSTO001 that 60 trees out of 101 trees or 59.40% are being removed this is deemed unsatisfactory. The proposed development is not considered to be in accordance with the South Dublin County Development Plan 2016-2022 and below are a number of extracts from policies and sections which confirms same: G2 Objective 2: To protect and enhance the biodiversity value and ecological function of the Green Infrastructure network. It is considered that the site of the proposal is situated in an area under strong urban influence and therefore, pursuant to the National Policies contained within ‘Project Ireland 2040: National Planning Framework’, the Core Strategy and Rural Settlement Strategy outlined in the South Dublin County Council Development Plan, the proposed development would by itself and cumulatively, constitute the proliferation of development in an area under strong urban influence and hinder the achievement of the policies and objective of the National Planning Framework to consolidate existing urban settlements and contribute to compact growth within the Dublin Region. The proposed development is located in an area zoned 'RES' in the South Dublin County Development Plan 2016 - 2022, with an objective 'to protect and /or improve residential amenity. Having regard to: (a) section 11.3.2 (i) 'infill development'; (b) the pattern of development in the area; (c) the overbearing visual impact of the proposed development in the streetscape of Nutgrove Avenue and on dwellings to the south of the site, and the consequent loss of amenity for dwellings to the south, in particular Nos. 17 and 18 Stonepark Orchard; (d) the blank and imposing brick wall boundary treatment proposed to the western section of the northern boundary, and the detrimental impact on the streetscape at Nutgrove Avenue; (e) the use of a single, standalone, bin store located in the northwest corner of the site and directly addressing Nutgrove Avenue, and the detrimental visual impact and potentially detrimental impact on air quality it would have; (f) the likelihood of direct overlooking of neighbouring private gardens and the risk of overshadowing of those gardens, and the consequent loss of residential amenity; the proposed development would contravene the 'RES' land-use zoning objective and policy on infill development contained in the South Dublin County Development Plan 2016 - 2022, and would undermine the residential character of the area, and seriously injure the amenities of property in the vicinity, and would therefore be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The Landscape proposals are not acceptable to the Planning Authority, due to the following deficiencies: (i) The communal amenity space is provided in a series of areas; those areas to the north, west and south of Block A are narrow strips with questionable amenity value, and are peripheral to the overall scheme. The communal amenity space to the west of Block A suffers from lack of passive surveillance - no habitable rooms have windows facing onto this space. (ii) The number of trees proposed to be planted or retained is insufficient and the applicant should have sought to retain more of the existing trees. The proposed development would contravene Policy G2, Objective 9, of the County Development Plan (the objective of which is: To preserve, protect and augment trees, groups of trees, woodlands and hedgerows within the County by increasing tree canopy coverage using locally native species and by incorporating them within design proposals and supporting their integration into the Green Infrastructure network) (iii) No public open space proposed to be provided, as required under section 11.3.1 (iii) of the South Dublin County Development Plan 2016 - 2022. || The Council's building height strategy is contained in Section 11.2.7 of the South Dublin County Development Plan 2016 - 2022. With regard to this strategy, the proposed 4-storey development is considered to be unacceptable as the applicant has failed to demonstrate due regard to the prevailing building height in the surrounding area, the proximity of existing housing, or the formation of a cohesive streetscape pattern, and the proposed development does not integrate well with the surrounding area because of this. Furthermore, no transition of height is provided at this site, which is surrounded by 2-storey suburban development. The proposed development would therefore be in contravention of Policy H9 Objective 3 of the County Development Plan (which seeks: To ensure that new residential developments immediately adjoining existing one and two storey housing incorporate a gradual change in building heights with no significant marked increase in building height in close proximity to existing housing), and would not accord with the recommendations contained in sections 11.2.7 and 11.3.2 (i) Infill Development. The proposed development would therefore be a material contravention of the County Development Plan and would not accord with the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The proposed development features ground floor terraces and above ground level balconies in Blocks A and B which are located in a proposed 7-metre wayleave around a 1,050mm surface water pipe. The terraces and balconies would be closer than 3.5 metres from the centre-point of the pipe and would therefore not comply with the requirements of Irish Water or the Environmental Services section of South Dublin County Council. The proposed development would therefore be prejudicial to public health and would not be in the interests of the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The proposed pedestrian and cycle throughway to the east of the site would not provide adeqaute comfort or safety for pedestrians or cyclists as it is directed through a car park, and would be used by cars for turnaround manoeuvres, or manoeuvres in reverse gear, necessary to access and egress from parking spaces. This arrangement would contravene Policy TM7 of the County Development Plan (the objective of which is To ensure that car parking does not detract from the comfort and safety of pedestrians and cyclists or the attractiveness of the landscape) on the protection of pedestrians and cyclists.

The site is zoned objective RES- ‘To protect and/or improve residential amenity / zoning objective’ and subject to Specific Local Objective (SLO) H3 SLO1 under the South Dublin County Council Development Plan 2016 – 2022. Housing Policy H3 SLO 1 states: ‘To facilitate the development of lands at Edmondstown (former Kilmashogue House) for the purpose of low density residential development at a net density of not more than 12 dwellings per hectare, and to promote housing for older people (nursing home, independent and semi- independent) as a fully integrated part of such development with an increased density of not more than 20 dwellings per hectare to apply to independent and semi-independent housing for older people. All residential development, including housing for older people, shall be integrated within a sustainable residential neighbourhood that is served by shared public open space, community and local facilities. Permissible densities may be increased in accordance with the relevant ministerial guidelines where issues of accessibility have been fully resolved in an appropriate manner. Any future development should have regard to the boundaries with and the protection of the existing amenity and function of Edmondstown Golf Course.’ Having regard to H3 SLO1 that applies to the subject lands and those to the south and west of the application site, the proposed scheme does not adequately address the Specific Local Objective attached to the site. The proposed development is significantly at variance with H3 SLO1 as it: (a) proposes a density of 38.8 units per hectare, which would be significantly in excess of the ‘low density residential development at a net density of not more than 12 units per hectare’ or the 'not more than 20 dwellings per hectare to apply to independent and semi-independent housing for older people' (b) has not adequately promoted housing for older people (nursing home, independent and semi-independent) as a fully integrated part of such development (c) lacks integration within a sustainable residential neighbourhood that is served by shared public open space, community and local facilities, which is of particular importance to the sustainable provision of housing for older people. The proposed development would, therefore, materially contravene the policies and objectives of the South Dublin County Council Development Plan 2016-2022, specifically Policy H3 SLO1, and be contrary the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || The layout and design of the proposed development would be contrary to best practice urban design principles set out in the Urban Design Manual: A Best Practice Guide (2009) and the South Dublin County Development Plan 2016 - 2022. Site specific characteristics and site constraints have not been adequately addressed as part of the design solution, and result in a largely 'urban' development which fails to respond to its location at the rural fringe. Having regard to layout and design shortfalls, the proposed development would represent overdevelopment of the subject site which would not support the creation of a sustainable community. This is demosntrated by the following deficiencies: • The proposed ‘village green’ public open space is substandard in terms of size and is disconnected from the houses to the west of the site (House types C4 to C9). • Lack of any surveillance of the play area proposed within the woodland east of the site. • The design fails to take sufficient account of the existing Green Infrastructure onsite including extensive trees, hedgerows and woodland, a high proportion of which is proposed to be removed. • The design has failed to adequately incorporate sufficient SUDS features in accordance with the South Dublin County Development Plan 2016-2022 Policy IE2 Objective 5. • Failure to incorporate a minimum distance of 22m between opposing windows between House types C4 to C9 to the west of the site; • Seven out of the sixteen apartment units would be predominantly north facing with substandard dual aspect windows proposed at east elevation in Block A and at west elevation in Block B; • Failure to clearly outline what is private, semi-private and public open space in the vicinity of the apartment blocks; • The private amenity space / terrace belonging to apartment Unit A2 would directly abut the public footpath, with no privacy strip incorporated into the design layout. • Unit B1 would have no private amenity space provision which would not accord with the Sustainable Urban Housing: Design Standards for New Apartments (2018) • Substandard size provision for a community room (at 26sq.m.) for a development of this scale and such location would compromise residential amenity of future occupants; • House type C6-3B would have a constrained driveway resulting in parking for only 1 no. car. There is no provision for on-street parking owing to the layout of the homezone street layout. • The location of the community room directly adjacent to apartment Unit B1 is unsuitable owing to potential noise impact during periods of use, adversely impacting upon the residential amenity of any future occupant of Unit B1. • The external amenity space associated with the community room would traverse directly across the south façade of apartment Unit B1, therefore, adversely impacting on the residential amenity of future occupants of B1, by way of noise and loss of privacy. Having regard to the above, the proposed development would seriously injure the amenities of property in the vicinity and within the site and would be contrary to the ‘RES' zoning objective of the site, ‘to protect and/or improve residential amenity, as set out in South Dublin County Council Development Plan 2016-2022 and would therefore, be contrary to the proper planning and sustainable development of the area. || (a) The layout of the proposed residential development would necessitate the removal of a significant proportion of hedgerow, trees and area of woodland onsite. The design fails to take sufficient account of the existing Green Infrastructure onsite including extensive trees, hedgerows and woodland, a high proportion of which is proposed to be removed. The proposed development falls seriously short of recommended residential standards contained in the 'Quality Housing for Sustainable Communities - Best Practice Guidelines' (2009) or ‘Sustainable Urban Housing: Design Standards for New Apartments – Guidelines for Planning Authorities’ (2018) and the South Dublin County Development Plan 2016 - 2022 in relation to: - unit size - room size - private amenity space - communal or semi-private amenity space - storage both internal and for bulky items - car and bicycle parking The proposed development is substandard and would not meet the minimum requirements for residential development contained in the County Development Plan, and would provide an unacceptable residential amenity for future occupants. The LAP includes 5 criteria for the sequencing of development in 'REGEN' zoned lands: 1. Clear transition towards more urban form. 2. Connectivity and Linkages 3. Careful design of residential development at ground level in relation to commercial traffic. 4. Noise pollution, air pollution, or other nuisance. 5. Prevent piecemental premature development. The proposed development would constitute piecemeal residential development, not only adjacent to but ancillary to, and sharing a site with, an active commercial/industrial site, and surrounded on all sides by other active commercia/industrial sites. The proposed development would constitute piecemeal residential development of a scale and urban form contrary to the ambition, policies and objectives of the LAP.
